jobs.title: Principal Data Scientist - Geotechnical & Water | Brisbane, Perth or Adelaide
jobs.description:
About BHP 

At BHP we support our people to grow, learn, develop their skills and reach their potential. With a global portfolio of operations, we offer a diverse and inclusive environment with extraordinary career opportunities. Our strategy is to focus on creating a safe work environment where our employees feel strongly connected to our values and objectives, and where the capability of our people is key to our success.

Come and be a part of this success.

About the Role

Data Scientist – Geotechnical & Water

The
Data Scientist – Geotechnical & Water
is responsible for enabling data-driven decision-making across BHP’s global geotechnical and water portfolio. This role acts as the critical link between domain experts and data science capabilities, partnering with asset teams, projects, and Regional Centre of Excellence (RCoE) teams to identify opportunities, develop advanced analytical solutions, and embed actionable insights into operational processes.

The position combines expertise in
data science, analytics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and data engineering
with a strong understanding of
geotechnical, hydrogeological, and water management systems
. The role is focused on transforming complex data into practical solutions that enhance risk management, monitoring, forecasting, planning, and technical performance across the business.

By leveraging advanced analytics and digital technologies, the role drives innovation, improves decision quality, supports proactive risk management, and delivers measurable business value through safer, more sustainable, and more productive operations.

About You

Required

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, Geoscience, or a related discipline.

Extensive experience in data science, machine learning, analytics, and statistical modelling. 

Strong proficiency in Python, SQL, and data visualization tools.

Proven experience translating business challenges into data-driven solutions and influencing stakeholders.

Preferred

Master's degree or PhD in a relevant field.

Experience in mining, geotechnical, hydrogeological, water management, or related industries.

Knowledge of cloud platforms, data engineering, and enterprise analytics environments.

Experience mentoring teams and leading analytics initiatives at scale.

About Our Process 

At BHP, we are committed to employing individuals who align with the BHP Charter Values and meet the requirements of the role. As part of the recruitment process, there are a number of checks which may be conducted to demonstrate applicants suitability for a role including police / criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks, and/or reference checks. 

If you are already employed directly by BHP, please log in using your BHP email address or apply via our internal jobs portal. 

Supporting a Diverse Workforce  

The size, stability and magnitude of our business not only provides significant opportunity for professional development, but also attractive salary packages with performance-based bonuses and a best-in-class employee share program. We know there are many aspects of our employees' lives that are important, and work is only one of these, so we offer benefits to enable your work to fit with your life. These benefits include flexible working options, a generous paid parental leave policy, other extended leave entitlements and parent rooms.  

At BHP, we know that we are strengthened by diversity. We are an Equal Opportunity employer that is committed to making BHP a safe and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive and be at their best every day. We are focused on creating a workforce that’s more diverse and represents the communities where we work and live. providing a work environment in which everyone is included, treated fairly and with respect. We are an Equal Opportunity employer and recognise that true diversity includes gender, age, race, disability status, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, education levels, and many more aspects of your identity.

BHP is committed to providing a recruitment process that is fair, equitable and accessible for all. If you have a disability, we know that it may be helpful for us to adjust our process to make it equitable for your individual situation. If you would like to reach out to someone about your situation and our recruitment process, please email us at

inclusion@bhp.com

.

Apply now »

jobs.title: Water Systems Coordinator | Prominent Hill | 6 months Fixed term contract
jobs.description:
About Copper SA Operations at BHP

BHP is a global resources company operating across more than 90 locations worldwide, with a purpose to improve lives and support a more sustainable future.

Through Copper South Australia (Copper SA), we are building a leading copper portfolio that supports the global energy transition, supplying materials essential for renewable energy, electric vehicles and digital infrastructure.

For you, this is an exciting opportunity to grow your career, make a meaningful impact, and help shape the future of one of Australia's leading copper businesses.

About Prominent Hill

Prominent Hill is a well-established copper-gold operation within BHP’s Minerals Australia portfolio, with a strong future and ongoing investment.

Located 650km north-west of Adelaide, the site operates across underground and surface mining on a
4/3 days only FIFO roster
.

A major shaft project is supporting underground expansion and extending mine life to at least 2040, creating long-term opportunities across the operation.

It’s a technically complex site where you can build your skills, take on new challenges, and be part of a team where safety and looking out for each other matters.

We currently have a vacancy for a 
Water Systems Coordinator
, reporting to the
Infrastructure & Services team
.

The Challenge Ahead

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in improving the integrity, reliability and compliance of the potable water supply network at Prominent Hill.

As
Water Systems Coordinator,
you will lead the implementation and close-out of a broad range of improvement initiatives arising from potable water infrastructure reviews and Drinking Water Risk Management activities. This is a hands-on role where you'll spend time in the field inspecting assets, verifying infrastructure, coordinating corrective works, updating asset information and working closely with site stakeholders.

You'll have the opportunity to influence meaningful improvements across water quality, infrastructure compliance, risk management and asset reliability while helping ensure safe and sustainable operations across site. The role offers variety, collaboration and the chance to make a visible impact through the delivery of important water management initiatives.

What You'll Bring to the Role

We're looking for a practical, solutions-focused professional who enjoys working across multiple teams and has a strong commitment to safety, compliance and continuous improvement.

Your background may include experience in potable water systems, water treatment, utilities, infrastructure, fixed plant maintenance, plumbing or related industrial environments.

You will bring:

Strong practical knowledge of piping systems, pumps, tanks, valves and associated infrastructure.

Experience working with potable water systems, process water systems, utilities infrastructure or fixed plant assets.

The ability to interpret drawings, verify field conditions and identify opportunities for improvement.

Experience coordinating contractors and engaging a range of stakeholders.

Well-developed planning, organisation and execution skills.

Strong communication and stakeholder engagement capability.

High attention to detail and confidence maintaining documentation and asset information.

The ability to balance field-based activities with administrative coordination and reporting.

A proactive approach to identifying risks, solving problems and delivering improvement initiatives.

A demonstrated commitment to safety, compliance and risk management.

Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

Conduct field inspections of potable water infrastructure across site.

Verify tank installations, pipework, pumps, valve alignments, sampling points and backflow prevention devices.

Coordinate identification, documentation and rectification of infrastructure defects and non-conformances.

Lead potable water plumbing conformity assessments and infrastructure reviews.

Verify potable and non-potable water service arrangements.

Coordinate potable water tank audits and associated rectification programs.

Validate P&IDs and infrastructure drawings against field conditions.

Maintain asset registers and support updates to asset management information.

Coordinate installation and improvement of water quality monitoring and sampling points.

Support chlorine monitoring, water quality investigations and tank maintenance activities.

Coordinate work between internal maintenance teams and external contractors.

Partner with Processing, Operations, Camp Operations, Hygiene, Infrastructure and Underground teams.

Implement recommendations arising from the Drinking Water Risk Management Plan.

Develop and maintain action registers, monitor progress and report outcomes.

Support the development of maintenance, inspection and compliance programs.

Ensure all work is completed safely and in accordance with operational requirements.

Work Location

This opportunity is based at
Prominent Hill
, located approximately 650km north-west of Adelaide in South Australia.

The role is offered as a
6 months fixed-term opportunity
and operates on a
4 days on / 3 days off roster
. It is well suited to individuals who enjoy a balance of field-based and coordination work while contributing to critical infrastructure and water management outcomes.

Why You'll Love Working Here

At BHP, you’ll do meaningful work in an environment that supports you to perform at your best; on site and at home. That’s why our benefits are designed to support your health, your growth, and your personal balance:

Grow your career your way, with opportunities to develop and move across BHP.

Be rewarded with competitive pay, performance bonuses and our BHP employee share plan.

Work in an inclusive team where people support each other every day.

Enjoy flexibility and family-friendly options that help you balance work and life.

Access wellbeing support, including 24/7 confident

jobs.title: Senior Engineer Medium-Term Mine Planning - Adelaide
jobs.description:
About Copper SA Operations at BHP

BHP is a global resources company operating across more than 90 locations worldwide. Through Copper South Australia (Copper SA), we are building a leading copper portfolio that supports the global energy transition, supplying materials essential for renewable energy, electric vehicles and digital infrastructure.  

For you, this is an exciting opportunity to grow your career, make a meaningful impact, and help shape the future of one of Australia's leading copper businesses. 

About the Role

Reporting to the Superintendent Planning and Infrastructure, this role is responsible for executing strategic and technical mine planning work in the 2-8 year planning horizon for our Copper SA Underground Mines. The role provides guidance to a range of technical and operational stakeholders with a focus on medium-term mine planning and infrastructure required to support the asset strategy. Mine infrastructure includes ventilation, air, power, water, pastefill and their impacts on safety, production, cost and achievement of the mine plan and future growth at Copper SA. Your extensive industry experience will enable you to develop and maintain effective working relationships with a wide stakeholder group with the ability to communicate at all levels of the organisation.

This position is based at Adelaide on a 5:2 roster with occasional site travel to each of the operating mine sites, flexible work arrangements available.

In this role you will:

Model mine plans and requisite infrastructure demand over the 5 year mine plan to understand capital infrastructure project requirements

Justify capital spend using the projects framework whilst optimising for capital efficiencies

Education and coaching of personnel across technical and project teams to improve understanding of mine services systems

Support the integration and optimisation of Copper SA

Consultation in 5YP/LoA planning processes with attention to safety, schedule, reliability and costs

Focus on understanding and supporting mine long-term planning and continuous improvement initiatives

Leverage your expertise and industry connections to bring new technologies and ways of working to the business to improve safety and productivity

Provide technical support for significant mine planning projects, studies, and reviews across the sites.

Develop scopes of work to engage additional external stakeholders as required to support business needs

Project management of packages of work as required to support studies

Liaising between stakeholders to support a comprehensive integrated mine plan

Integration of associated planning and schedule software to support operations

Demonstrate an overriding commitment to health, safety, environmental responsibility and sustainable development.

About You

Mining Engineering degree or similar

Experience in underground mine planning and operations across various mining methods and projects

Experience in mine or project scheduling is highly desirable

Experience in mine design software platforms (VentSim, Deswik, MS Office)

Ability to interpret limited measured / monitoring data, identify potential issues and causes of change, and develop processes to validate assumptions

Able to develop preferred and alternate mine infrastructure strategies, identify and escalate potential risks and mitigating actions

Excellent communication skills including the ability to influence others, communicate complex concepts, and document clearly and concisely

Ability to work collaboratively across different work groups and proactively engage with a range of stakeholders including senior levels of management

Experience in Lean Six Sigma and Theory of Constraints will be advantageous

Previous experience delivering studies through to operations readiness and execution advantageous

Demonstrated ability to solve complex problems with minimal direction

Strong ability to develop own work plan and adapt to change

Why You’ll Love Working Here

At BHP, you’ll do meaningful work in an environment that supports you to perform at your best; on site and at home. That’s why our benefits are designed to support your health, your growth, and your personal balance: 

Grow your career your way, with opportunities to develop and move across BHP

Be rewarded with competitive pay, performance bonuses and our BHP employee share plan

Work in an inclusive team where people support each other every day

Enjoy flexibility and family-friendly options that help you balance work and life

Access wellbeing support, including 24/7 confidential assistance for you and your family

Build your future with benefits like paid parental leave, recognition programs, etc. 

How to Apply

Please apply before 27 September 2026

About Our Process

At BHP, we are committed to employing individuals who align with the BHP Charter Values and meet the requirements of the role. As part of the recruitment process, there are several checks which may be conducted to demonstrate applicants’ suitability for a role including police / criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks, and/or reference checks.  

We Support a Diverse Workforce

At BHP, we believe diversity makes us stronger. We’re committed to creating a safe, inclusive workplace where everyone is treated fairly and can thrive. Our workforce reflects the communities where we operate, and we value all aspects of identity; gender, age, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, education, and more.  

We ensure that our recruitment process is fair, accessible, and equitable. If you have a disability and need adjustments, please contact us at inclusion@bhp.com.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location:
Perth - Fortescue’s Perth office is located on the traditional lands of the Whadjuk Noongar people

Roster:
Monday to Friday

We are seeking a highly organised, proactive and team-oriented Executive Assistant to provide timely, efficient and effective high-level support to the Director Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Technology. This role will be responsible for anticipating priorities, coordinating complex diaries and travel, preparing high-quality meeting and reporting materials, and ensuring leaders are supported to focus on strategic and operational priorities.

The successful candidate will build trusted relationships across the business and manage sensitive information with discretion. The role requires sound judgement, strong attention to detail and the ability to work calmly and confidently in a fast-paced environment, balancing competing priorities while maintaining a high standard of service.

Key Responsibilities

Provide comprehensive executive support, diary and email management

Coordinate complex domestic and international travel, meetings, workshops, site visits, events and stakeholder engagements, ensuring logistics, venues and attendees are well managed.

Use AI and digital tools to improve executive preparation, information management and administrative workflows increasing efficiency and responsiveness

Support financial and administrative processes, including purchase requisitions, invoice reconciliation, receipting and end-of-month activities.

Act as a professional first point of contact for internal and external stakeholders, building effective relationships across all levels of the organisation.

Qualifications and Experience

At least five years' experience in an Executive Assistant, Personal Assistant or senior administration role, with a demonstrated ability to provide proactive, positive and confidential support to senior leaders in a complex corporate environment.

Strong capability in complex diary management, meeting preparation, travel coordination and executive administration.

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office 365, together with excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to prepare clear, accurate and professional correspondence and documents.

Highly organised, self-motivated and resilient, with the ability to manage competing priorities and demanding stakeholder needs.

Experience in the resources or mining industry would be advantageous.

About Us

Be part of something big. Fortescue is leading the world with our plan to decarbonise our iron ore operations, projects that harness renewable energy and the development of technology that will change our planet forever.

Our Commitment

Fortescue celebrates individual strengths and team members are encouraged to bring their whole selves to work. Our global workforce drives and promotes an inclusive culture, both within our organisation and throughout the communities we interact with. Diverse backgrounds include First Nations Peoples, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+ community, gender, neurodiverse, cultural diversity, all age groups, and those with an intersectional or multiple diverse characteristics. 
We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Inventory and Warehouse Superintendent (Tasiast, 12, MR)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1993, Kinross is a Canadian-based senior gold mining company with operations and projects in the United States, Brazil, Mauritania, Chile and Canada. Our focus on delivering value is based on our four core values of Putting People First, Outstanding Corporate Citizenship, High Performance Culture, and Rigorous Financial Discipline.
 
Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC). 

Tasiast Mine

The Tasiast mine is an open-pit operation in northwestern Mauritania located within an extensive gold system that is largely underexplored. The mine is proceeding with an expansion that is expected to increase production and lower operating costs. Tasiast is a cornerstone asset in Kinross’ portfolio, with a long mine life a large mineral reserve base.

As one of the largest private employers in Mauritania, Tasiast invests heavily in training and career development opportunities and has many important programs in place to support its host communities. For example, since 2014, Tasiast’s mobile clinic, which provides free medical support to isolated communities, has provided over 32,000 consultations. 

Reporting to the Supply Chain Manager, the Inventory & Warehouse Superintendent is accountable for inventory planning, control and warehouse service delivery across TMLSA.

Purpose of Role

To lead the safe, efficient and data-driven management of TMLSA's large, complex and high-value inventory and warehouse operations, ensuring critical materials are available when required while optimizing inventory accuracy, service levels, working capital and storage capacity.

The role requires a highly experienced inventory and warehouse professional with practical expertise in inventory planning, replenishment, optimization and control across critical spares, consumables, bulk commodities, repairables and other operational materials. The Superintendent will translate operational demand into disciplined stocking strategies and robust inventory parameters.

This is a strongly systems- and analytics-oriented leadership role. The Inventory & Warehouse Superintendent will use JDE/ERP data, advanced Excel and business-intelligence tools to interrogate large datasets, improve planning decisions, strengthen master-data quality and drive measurable improvements in material availability, inventory value and working capital, while leading safe and reliable warehouse service delivery.

Job Responsibilities

Own the inventory management strategy and performance for a large, complex and high-value inventory portfolio, with clear governance, standards and accountability for service, accuracy and working capital

Set and continuously optimize replenishment parameters using demand history, criticality, lead times, consumption variability and service-level requirements, including min/max, reorder-point and safety-stock settings.

Apply advanced inventory segmentation and demand profiling, including ABC/XYZ and criticality-based analysis, to differentiate stocking policies and focus attention on the highest-value and highest-risk materials.

Lead demand analysis and forecasting, challenge assumptions with Operations and Maintenance, and translate operating and maintenance plans into a coordinated inventory and materials plan.

Manage critical spares, bulk commodities, repairables and other major cost-driver categories to protect site reliability while controlling inventory investment.

Drive inventory optimization and working-capital improvement by reducing excess, obsolete and slow-moving stock, improving inventory turns and days-on-hand, and releasing value without creating unacceptable operational risk.

Govern item-master and catalogue data in JDE/ERP, including descriptions, units of measure, classifications, lead times, stocking types and planning parameters; eliminate duplicates and maintain strong data quality.

Control new-item creation and Phase In/Phase Out decisions using criticality, demand, lead time, interchangeability and stocking-risk assessments.

Lead annual stock counts and risk-based cycle-count programs and ensure high-value and high-risk inventory receives appropriate count coverage and control.

Investigate physical-to-system variances, inventory adjustments, negative stock and recurring transaction errors; identify root causes and implement sustainable corrective controls.

Act as the functional expert for inventory processes in JDE/ERP and associated tools, ensuring system settings, workflows, transactions and controls support accurate and efficient inventory management.

Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting for inventory value, service level, stockouts, forecast accuracy, turns, days-on-hand, ageing, excess and obsolete stock and count accuracy.

Use large datasets and analytical tools to identify abnormal consumption, emerging stockout risk, overstock, parameter issues and inventory trends, and convert findings into clear, evidence-based actions.

Ensure accurate and timely receipt, inspection, binning, storage, preservation, issue, movement and dispatch of materials, with strong transaction discipline and prompt resolution of discrepancies.

Maintain secure, orderly and fit-for-purpose warehouses, yards and storage areas with effective preservation, location control, housekeeping, material-handling, HSE and asset-security practices.

jobs.title: Advisor, Human Resources (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

Reporting to the Business Partner, Human Resources, the Advisor, Human Resources provides front-line Human Resources advisory and support to employees, supervisors, and site leaders across the Great Bear Project. This role supports employee relations, disciplinary and fact-finding meetings, investigations, attendance and performance management, policy interpretation, workforce administration, payroll support, onboarding, training coordination, and employee lifecycle processes. The Advisor, Human Resources helps leaders apply Human Resources programs consistently, address workplace issues early, and maintain a safe, compliant, and productive work environment during the transition from construction to operations.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Provide front-line HR advice to employees, supervisors, and site leaders on policy interpretation, employee inquiries, workforce administration, and day-to-day employee relations matters.

Support employee relations activities, including disciplinary interviews, fact-finding meetings, investigations, attendance management, performance management, accommodation and return-to-work processes, and related documentation.

Gather information, prepare interview questions, participate in meetings, document findings, identify risks, and escalate complex or sensitive employee relations matters to the Business Partner, Human Resources as required.

Coach supervisors and site leaders on performance expectations, progressive discipline, attendance standards, respectful workplace practices, and preparation for difficult employee conversations.

Maintain Human Resource Information System (HRIS) records and support HR data accuracy through regular audits, reporting, and record maintenance.

Maintain accurate and confidential employee files and records in accordance with Company standards and applicable privacy requirements.

Support site payroll administration, including time and attendance review, discrepancy follow-up, employee payroll inquiries, and coordination with payroll resources to ensure accurate and timely processing.

A Great Place to Work

Who We Are

Founded in 1993, Kinross is a Canadian-based senior gold mining company with operations and projects in the United States, Brazil, Mauritania, Chile and Canada. Our focus on delivering value is based on our four core values of Putting People First, Outstanding Corporate Citizenship, High Performance Culture, and Rigorous Financial Discipline.

Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

 Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC). 

Job Description

To oversee the daily activities of the global engineering function for major projects and site led activities, to support developing and deploying engineering talent at Kinross.

The role will report to the Senior Director, Engineering & Energy and work closely with Kinross’ Corporate and Site leadership teams, Supply Chain, Technical Services, Strategic Business Planning, Projects, Corporate Development, Safety, Sustainability, Maintenance, and Continuous improvement to support a portfolio of operations and projects.   

Job Responsibilities

Manage Kinross’ corporate engineering department

Scope includes mechanical, piping, civil, structural engineering, electrical, instrumentation and controls

Establish or update engineering corporate standards and documents for engineering at Kinross, for use both on major projects and sustaining capital projects

Stay in contact with Project Directors to understand evolving needs of the project and performance of engineer(s) supporting the project 

As required, review the quality of engineering work taking place on a project (e.g., QA/QC audit) from study phase through to construction and commissioning

Assist Supply Chain in preparing and executing engineering service agreements, procurement and construction contracts

Provide technical support to site operations

Provide engineering services and support for workstreams led by sites. This may include field visits, technical analysis, peer review of work by others, engineering calculations, preparation of engineering documents, and recommendations

Support in developing the resulting capital estimates and project execution plans

Minimum Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Experience with engineering management of large projects.  This includes development and management of scope of work, schedules, budget as well as co-ordination.  Working with engineering consultants, vendors, contractors and other stakeholders.  

Ability to work independently as well as part of large multi-disciplinary teams

International experience is an asset

Project management or operational experience are an asset

Language skills in Spanish, French or Portuguese are an asset

Other Attributes

Team player, pro-active, and ability to drive co-operative solutions in situations where there is no direct authority

Works well in a structured, corporate environment

Able to travel domestically and internationally for short periods

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

jobs.title: Process Control Engineer (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The Process Control Engineer is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing process control systems that support safe, reliable, and efficient mineral processing operations at the Round Mountain Gold Mine. This role focuses on improving plant stability, throughput, recovery, and equipment performance through effective control strategies, automation enhancements, and close collaboration with operations, metallurgy, and maintenance teams.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

Process Control & Automation
•    Design, implement, maintain, and optimize control strategies for crushing, grinding, classification, leaching, adsorption, detoxification, and ancillary systems as applicable.
•    Configure, troubleshoot, and support plant control systems (e.g., DCS, PLCs, HMI/SCADA) to ensure high system availability and reliability.
•    Develop and tune regulatory, advanced, and model-based control loops to improve process stability and metallurgical performance.
•    Lead and support control system upgrades, logic changes, alarm management, and interface improvements in accordance with site change management procedures.
Operational Support
•    Partner with Operations and Metallurgy to identify process constraints and variability, and implement control solutions that improve throughput, recovery, and reagent efficiency.
•    Provide on-shift and off-shift technical support for control system issues impacting production or safety.
•    Analyze process data and trends to proactively identify opportunities for improvement and risk mitigation.
Maintenance & Reliability Interface
•    Work closely with the Process Maintenance Superintendent and maintenance teams to support instrumentation, control hardware, and network reliability.
•    Support preventative maintenance strategies, control system documentation, and lifecycle management of automation assets.
•    Assist with root cause analysis for process upsets and equipment or control-related failures.
Safety, Compliance & Standards
•    Promote a strong safety culture by ensuring control systems support safe operating limits and critical safeguards.
•    Participate in hazard analyses, management of change (MOC), and operational readiness reviews.
Projects & Continuous Improvement
•    Provide process control expertise for capital projects, plant modifications, and technology trials.
•    Develop functional specifications, FAT/SAT documentation, and commissioning plans for automation-related projects.
•    Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on cost reduction, energy efficiency, and operational excellence.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Automation, or a related discipline.
•    5–8 years of experience in process control or automation within mineral processing, mining, or heavy industrial environments.
•    Familiarity with CMMS 
•    Hands-on experience with DCS and/or PLC platforms commonly used in mining operations (e.g., Honeywell, ABB, Emerson, Rockwell).
•    Strong understanding of mineral processing unit operations and their control requirements.
•    Control loop tuning, alarm management, and control system troubleshooting.
•    Process data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., Wonderware, PI System or equivalent historians).
•    Instrumentation fundamentals, including flow, level, pressure, density, and analytical measurements.
•    Familiarity with advanced process control (APC) concepts is preferred.
•    Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
•    Ability to work effectively across operations, maintenance, and technical disciplines.
•    Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into operational guidance.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Has a strong commitment to Environmental, health and safety.
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment.
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions and behaviors.
•    Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements.

Kinross Competencies

•    Strategic Effectiveness
Develops and communicates creative business strategies that drive sustainable value.
•    External Engagement
Understands and builds relationships with external parties that strengthen and sustain competitive advantage.
•    Business Focus
Applies commercial rigor and discipline to all business decisions and relationships.
•    Living the Kinross Values
Aligns behavior, decisions, and actions with Kinross values and principles.

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

jobs.description:
La mina La Coipa de Kinross está ubicada en la Región de Atacama en el norte de Chile, aproximadamente 1.000 kilómetros al norte de Santiago y 140 kilómetros al noreste de Copiapó. La Coipa vertió su primera barra de oro en marzo de 2022 después de reiniciar las operaciones luego de la suspensión en 2013. Kinross está llevando a cabo un programa de exploración para extender potencialmente la vida útil de la mina.

Kinross Chile ha construido relaciones sólidas con sus comunidades anfitrionas basadas en la confianza y el respeto a través del compromiso y la consulta. La operación se abastece con en un 100% con energías renovables no convencionales para satisfacer sus necesidades de energía.

Descripción del puesto

Inspeccionar y diagnosticar con la instrumentación adecuada y en base a los programas, normas y procedimientos del área, las intervenciones a los equipos mina para detectar y prevenir fallas, garantizando la disponibilidad y confiabilidad de los equipos según las políticas, normas y procedimientos de MDO y Kinross. En caso de necesidad operacional está facultado para participar en el proceso de mantenimiento equipos.

Responsabilidades del puesto

Inspeccionar, detectar y diagnosticar equipos e instalaciones para identificar tendencias (ruido, vibración, temperatura, mapas de fisuras) mediante técnicas de ensayos no destructivos.

Diagnosticar fallas como desalineamiento, fallas de rodamientos o cavitaciones, manteniendo el equipamiento de medición en óptimo estado y ejecutando medidas de control de riesgos.

Confeccionar y enviar informes de diagnóstico y recomendaciones a los responsables de mantenimiento para evitar fallas prematuras. 

Realizar informes semanales sobre el estado de condición de los principales activos a su cargo.

Velar por el fiel cumplimiento de las normas y procedimientos de la empresa, el control de pérdidas y las políticas de Seguridad y Medio Ambiente, resguardando su propia seguridad y la del equipo.

Formación y experiencia

Título de Técnico Universitario con mención en Mecánica - Eléctrica, o 12 años de experiencia en mantenimiento de equipos mineros.

7 años de experiencia en mantenimiento y análisis sintomático de equipos mineros de alto tonelaje (camiones, cargadores, motoniveladoras, bulldozer, entre otros).

Experiencia en diagnóstico y monitoreo de condiciones a componentes mayores, estructura y sistemas de control (análisis de vibraciones, termografía, ensayos no destructivos, mapas de fisuras).

Experiencia en administración y reportabilidad de mantenimiento. 

Conocimientos en metrología y soldadura.

Mantenimiento de equipos mineros (camiones, cargadores, motoniveladoras, bulldozer, etc.) 

Manejo de Excel, Word y ERPs a nivel usuario.

Nivel de inglés Intermedio.

Kinross es una empresa minera de oro senior global con sede en Canadá con operaciones y proyectos en los Estados Unidos, Brasil, Mauritania, Chile y Canadá. Nuestro enfoque en la entrega de valor se basa en nuestros principios básicos de minería responsable, excelencia operativa, crecimiento disciplinado y solidez del balance. jobs.description:
Start Date: ASAP
Work Model: Hybrid 
Location: Downtown Toronto (outside Union Station – TTC & GO accessible)
Dress Code: Business Casual 
A Great Place to Work

Who We Are

Founded in 1993, Kinross is a Canadian-based senior gold mining company with operations and projects in the United States, Brazil, Mauritania, Chile and Canada. Our focus on delivering value is based on our four core values of Putting People First, Outstanding Corporate Citizenship, High Performance Culture, and Rigorous Financial Discipline.

Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC).

Job Summary

The Reliability Engineer, as part of the Asset Management team, plays a vital role in enhancing the reliability, performance, and life cycle management of critical equipment assets. This role involves analyzing equipment performance data, implementing predictive and preventive maintenance strategies, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to optimize asset reliability, availability, and maintainability. The engineer will conduct root cause failure analysis (RCFA), develop corrective action plans, and drive continuous improvement initiatives to minimize downtime, reduce maintenance costs, and improve asset performance. Working closely with the broader Asset Management team, the engineer ensures alignment with the overall asset management strategy, while ensuring compliance with safety and regulatory standards. The ultimate objective is to maximize the operational life of key assets, improve overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), and contribute to the success of the asset management program. Will also lead and mentor junior engineers, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement. This position requires 50%+ travel to remote sites overseas, ensuring that global operations are supported for reliability excellence.

Key Responsibilities

1. Asset Performance and Reliability Analysis:

Analyze asset performance data to identify trends, potential failures, and areas for improvement in the life cycle of critical equipment.

Develop and execute strategies to optimize asset reliability, availability, and maintainability (RAM) across the organization.

2. Failure Mode and Root Cause Analysis

Perform Failure Mode Effects and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA) to identify underlying issues causing equipment failure.

Develop and implement corrective and preventive actions to address recurring failures and improve overall equipment performance.

3. Data Analysis & Risk Assessment

Develop and track reliability performance metrics such as Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), and others.

Provide regular reports to senior management, highlighting reliability performance, asset health, and areas for improvement.

Ensure that reliability strategies and asset management practices adhere to industry standards, regulations, and safety guidelines (e.g., ISO 55000, PAS 55).

Assess and mitigate risks related to equipment failure, safety hazards, and operational impact on asset performance.

4. Maintenance Optimization

Apply RCM principles to prioritize and optimize maintenance tasks based on asset criticality and failure consequences.

Identify and implement improvements to maintenance strategies that maximize asset life and performance while reducing costs.

5. Asset Management Strategy Development

As a key member of asset management team develop and implement a comprehensive asset management strategy that aligns with organizational goals.

Ensure asset management policies are integrated with reliability engineering practices to optimize the lifecycle of key assets.

Conduct life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) for major assets to assess their total cost of ownership and identify cost-saving opportunities.

Ensure that asset management decisions are based on long-term value rather than short-term costs.

6. Project Management

6. Project Management

Manage and oversee reliability projects from conception to completion, ensuring they are delivered on time and within budget.

Coordinate with project teams, vendors, and contractors to ensure alignment with reliability objectives.

7. Technical Leadership & Mentorship

Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior reliability engineers and maintenance personnel.

Lead training sessions and workshops to promote a culture of reliability within the organization.

8. Compliance & Safety

Ensure all reliability engineering activities comply with industry standards, regulations, and company policies.

Participate in safety audits, inspections, and reviews to identify and address potential reliability issues.

9. Global Support & Travel

Provide on-site support and expertise to remote sites overseas, ensuring consistent reliability practices and solutions across all locations.

Facilitate the implementation of global reliability initiatives, adapting strategies to local conditions and challenges.

10. Continuous Improvement

Drive continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities for cost reduction, process optimization, and reliability enhancement.

Stay updated with the latest industry trends, technologies, and best practices in reliability engineering.Collaborate with maintenance, operations, safety, and engineering teams to align on reliability goals and ensure smooth asset management execution.

Job Summary

The IAM Specialist is responsible for the design, implementation, integration, and ongoing operation of the organization’s identity infrastructure, with primary ownership of Active Directory (AD), Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), and the enterprise Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) platform. This is a hands-on engineering role that is evolving from operational execution toward strategic oversight: as automation and AI take on routine identity tasks, the engineer increasingly acts as an architect of the organization’s identity fabric — ensuring security, resilience, interoperability, and compliance across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. The successful candidate should be able to understand and manage identity dependencies across infrastructure, cloud platforms, security controls, automations while evaluating the broader impact of identity-related decisions across the enterprise. They will balance deep technical execution (directory services, authentication protocols, governance, automation) with governance, and cross-functional collaboration needed to secure an increasingly autonomous, AI-driven enterprise.

Key Responsibilities

Directory Services (Active Directory & Entra ID)

Responsible for Active Directory modernization, transformation, and future-state architecture.

Administer, secure, and optimize on-premises Active Directory (domains, forests, trusts, Group Policy, DNS, sites & services) and Microsoft Entra ID.

Manage hybrid identity: Entra Connect / Cloud Sync, password hash sync / pass-through authentication, federation, and seamless SSO.

Design and maintain Conditional Access policies, MFA, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), and Identity Protection.

Identity Governance & Administration (IGA)

Manage, configure, and continuously improve the enterprise IGA platform (e.g., Saviynt, SailPoint), including connectors, workflows, and integrations with AD, Entra ID, and downstream applications.

Own the identity lifecycle end to end — provisioning, deprovisioning, and joiner/mover/leaver automation — orchestrated through the IGA platform.

Design and operate access certification and recertification campaigns, segregation-of-duties (SoD) controls, role-based access control (RBAC), and entitlement management.

Build and maintain birthright access, access request and approval workflows, and policy-driven provisioning rules.

Partner with audit, compliance, and application owners to ensure governance controls meet regulatory and internal requirements, and produce evidence for audits.

Authentication, Authorization & Integration

Configure and troubleshoot SSO and application onboarding across SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, and SCIM.

Integrate enterprise applications with Entra ID, AD, and the IGA platform; manage service principals, enterprise apps, app registrations, and API permissions.

Govern machine and workload identities — service accounts, API keys, certificates, and secrets — with appropriate rotation and least-privilege controls.

Automation, Resilience & AI Oversight

Develop and maintain automation (PowerShell, Microsoft Graph API, IGA connectors/SDKs, infrastructure-as-code) to streamline identity workflows.

Apply AI/automation tools to routine identity and governance tasks while maintaining human oversight — validating AI-generated configurations and code, and intervening where nuanced judgment is required.

Conduct resilience and chaos testing of identity systems (e.g., directory outage, MFA bypass scenarios) and lead root-cause analysis during incidents.

Security, Risk & Governance

Enforce identity security best practices, hardening, and Zero Trust principles across AD, Entra ID, and the IGA platform.

Support compliance, audit, and regulatory requirements through access certification, logging, and policy enforcement.

Partner with security operations, DevOps/platform teams, HR, and application owners to embed identity standards across the enterprise.

Qualifications and Skills

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or equivalent experience.

4+ years of hands-on experience with Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID in enterprise/hybrid environments.

Demonstrated experience implementing or operating an enterprise IGA platform (Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent) is highly valued.

Relevant certifications preferred: Microsoft Certified — Identity and Access Administrator (SC-300), Azure Administrator (AZ-104), or vendor IGA certifications (e.g., Saviynt, SailPoint).

Required Technical Skills

Active Directory: Deep expertise in domains, forests, trusts, Group Policy, DNS, replication, FSMO roles, AD security hardening, and recovery.

Microsoft Entra ID: Conditional Access, MFA, PIM, Identity Protection, app registrations, enterprise applications, dynamic groups, and licensing.

Identity Governa

jobs.title: Underground Chief Engineer (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking an experienced Chief Underground Mining Engineer to lead the underground tech services group comprising of mine engineers, planners, surveyors, ventilation engineers, and technical technicians for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Technical Services Manager, you will ensure that the mine’s long-hope stoping mining method is designed, scheduled, and executed safely and profitably. This role will also act as the primary technical liaison between operations, geology, and management. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground mining engineering group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

• Mine Planning & Design
Develop and oversee short , mid , and long range mine plans for a long hole stoping operation using paste backfill and cemented rockfill. Approve stope designs, drill patterns, sequencing, and ground support strategies. Ensure backfill requirements (strength, timing, curing windows) are integrated into the mine schedule. Optimize stope sequencing to balance geotechnical stability, ventilation constraints, and production targets
• Technical Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and develop mine engineers, surveyors, and technical staff. Foster a collaborative environment between engineering and operations, emphasizing problem solving and continuous improvement. Set technical standards, review engineering work, and ensure quality control across all engineering deliverables.
• Operational Support
Provide real time technical guidance to underground operations, including drilling, blasting, backfilling, and ground support installation. Troubleshoot stope performance issues (dilution, overbreak, paste delivery, drilling accuracy). Coordinate with maintenance, backfill plant personnel, and production supervisors to ensure alignment with engineering plans
• Safety, Regulatory, and Environmental Compliance
Ensure all engineering designs comply with MSHA regulations and Nevada state mining requirements. Support and reinforce site Health & Safety Management Systems and environmental compliance programs. Lead risk assessments for new stopes, mining methods, or ground conditions.
• Backfill & Geotechnical Integration
Work closely with geotechnical engineers to ensure stope stability, pillar design, and sequencing meet safety and production needs. Oversee paste backfill and CRF design parameters, QA/QC, and scheduling to maintain mine stability and minimize dilution.

• Budgeting & Project Management
Manage engineering department budgets, staffing, and capital project planning. Lead or support underground capital projects (ventilation upgrades, dewatering systems, new development headings, backfill plant improvements). Evaluate and justify new technologies, equipment, or software to improve efficiency.
• Data Management & Reporting
Oversee production reporting, stope reconciliation, and variance analysis. Ensure accurate survey control, mine modeling, and engineering databases. Present engineering updates to senior leadership and contribute to life of mine planning.

•    8-15+ years of experience in underground hard-rock mining experience, with significant exposure to long-hole stoping
•    Demonstrated experience with paste backfill and CRF operations

Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The Mine Engineer I reports to the Senior Mine Engineer and is responsible for carrying out a full range of engineering functions including, but not limited to: mine planning, leach stacking plans, drill pattern design, drill and blast scheduling, blast pattern design, pit designs, stockpile, road and dump designs, mine analysis and production reporting. Will have direct involvement and communication with staff from other departments (Geology, Geotechnics, Maintenance and Operations).
Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

1.  Develop and communicate engineering plans, technical reports and presentations, sequences, dumping priorities, etc. to Mine Operations and other stakeholders on site and ensure plans are carried out safely and efficiently 
2.  Leading pit tour with mine operations, supporting mine operations on the daily production meeting.
3.  Working on optimizing and improving the short-range planning processes
4.  Develop weekly mine plan, weekly mill feed strategy and perform a weekly mine plan adherence.  
5.  Drill and Blast Planning and Scheduling 
6.  Utilize geological data, mine plans and survey information to develop blast designs and shot timing, and release patterns as required for execution.
7.  Consult and develop a close working relationship with the Geotechnical Engineer in order to optimize pit wall stability.
8.  Perform accurate Drill/Blast pattern design duties on time - Preparation and Implementation of a Weekly Drill and Blast Plan.
9.  Perform pit design, dump design and infrastructure/road design.
10.  Identify risks (production and mine movement, equipment priorities, geotech, dewatering, grade, manpower, etc.) and opportunities that may impact the mine plans.
11.  Ensure information flow and buy-in to the mine plan process from various departments (load and haul, drill and blast, processing, etc).
12.  Collect and interpret technical data such as blast-induced vibration and utilize findings to inform pattern design decisions and improvements, with specific focus on high-risk sectors of the open pit.
13.  Safety Performance & Record, perform field engagement and risk identifications.
14.  Ensure drill & blast planning complies with applicable safety regulations, environmental standards, standard operating procedures and company best practices.
15.  Promote and engage strongly with a pro-active safety culture.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or similar field is required.
2.  1-5 years of planning and/or drill & blast experience in hard-rock, open pit mine operations is strongly preferred.
3.  Proficiency with mining software packages (Deswik, AutoCAD, Vulcan, MineSite) is strongly preferred.
4.  Working knowledge of mine operations and drill & blast principles.
5.  Comfortable working collaboratively in a team environment.
6.  Strong engagement with technical details, self-motivated to learn and continuously improve our mine planning and drill & blast practices.
7.  Must be presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Description

Under the general supervision of the Process Maintenance Supervisor, the Maintenance Mechanic is responsible for performing preventative and corrective maintenance on all plant equipment, including milling, crushing, conveying, flotation, leaching, thickeners, gravity spirals, CICs, elution, refining, pumping, piping, and all supporting infrastructure.

1.    Perform mechanical maintenance, troubleshooting, diagnosis, and repair plant equipment including ADR systems, crushing circuits, milling circuits, and pumping/piping systems.
2.    Operate support equipment such as forklifts and overhead cranes.
3.    Perform bearing analysis and installation.
4.    Complete mechanical projects and fabrication work using basic cutting and welding techniques.
5.    Lubricate equipment, manage oil inventory, and ensure proper disposal of waste oil.
6.    Participate in preventative maintenance and capital/construction projects in coordination with operations and technical services.

9.    Maintain accurate maintenance records and documentation for all work performed.
10.    Attend required classes and complete coursework and lab training as part of an apprenticeship (if enrolled).

12.    Exhibit regular attendance, punctuality, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

2.    Minimum of 3 years of relevant maintenance experience in ADR and/or crusher systems preferred.
3.    Minimum of 3 years of relevant maintenance experience in an industrial setting required.
4.    Enrollment or completion of Millwright Apprenticeship Program preferred (including a minimum of 9 credit hours/semester and monthly lab work at Great Basin College).
5.    Knowledge of lubrication practices and mechanical systems.
6.    Skilled in basic welding and cutting
7.    Certified welding skills beneficial but not required
8.    Strong verbal, written, analytical, and interpersonal skills.
9.    Proficiency with computers and standard office software (Word, Excel, etc.).
10.    Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and all levels of personnel.
11.    Valid driver’s license.
12.    Ability to meet “Authorized User” requirements for High Risk Activities, including Fall Protection and Confined Space.

jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Description

The incumbent will be responsible for the daily operation of heavy equipment in an active surface mine environment. All work must be completed in a safe and efficient manner. The employee will work continuously to align daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values and work in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Job Responsibilities

•    Proficiently operate equipment according to established, safe operating procedures in forward and reverse directions in various weather conditions day or night: rain, snow, fog, cold, heat, and dust; and upon various surface conditions: wet, muddy, snowy, icy, and/or uneven or rock-strewn.
•    Operate in a safe and efficient manner, causing the least wear and/or damage to the equipment and mine property; maintaining the highest level of production possible.
•    Follow direction of dispatch and supervisor.
•    Must be able to operate overhead dispatch display panel and fire suppression system
•    Identify hazards in work areas and report or mitigate the risk appropriately.

•    Be fit for duty, attend and work through scheduled shift without causing harm to self, to others, or to equipment.

jobs.title: Superintendent, Site Services (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

As the Superintendent, Site Services for the Great Bear Project you will provide leadership, planning, and overall accountability for the safe, reliable, and cost-effective delivery of site services. The role leads the operation, maintenance, and repair oversight of surface infrastructure, facilities and utilities, logistics, yard operations, waste management, water treatment, and associated maintenance activities, and provides direction to the Supervisor, Site Services internal crews, and contractors. Until the start of main project construction, you will oversee the maintenance and repair of site infrastructure, utilities, facilities, and non-core operational assets following handover from Project, supporting underground development and exploration including the operation of the 13km Chukuni Pipeline, worker camp and associated effluent treatment system. Upon project transition into full operations, you will assume full accountability for non-core operational assets following handover from Project.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Provide leadership, planning, and direction for site services team responsible for the operation and maintenance of the worker camp, yards, roads, utilities, logistics, site-wide waste management, and non-core infrastructure.

Develop and execute site services budgets, plans, preventative maintenance programs, and resource requirements in alignment with operational priorities. Support to the Projects team on an as-needed basis.

Establish and monitor service levels and key performance indicators for safety, environmental compliance, asset reliability, maintenance completion, cost, budget schedule; identify trends and implement corrective actions.

Provide oversight of contracts and contractors related to site services’ areas of responsibility.

Develop and implement contingency and business continuity planning for utility outages, equipment failures, severe weather, transportation disruptions, and other events that could affect site services.

Lead, coach, and hold accountable the Site Services Supervisor(s) and internal crews; establish clear roles, rotation handovers, staffing plans, training requirements, and performance expectations.

Participate in the development and execution of the Operational Readiness Plan for surface infrastructure, including maintenance strategies, procedures, staffing, training, spares, and service continuity.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A minimum of 7–10 years of progressive experience in site services, facilities, infrastructure, maintenance, logistics, or related functions within mining, construction, or industrial environments, including 3-5 years in a supervisory or superintendent capacity.

Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and contractors in a remote operating environment, during the start up phase, is required. 

A technical diploma, trade certificate, or equivalent combination of education and experience in mining, mechanical systems, and/or facilities management is preferred.

Strong working knowledge of site services support equipment such as forklifts, skid steers, generators, etc.

Strong knowledge of carpentry, plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems and maintenance best practices.

Knowledge of materials-handling practices, lifting and rigging requirements, and safe equipment operation.

Experience with contractor management and project execution in remote mining environments.

Ability to read, interpret, and apply operating manuals and procedures.

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 Hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position is based in Red Lake, Ontario. Local candidates, or those willing to relocate, with relocation assistance, will be given priority for this position. The schedule for this position is 14X14, 12 hour days.

The base salary for the Superintendent, Site Services is $140,000.00 to $170,000.00 + Short Term Incentive, + Long Term Incentive, + Group Benefit Coverage.

jobs.title: IT Specialist (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The IT Specialist is a hands‑on, customer‑focused technologist who keeps Bald Mountain’s users productive and our site technology resilient. The IT Specialist will split time between first‑line/second‑line support and have ownership of core systems: Windows servers/Active Directory, IGA (Identity Governance and Administration), Nutanix‑based virtualization and storage, Cisco switching and fiber, point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless links, and Dell client endpoints. The IT Specialist will collaborate with OT and plant teams to support industrial networks and site infrastructure. 

Essential Functions

1.    Systems analysis techniques and procedures, including consulting with end users, contractors and vendors to determine hardware and software or system functional specifications.
2.    Design, documentation, analysis, testing of computer systems or programs, based on site and department specifications. 
3.    Serve as a primary contact for the North America Service Desk; troubleshoot and resolve incidents/requests for Windows 11, Windows Server 2019 and newer, O365, Teams, Printing, VPN, and core business apps with high first‑time‑fix rates.
4.    Provide one‑on‑one and small‑group end‑user training; write how‑to guides and knowledge base articles.
5.    Administer Windows Server/AD, DNS/DHCP, GPO, and patching; monitor backups and recovery procedures.
6.    Operate Nutanix‑based clusters (compute/storage/virtualization) and site NAS/SAN (Dell/Synology); perform capacity and health checks and coordinate upgrades with vendors.
7.    Maintain and administer campus/industrial Ethernet (Cisco) switching, VLANs, QoS, link aggregation, and optics; ensure fiber plant integrity and documentation.
8.    Support site point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless systems (backhaul and access), including design inputs, LOS checks, and alignment/validation.
9.    Support for Cisco Desk Telephones and Teleconference Systems including Cisco desk telephones and teleconference systems.
10.    Partner with Operational and Support Departments on industrial networks, historian/SCADA connectivity, and change management that protects safety and uptime.
11.    Own device imaging/provisioning for Dell laptops/workstations; manage asset inventory and lifecycle.
12.    Follow site safety and LOTOTO practices; complete required MSHA new‑miner training; adhere to Kinross Americas Safety Guidelines in all work.
13.    Contribute to change records and diagrams; keep runbooks, network maps, and rack elevations current.
14.    Participate in after‑hours and weekend support rotation; travel to comm sites and facilities around the property as needed (all weather).
15.    Work independently and with minimal supervision.  Present concerns and potential solution to KNV IT Leadership for decision making as appropriate.  

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Advance knowledge in information technology, information systems and/or networking or 3+ years’ experience in a relevant field required.
•    Experience in IT support/operations with demonstrated customer service mindset.
•    Solid skills with Windows client/Server, AD, DNS/DHCP, GPO, and endpoint management; strong troubleshooting across OS/app/network stacks.
•    Hands‑on experience with Cisco switching and fiber (port/VLAN provisioning, SFPs, optics, link testing).
•    Working knowledge of wireless links (P2P/PMP) and fundamentals like RSSI/SNR, alignment, and link budgets.
•    Familiarity with virtualization and enterprise storage (Nutanix preferred) and backup/recovery workflows.
•    Ability to create and deliver clear user training and concise documentation.
•    Valid driver’s license; ability to safely work at heights/rack spaces and lift up to ~50 lbs; willingness to work outdoors in a mine environment.
•    Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive business or personal information.
•    Commitment to ethical conduct and compliance with Kinross data protection and privacy standards

Preferred Experience

•    Certifications: CompTIA A+/Network+, CCNA, Microsoft MD‑102/Windows, AZ‑104, Nutanix NCP.
•    Experience in OT/industrial networks and CPwE concepts; exposure to SCADA/historian connectivity.
•    Scripting/automation (PowerShell), imaging tools, and endpoint security/patching platforms.
•    Familiar with JDE system for equipment procurement.

Lead the execution of the long-term strategy for multi-discipline functions including the following departments: mine, processing, asset management, and geology.

Oversee site performance metrics, operational plans, and cost forecasts, ensuring targets are met or exceeded.

Formulates the annual operating and capital budgets for the function consistent with Kinross’ established financial guidelines and business planning process.

 Prepares business cases and reports regarding strategic projects and initiatives and presents recommendations and status updates to key stakeholders

Act as a change agent and project sponsor for key initiatives; models organizational values, sets the cultural tone, and prioritizes business goals.

Lead the Continuous Improvement program using tools and systems that support Kinross’ management operating philosophy.

Set performance targets and measures, monitors, and manages overall performance of direct reports and operational departments.
