jobs.title: Core Logging Geologist (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

Under the guidance of the Chief Geologist, the Core Logging Geologists will be positive hard working team players who are passionate about geology and help to grow the Kinross – Great Bear project from generative exploration and drill targeting, through to resource delineation and grade control in the future Open Pit and Underground environments. Core Logging Geologists will work independently to better understand all geologic factors and bring forward ideas to further improve our understanding of the mineralized system and surrounding areas.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

The primary duty will be logging diamond drill core with an emphasis on recording lithology, structure mineralization and alteration. 

A geological interpretation may be required after each hole, or fan of logging is completed.

Provide drill shutdowns and line ups when survey team is not available.  

Fill-in for UG/OP Beat Geologists as necessary.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A Bachelor of Science in Geology or Earth Sciences is required. Professional Geoscience or G.I.T is beneficial. There is no minimum experience requirement for this position; however, individuals with previous exploration experience is beneficial. 

Previous core logging experience is considered an asset. 

Experience with Leapfrog, or similar program is desired. 

Ability to plan drill holes and interpret results. 

Capable of learning and adapting to new equipment and software.

Comprehends and capable of interpreting technical language. 

High level of technical skills in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook).

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement 

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program (Living our Values Award Program)

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position is based in Red Lake, Ontario. Local candidates, or those willing to relocate with relocation assistance, will be given priority for this position. The local schedule is 8X6. However, a FIFO/DIDO arrangement may be considered with a schedule of 21X14.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary range for the Core Logging Geologist is $85,000 to $100,000 + Short Term Incentive Bonus, + Group Benefit Coverage. 

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate's experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. 

In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development.

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

jobs.description:

Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

The Senior Mine Engineer (Long Range) is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing the Life of Mine (LOM) plans and designs for Kinross Nevada open-pit operations. This role ensures long-term strategic plans are economically optimized, safe, and compliant with geotechnical and environmental standards. They work closely with technical services, geology, and site management to maximize shareholder value and operational performance.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

2.    Design And Modelling: Create open pits, waste rock dumps, haul roads and stormwater drainages. Able to check block models using drill data, run statistics and create scripts preferred.
3.    Scheduling and Economic Analysis: Integrates short-term plans into long-term, and life-of-mine plans. Perform excel level economic analysis. Support feasibility studies (NI 43-101) as required.
4.    Reconciliation and Compliance: Analyzes and interprets mine plans to ensure alignment with financial, environmental and operational objectives. Perform reconciliation of actuals vs. planned production, updating plans to reflect reality while maximizing NPV.
5.    Collaboration: Work with short range planners, environmental, exploration, metallurgy, geotech, maintenance, and leadership teams to ensure long term plans are technically sound.
6.    Innovation: Researches information to support decision-making and improve processes, technologies or methodologies.
7.    Safety and Mentorship: Contributes to safety culture, and the development of policies and practices. Must be willing to take on cross-rotation assignments within the Technical Services Group for personal development.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

4.    General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations.

7.    Strong communication skills (written and verbal) including presenting to senior leadership.

Liderar la planificación, coordinación y ejecución de estudios de proyectos de crecimiento en las etapas de alcance, prefactibilidad y factibilidad liderando equipos multidisciplinarios con énfasis en la excelencia técnica, la rentabilidad y la alineación con las prioridades estratégicas de Kinross.

Definir y gestionar los alcances de los estudios en coordinación con departamentos técnicos y consultores externos.

Discover a rewarding career opportunity at Kinross in the stunning rural landscapes of Washington State.  Recognized for our leadership in low-impact mine development and nationally acclaimed for our reclamation and closure practices, our team has produced gold from six different deposits in the region since 1990.  Currently we are advancing a multi-year pipeline of projects and growing our team to ensure effective delivery and seamless transition into operations.

Job Summary

The Accounting Technician provides essential support to the site finance team by maintaining accurate financial records, processing transactions, and ensuring compliance with internal and external accounting standards. This role focuses on day-to-day accounting tasks such as data entry, reconciliations, and preparing routine reports, enabling smooth financial operations and supporting senior accountants.

Essential Functions

Maintain and update financial records, ledgers, and subsidiary journals for site operations.

Process accounts payable and receivable, ensure timely payments to suppliers and prompt collection of receivables.

Prepare and record journal entries, ensuring accuracy prior to posting.

Perform monthly bank and account reconciliations to maintain data integrity.

Assist with payroll processing and calculation of pay cheques and related deductions.

Compile and distribute reports such as cost analyses, statements, invoices, and regulatory documentation.

Support audits by providing documentation and resolving discrepancies.

Implement internal controls and monitor compliance to protect company assets.

Assist with maintaining and updating accounting software or ERP systems as required.

Retain and organize technical and financial records to ensure compliance with operational and industry requirements.

Respond to internal and external requests for financial documents and information.

Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skills

High school diploma or equivalent required; post-secondary coursework in accounting, finance, or bookkeeping preferred.

3 years of related experience in accounting or bookkeeping; mining or industrial experience considered an asset.

Attention to detail, strong numeracy, and analytical skills.

Computer proficiency in Microsoft Excel, general ledger, and accounting software.

Ability to maintain confidentiality and demonstrate ethical conduct in managing sensitive records.

Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Organizational skills for managing multiple tasks and meeting deadlines.

Sound understanding of basic accounting principles and practices.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Valid driver’s license and authorized to work in the US.

jobs.title: Part-time Equipment Operator (Relief Operator) (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

We are seeking candidates interested in a
part-time Relief Operator position
operating off-road haul trucks in an active mine environment. 

This position will work a
7-on / 7-off schedule, approximately 9 hours per shift
, with employees assigned to either
straight day shift or straight night shift
. Employees will not rotate between days and nights. The schedule will not exceed
130 hours per month
.

Employees are responsible for commuting to and from the mine site. Company medical insurance is not provided for this position; however, an
insurance stipend may be available
for employees who do not have access to other medical coverage.

Relief Drivers must be able to work effectively both independently and as part of the Operations team and be willing to adapt to changing priorities, assignments, and operating conditions. All work must be performed safely and efficiently while demonstrating Kinross’ values in day-to-day responsibilities.

Assigned schedules and shift hours may be subject to change based on the needs of the Relief Driver Program.

Essential Functions

1. Operate an off-road haul truck as a relief operator to support break management.
2. Operate equipment in a safe and efficient manner, minimizing wear and/or damage to equipment and mine property while maintaining the highest level of production possible and hauling material from point A to point B.
3. Maintain knowledge of work areas and dump locations within the mine. Demonstrate a strong commitment to safety and a basic knowledge of pit policies and procedures.
4. Maintain basic knowledge of mechanical systems and demonstrate the ability to perform and document a thorough pre-operational inspection to evaluate the mechanical condition of the truck.
5. Be responsible for the care and custody of assigned equipment.
6. Understand the functions of the Caterpillar EMS/VIMS panel.
7. Be able to operate CAT MineStar (dispatch operating system).
8. Maintain accurate records of loads hauled and trucks relieved.
9. Comply with all Company policies and procedures, including but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality, and Code of Conduct requirements.
10. Meet or exceed established performance expectations set by management.
11. Consistently exercise discretion and judgment in job performance.
12. Perform work without risk or harm to self or others.
13. Maintain punctuality and regular attendance.
14. Work and collaborate effectively with department personnel to perform the duties and responsibilities of the position.
15. Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1. Must be able to operate a two-way radio and follow instructions.
2. Possess good communication and interpersonal skills.
3. General understanding of mining operations is preferred but not required.
4. Must be able to read and understand written documentation and communicate effectively with employees and management at all levels.
5. Must be self-motivated and able to work independently as well as part of a team.
6. Must be able to perform within the qualifications outlined in the applicable physical demands documentation.
7. Must be receptive to feedback and willing to improve in areas as needed.
8. Previous off-highway heavy equipment or haul truck operating experience is preferred but not required.
9. Previous experience working in an active mine environment is preferred but not required.
10. A valid driver’s license is required.

jobs.title: Mine Electrician (Republic, WA, US)
jobs.description:
Discover a rewarding career opportunity at Kinross in the stunning rural landscapes of Washington State.  Recognized for our leadership in low-impact mine development and nationally acclaimed for our reclamation and closure practices. Our team has produced gold from six different deposits in the region since 1990.  Currently we are advancing a multi-year pipeline of projects and growing our team to ensure effective delivery and seamless transition into operations.

Job Summary

The Mine Electrician is responsible for the safe installation, maintenance, testing, and repair of high voltage (HV) electrical systems that support reliable operations at the Curlew mine. This role ensures the integrity and availability of critical power distribution infrastructure—including transformers, substations, switchgear, and overhead/underground distribution systems, and 480v and 120v systems on the underground mobile fleet. The position plays a key role in system reliability, operational continuity, and the safe execution of electrical work, in alignment with Kinross values, policies, and all MSHA and regulatory requirements.

Essential Functions

Participate in planning, installation, commissioning, and upgrade projects for high voltage electrical systems and distribution infrastructure across the Curlew mine site.

Install, inspect, maintain, test, and repair high voltage equipment such as transformers, circuit breakers, switchgear, substations, and overhead/underground power lines.

Test, repair, install and maintain 480v and 120v systems on the mobile underground fleet of Development jumbos, bolters, and Production drills.

Install and maintain the mine’s communications network infrastructure such as Femco mine phones, leaky feeder, and assist with network communications such as fiber optic.

Conduct high voltage switching operations, isolations/LOTO, grounding procedures, and energization of circuits in accordance with KRO procedures, MSHA requirements, and electrical codes.

Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve faults in high voltage distribution systems using specialized test equipment, schematics, and technical standards.

Perform routine thermography, insulation resistance testing, contact resistance testing, relay checks, and other preventive maintenance tasks.

Maintain readiness of critical HV components and ensure appropriate inventory levels for rapid response to system failures or operational disruptions.

Support coordination between electrical, maintenance, operations, and engineering teams during outages, shutdowns, and system upgrades.

Ensure all HV work is performed safely, meeting Kinross SafeGround expectations and following NFPA 70E, MSHA, NEC, and company electrical standards.

Document maintenance, inspections, switching activities, testing results, and repair work in the CMMS for compliance, traceability, and long-term reliability tracking.

Mentor and support lower-level electricians in safe HV work practices, reinforcing a safety-first culture.

Participate in energy efficiency and cost reduction initiatives related to power distribution reliability and usage.

Maintain strong housekeeping and ensure all tools, PPE, and equipment are inspected and maintained in proper working conditions.

Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications and Skills

High school diploma or GED required.

Electrical trade qualification or diploma, with HV Switching Operator certification and current electrical license (Grade A or equivalent) preferred.

5+ years of experience working at an underground mining operation.

Current Underground 5000-23 preferred.

Experience maintaining and repairing transformers, substations, breakers, relays, and switchgear.

Strong knowledge of high voltage switching procedures, arc flash safety, and electrical isolation practices.

Ability to read and interpret HV diagrams, one-line drawings, and electrical schematics.

Proficient in troubleshooting HV faults with appropriate diagnostic tools.

Good communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with multi-disciplinary teams.

Strong understanding of MSHA regulations, NEC, NFPA 70E, and other applicable electrical safety standards.

Able to prioritize work, respond effectively to urgent electrical issues, and manage conflicting priorities.

Capable of working independently with minimal supervision and mentoring less experienced personnel.

Work performed indoors and outdoors in a remote mine site environment, with exposure to weather, heights, energized equipment, and high-voltage hazards.

Valid driver's license and authorized to work in the US.

jobs.title: Underground Maintenance Mechanic (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Description

Under the direction of the Underground Mobile Maintenance Supervisor, the Underground Mobile Maintenance Technician is responsible for safely inspecting, troubleshooting, servicing, and repairing underground mobile mining equipment in both shop and field environments. This role supports reliable production by maintaining loaders, haul trucks, drills, bolters, shotcrete and support equipment, with a strong focus on safety, equipment availability, diagnostic accuracy, and quality workmanship in a fast-paced underground mining operation. 

Job Responsibilities

Comply with all company policies, procedures, and applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements, including underground mining standards and safe work practices. 

Inspect, troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair underground mobile equipment including loaders, haul trucks, drills, bolters, shotcrete equipment, utility vehicles, and other support equipment. 

Perform planned maintenance, component change-outs, breakdown repairs, and follow-up inspections in both underground field locations and shop settings. 

Troubleshoot hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, powertrain, and braking systems using schematics, manuals, onboard diagnostics, and technical support resources. 

Read and interpret service manuals, blueprints, parts information, and equipment schematics to complete accurate and efficient repairs. 

Complete detailed work orders, service reports, failure documentation, and parts requests with a high level of accuracy and timeliness. 

Maintain high housekeeping standards in work areas, service trucks, and shops to support a safe and efficient underground maintenance environment. 

Work closely with operations, planning, warehouse, and fellow maintenance team members to minimize downtime and support reliable production. 

Demonstrate ownership of assigned equipment, tools, and tasks while consistently meeting performance, attendance, and workmanship expectations. 

Support continuous improvement efforts, share technical knowledge with teammates, and assist in developing less experienced maintenance personnel. 

Perform other related duties as assigned by supervision in support of underground maintenance and production objectives. 

Education and Experience

Qualifications and Education Requirements  

Three (3) or more years of heavy equipment maintenance experience preferred, with underground mobile maintenance experience strongly preferred. 

Strong troubleshooting and repair skills in hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, and powertrain systems on underground mining equipment required. 

Experience maintaining underground equipment such as loaders, haul trucks, jumbos, bolters, drills, shotcrete units, and utility/support equipment preferred. 

Strong background in underground drilling and bolting equipment repair is highly preferred. 

Ability to read and interpret schematics, service manuals, technical bulletins, and parts information required. 

Experience with OEM diagnostic and service software is preferred. 

Diesel technology training, technical certification, or equivalent hands-on experience is preferred. 

Ability to safely operate support equipment including forklifts, skid steers, telehandlers, service trucks, and similar tools/equipment preferred. 

Strong communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across maintenance and operations teams required. 

Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and perform effectively with limited supervision in a production-driven underground environment required. 

Strong computer skills for work order entry, equipment history review, and maintenance reporting preferred. 

Must have a proven commitment to safety, quality workmanship, and dependable attendance. 

Must be willing and able to work rotating shifts, including days, nights, weekends, holidays, overtime, and callouts as needed to support operations. 

Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 

Valid driver’s license required. 

Skills

Must have sufficient mechanical knowledge. 

4-5 years of underground heavy equipment repair experience preferred. 

Strong troubleshooting and failure analysis skills.   

Must be willing to work overtime on short notice. 

Diesel technician diploma is preferred. 

Ability to operate various equipment including forklifts, skid steers, telehandlers and service trucks.   

Possesses good communication and interpersonal skills.  

General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations. 

Working knowledge and skill with P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation software.  

Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management. 

Ability to work independently and as a member of the management team.  

Demonstrates strong administrative, organizational and technical writing skills. 

Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.  

Requires valid driver’s license.

Works under the direct supervision of the Underground Mobile Maintenance Supervisor.

jobs.title: UG Operations General Supervisor (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit and underground mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

Under the general direction of the UG Mine Manager, the UG Mine General Supervisor provides front-line leadership for safe, efficient, and productive underground mining operations. This role is responsible for leading crews, coordinating daily execution of development and production plans, maintaining compliance with MSHA, Nevada, environmental, and company standards, and building a culture where safety, accountability, communication, and operational excellence are consistently demonstrated. The UG Mine General Supervisor is expected to bring strong underground hard rock mining experience, sound judgment, effective employee leadership, and the ability to make timely decisions in a dynamic mining environment.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Contribute to and carry out a variety of tasks including but not limited to:

•  Lead, coach, and direct underground crews to safely achieve daily, weekly, and monthly development, production, rehabilitation, and construction targets.
•  Plan, prioritize, and assign work for underground activities, including drilling, blasting, ground support, bolting, scaling, mucking, haulage, ventilation, mine services, rehab, and general underground construction.
•  Conduct effective pre-shift meetings, communicate daily objectives, review ground conditions and hazards, confirm equipment availability, and ensure crews understand the work plan before entering the heading.
•  Coordinate closely with Mine Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Geology, Safety, Mine Rescue, and other support groups to ensure work is completed according to mine plans, standards, schedules, and priorities.
•  Verify that crews are trained, competent, properly assigned, and equipped for the work being performed, including task training, equipment authorization, and site-specific underground requirements.
•  Maintain strong field presence in active work areas to inspect headings, observe work practices, reinforce standards, resolve issues, and support safe production.
•  Identify, report, and mitigate hazards related to ground conditions, ventilation, mobile equipment, explosives, traffic management, utilities, water, confined spaces, and changing underground conditions.
•  Ensure pre-operational equipment inspections are completed, deficiencies are documented and escalated, and equipment is used, maintained, and cleaned according to company expectations.
•  Partner with Maintenance to prioritize repairs, manage equipment downtime, coordinate availability of mobile and fixed assets, and support efficient execution of the mine plan.
•  Review and support compliance with engineered mine designs, ground support standards, ventilation requirements, barricading, signage, lockout/tagout, work permits, and standard operating procedures.
•  Promote a proactive safety culture by encouraging hazard recognition, field level risk assessments, stop-work authority, employee engagement, near-miss reporting, and timely corrective action.
•  Take immediate action to stop and correct unsafe conditions, non-standard work, procedural deviations, or behaviors that could impact the safety of employees, contractors, equipment, or the mine.
•  Maintain accountability for crew performance, attendance, timekeeping, productivity, housekeeping, equipment care, and compliance with company policies and site expectations.
•  Support employee development through coaching, performance feedback, skills progression, training follow-up, corrective action, and consistent application of workplace expectations.
•  Prepare, review, and submit accurate shift reports, production updates, safety observations, incident information, equipment status, and other operational documentation as required.
•  Maintain adequate inventories of underground supplies, consumables, ground support materials, tools, and safety equipment needed to support planned work.
•  Respond to emergency situations, follow site emergency response procedures, communicate clearly during escalations, and support incident management as directed.
•  Demonstrate professional leadership through clear communication, sound decision-making, integrity, accountability, and the ability to lead in a high-risk, fast-paced underground environment.
•  Perform other duties as assigned to support safe and efficient underground operations.

The duties and responsibilities listed above are representative of the nature, and level of work assigned and are not necessarily all inclusive.  Other duties and responsibilities will apply.

Required Qualifications / Education

•    Valid drivers license.
•    High school diploma or equivalent required; technical training, associate degree, or bachelor’s degree in mining, engineering, construction management, or a related field preferred.
•    Minimum of six (6) years of underground mining experience preferred, with at least three (3) years in a supervisory, lead hand, shift boss, foreman, or equivalent leadership role.
•    Demonstrated experience leading underground crews in development, production, ground support, drilling and blasting, mucking, haulage, mine services, and/or rehabilitation activities.
•    Strong working knowledge of MSHA requirements, underground mining regulations, Nevada mine safety expectations, company safety systems, and site-specific operating

Job Summary

The Mine Maintenance Supervisor is responsible for leading the safe and efficient execution of fixed maintenance and electrical work at the Curlew mine site. This role ensures equipment reliability, infrastructure integrity, and compliance with safety and regulatory standards while supporting production targets and fostering a strong SafeGround culture

Essential Functions

Supervise and coordinate fixed maintenance and electrical crews to ensure work is executed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with production priorities.

Plan, prioritize, and assign daily and weekly maintenance activities, including preventive and corrective work.

Ensure all work is performed in compliance with MSHA regulations, company policies, and SafeGround principles, including hazard identification, risk mitigation, and stop-work authority.

Oversee maintenance of underground infrastructure including power distribution systems, substations, dewatering systems, ventilation components, and fixed mechanical equipment.

Provide technical guidance and troubleshooting support for complex mechanical, and high-voltage/medium-voltage electrical issues.

Coordinate with Operations, Technical Services, and Planning teams to align maintenance activities with mine production schedules.

Review and approve work orders, ensuring accurate documentation and closure in the CMMS (e.g., JDE).

Lead shift turnover meetings, communicate priorities, and ensure continuity between crews.

Monitor equipment performance and reliability, identifying trends and implementing corrective actions to reduce downtime.

Support contractor management, ensuring work is completed safely and to required standards.

Develop and mentor team members, supporting training, competency development, and performance management.

Participate in incident investigations and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

Maintain housekeeping standards and ensure all work areas meet safety and environmental expectations.

Perform other duties as assigned.

jobs.description:

Job Summary

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking a Underground Surveyor Supervisor to lead the Underground Survey group for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Chief Mine Engineer, you will lead the underground survey department, manage survey standards and quality control, and provide accurate, timely spatial data to engineering, geology, and operations. This role will ensure that all underground workings, long-hole stopes, and infrastructure are surveyed, mapped, and reported to support safe and efficient mining. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground survey group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

•  Survey Leadership and Team Management
Lead, train, and develop the underground survey team, ensuring consistent technical performance and adherence to best practices. Assign daily and weekly survey tasks aligned with mine planning and production priorities. Maintain a culture of safety, accuracy, and continuous improvement within the survey group.
•  Underground Surveying and Data Collection
Establish and maintain underground survey control networks, including primary and secondary control points. Perform development surveys, including heading markups, line and grade, and breakthrough checks. Conduct production surveys for long hole stopes, including collaring, toe checks, and cavity monitoring. Capture as built data for development, infrastructure, and backfill operations.
•  Long-hole Stoping Support
Provide precise drill markups for long hole production drilling. Verify stope boundaries, slot raises, and breakthrough locations to minimize dilution and ensure compliance with design. Survey underground backfill boundaries to support geotechnical and engineering QA/QC.
•  Data Management and Reporting
Maintain accurate survey databases, digital models, and spatial records. Deliver timely updates to mine engineering, geology, and operations, including 3D models, maps, and progress reports. Support reconciliation of planned vs. actual development and stope performance on a regular cadence as needed (daily, weekly, monthly)
•  Technology, Equipment, and Quality Control
Oversee maintenance, calibration, and proper use of survey instruments (total stations, scanners, LiDAR, GPS for surface tie ins). Implement QA/QC procedures for all survey data and deliverables. Evaluate and adopt new survey technologies to improve accuracy and efficiency.

jobs.description:
Discover a rewarding career opportunity at Kinross in the stunning rural landscapes of Washington State.  Recognized for our leadership in low-impact mine development and nationally acclaimed for our reclamation and closure practices, our team has extracted ore from six different deposits in the region since 1989.  Following the conclusion of mining activities in 2017, our operation now manages properties at various stages of exploration, development, care & maintenance, and closure.

Job Summary

The Millwright is responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing fixed plant equipment—including SAG/Ball mills, conveyors, compressors, hydraulic systems, pressure filters, pumps, and piping systems. This role ensures reliable mill operations by conducting preventative maintenance, responding to equipment breakdowns, and supporting safety, production, and environmental goals through technical expertise and effective collaboration with the Processing Maintenance Team.

Essential Functions

Conduct diagnostics, perform repairs, scheduled PMs (preventive maintenance), and remedial work on mill and stationary processing equipment to high compliance and quality standards.

Troubleshoot, modify, fabricate, and repair equipment per supervisor direction; provide input and technical guidance to the maintenance team.

Support all aspects of the preventive maintenance program, including fluid checks, lubrication, sampling, component inspections, and routine servicing.

Maintain accurate records: generate and complete work orders, select and document use of correct parts from warehouse, organize necessary permits (e.g., confine space, lockout/tagout, hot work).

Liaise closely with Mill Supervisors and key stakeholders to prioritize breakdowns and meet production goals.

Ensure proper history and records are kept in the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).

Review and help develop work procedures and JHAs, ensuring risks are identified and mitigated; comply with all safety standards (MSHA, OSHA, and site-specific).

Maintain high housekeeping standards in all work areas and pro-actively identify safety and process improvements

Completion of a recognized Millwright or Industrial Mechanic apprenticeship or similar related trade certification required.

3+ years’ experience maintaining, repairing, and installing fixed plant equipment in a mining or heavy industrial environment.

Strong mechanical, troubleshooting, and fabrication skills with proficiency in welding, alignment, rigging, and hydraulics.

Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, manuals, and equipment schematics accurately.

Strong focus on safety, familiarity with workplace safety standards, and commitment to lockout/tagout and other safety protocols.

jobs.title: Principal Security Architect (Toronto, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
-

Start Date: ASAP
Work Model: Hybrid 
Location: Downtown Toronto (outside Union Station – TTC & GO accessible)
Dress Code: Business Casual 
A Great Place to Work

Who We Are

Founded in 1993, Kinross is a Canadian-based senior gold mining company with operations and projects in the United States, Brazil, Mauritania, Chile and Canada. Our focus on delivering value is based on our four core values of Putting People First, Outstanding Corporate Citizenship, High Performance Culture, and Rigorous Financial Discipline.

Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC).

Job Summary

Kinross Gold is seeking a Principal Security Architect to lead the design and continuous evolution of our incident response and cyber defense architecture. This is a senior, hands-on-yet-strategic role: you will set the technical direction for how Kinross detects, contains, and recovers from threats across a global, hybrid environment spanning corporate IT, cloud, and operating mine sites. This role is defined for the current threat landscape, where AI accelerates both attacks and defense. Routine design, documentation, and signature-based detection work is increasingly automated. Your value lies where automation cannot reach: adversarial thinking, complex risk judgment, validating AI-generated defenses, and translating threat reality into business decisions.

Key Responsibilities

Incident Response Architecture

Own the end-to-end architecture of the incident response capability — detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review — across IT, cloud, and OT environments.

Design, develop, and continuously improve playbooks, escalation paths, and response automation (SOAR / agentic workflows), ensuring human oversight at decision points that carry material risk.

Lead major and complex security incidents, providing senior technical authority and adversarial perspective when automated tooling reaches its limits.

Cyber Defense Design

Define the reference architecture for defensive controls: SIEM/analytics, EDR/XDR, identity protection, network segmentation, and cloud security posture.

Establish detection engineering standards and validate AI- and analytics-driven detections to prevent control gaps from over-trusting automated output.

Conduct threat modeling and attack-path analysis against novel and AI-driven threats, prioritizing creative problem solving over checklist-driven, vendor-led control selection.

AI Oversight & Governance

Govern the responsible use of AI within the security function — setting guardrails for where automation is trusted, where human validation is mandatory, and how AI outputs are verified.

Assess and secure the organization's growing use of AI systems and agents as an emerging attack surface.

Strategic & Cross-Functional Influence

Serve as a trusted advisor to security leadership, translating technical threat and risk into business terms for non-technical stakeholders.

Partner with cloud, infrastructure, enterprise architecture, and operational teams to embed security-by-design into digital and AI initiatives.

Mentor and provide technical oversight to incident responders and analysts, pairing senior judgment with hands-on coaching to keep core skills strong across the team.

Technical Skills

Incident response & forensics: deep, hands-on expertise across the IR lifecycle, including digital forensics, malware triage, log analysis, and root-cause investigation.

Detection & response tooling: advanced command of SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, and threat intelligence platforms; able to architect, integrate, and tune them at enterprise scale.

Cloud & hybrid security: strong working knowledge of securing cloud (Azure, AWS) and on-premises environments, including identity, network segmentation, and cloud security posture management.

Threat & vulnerability management: proven ability in attack-path analysis, adversary emulation, and vulnerability prioritization against both conventional and novel/AI-driven threats.

AI-augmented security: ability to design, supervise, and validate AI- and analytics-driven detection and response, and to secure AI systems and agents as an attack surface.

Architecture & engineering: skilled in security architecture design, and at least one scripting language (e.g., Python, PowerShell) for automation.

Soft Skills

Adversarial thinking: the instinct to anticipate how an attacker behaves and to question assumptions that automated tooling cannot challenge on its own.

Sound judgment under pressure: calm, decisive leadership during active incidents, balancing speed with risk.

Communication & translation: able to abstract complex security needs into clear business language for executives, the board, and non-technical stakeholders.

Cross-functional influence: builds trust and drives alignment across IT, business, and operational teams without relying on direct authority.

Mentorship & collaboration: develops talent, coaches junior analysts, and sustains peer-review and knowledge-sharing as routine work automates.

Adaptability & continuous learning: embraces evolving responsibilities and emerging technologies with curiosity rather than resistance.

Ethical stewardship: applies responsible judgment to AI oversight and high-stakes risk decisions.

Qualifications and Skills

10+ years in cybersecurity, with significant depth in security architecture; senior incident-handling experience required.

You’ll split time between first‑line/second‑line support and ownership of core systems: Windows servers/Active Directory, IGA (Identity Governance and Administration), Nutanix‑based virtualization and storage, Cisco switching and fiber, point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless links, and Dell client endpoints. End‑user support & customer service

jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Description

Round Mountain Gold Corporation seeks a Health & Safety Superintendent in Round Mountain, NV. Round Mountain Gold Corporation is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kinross Gold Corporation. Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Work You'll Do

As a member of the site leadership team, the incumbent will provide strategic leadership and oversight for Health & Safety programs supporting both surface and underground mining operations. Under the direction of the Kinross Nevada H&S Manager and in partnership with the VP & Project Director, Phase X, Underground Mine Manager, and operational leaders, the Superintendent will integrate Health & Safety into business planning, operational execution, workforce development, and continuous improvement initiatives.

The Superintendent is responsible for developing and executing strategies that support safe, reliable, and productive operations while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, corporate standards, and industry best practices. The role will provide leadership for Health & Safety management systems, critical risk management, incident prevention and learning, emergency response preparedness, contractor management, occupational health programs, and regulatory compliance activities.

The incumbent will build and lead a high-performing team of Health & Safety professionals, foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement, and collaborate closely with site leadership, employees, business partners, and corporate stakeholders to improve risk management and organizational performance. All activities shall be conducted safely and in a manner consistent with Kinross Values and Safeground Principles.

Key Responsibilities

•  Develop and execute site Health & Safety strategies aligned with Kinross business objectives, Safeground Principles, and operational priorities.
•  Serve as a trusted advisor to site leadership regarding Health & Safety performance, critical risk management, regulatory compliance, and safety culture development.
•  Lead the integration of Health & Safety requirements into underground development projects, operational planning, engineering activities, and organizational change initiatives.
•  Provide strategic oversight of contractor and business partner Health & Safety performance, ensuring alignment with Kinross standards and critical risk management expectations.
•  Provide strategic oversight of emergency response preparedness, mine rescue capabilities, crisis management planning, and emergency response team development.
•  Ensure compliance with applicable MSHA regulations, corporate standards, and industry best practices.
•  Lead incident investigations, corrective action management processes, and continuous improvement initiatives.
•  Develop and monitor departmental budgets, staffing plans, business objectives, and performance metrics.
•  Analyze Health & Safety and operational performance metrics and provide recommendations to senior leadership.
•  Build, coach, mentor, and develop Health & Safety personnel while supporting succession planning and professional development.
•  Champion and model Kinross Values (Putting People First, High Performance Culture, Rigorous Financial Discipline and Corporate Social Responsibility) and Safeground Principles (People are the solution, Errors are normal, How we respond matters, Humility is a superpower, Learning over blame, Context drives behavior), fostering a culture where learning, engagement, respect, and continuous improvement drive decision-making and operational performance.
•  Coach leaders and employees in the practical application of Safeground Principles and learning-focused approaches to risk management and incident prevention.
•  Establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, contractors, regulators, community stakeholders, and corporate leadership.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Mining, Environmental Science, Business, or a related field. Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.

jobs.description:
Discover a rewarding career opportunity at Kinross in the stunning rural landscapes of Washington State.  Recognized for our leadership in low-impact mine development and nationally acclaimed for our reclamation and closure practices, our team has produced gold from six different deposits in the region since 1990.  Currently we are advancing a multi-year pipeline of projects and growing our team to ensure effective delivery and seamless transition into operations.

Job Summary

Under the direction of the Technical Services Manager, the Senior Geotechnical Engineer provides all underground geotechnical engineering activities for the Curlew mine to support safe, efficient, and productive mining operations. This role provides technical expertise for mine design, ground control, underground infrastructure, and operational planning while developing and maintaining geotechnical standards, programs, and best practices for the life of the mine. The Senior Geotechnical Engineer works closely with Operations, Technical Services, and contractors to identify and manage geotechnical risks, optimize mine performance, and ensure compliance with company standards and regulatory requirements. This position also provides technical leadership and mentorship while supporting the successful development, ramp-up, and long-term operation of the Curlew mine.

Essential Functions

Ground Control Management Planning:

Lead the design, implementation and continuous improvement of the Ground Control Management Plan (GCMP).

Ground Support Design:

Lead ground control planning and design for underground excavations, including selection and optimization of rock bolts, mesh, shotcrete, cable bolts, and other support systems suitable for complex ground conditions. Work with mining teams to ensure effective application.

QA/QC:

Lead Develop, implement and maintain the underground backfill and ground support QA/QC Program.

Stope Sequencing and Design:

Use numerical modeling (FLAC3D, Map3D or other) as appropriate along with other analytical methods to support stope design, backfill performance, pillar stability, and sequencing.

Instrumentation & Monitoring:

Implement and manage underground monitoring systems including all types of best practice underground mine instrumentation. Analyze data to track ground performance and inform mine planning.

Geotechnical Risk Management:

Identify ground control hazards, develop and maintain the mine’s Ground Control Trigger Action Response Plan (TARP) and work with all stakeholders to mitigate ground control hazards.

This position works approximately 30% of the time in the underground. Underground work includes field observations on foot, driving underground, engaging with and collecting information from employees in the field, and providing education to employees.

jobs.title: Ingeniero planificación Mina (CL)
jobs.description:
La mina La Coipa de Kinross está ubicada en la Región de Atacama en el norte de Chile, aproximadamente 1.000 kilómetros al norte de Santiago y 140 kilómetros al noreste de Copiapó. La Coipa vertió su primera barra de oro en marzo de 2022 después de reiniciar las operaciones luego de la suspensión en 2013. Kinross está llevando a cabo un programa de exploración para extender potencialmente la vida útil de la mina.

Kinross Chile ha construido relaciones sólidas con sus comunidades anfitrionas basadas en la confianza y el respeto a través del compromiso y la consulta. La operación se abastece con en un 100% con energías renovables no convencionales para satisfacer sus necesidades de energía.

Descripción del puesto

Responsable del proceso de planificación minera de corto y mediano plazo, traduciendo el plan minero presupuestado en secuencias ejecutables semanales, mensuales y anuales que la operación esté en condiciones de cumplir. El cargo responde por la integridad, la cadencia y la calidad del flujo de trabajo de planificación de corto y mediano plazo, y no por la elaboración del presupuesto, de acuerdo con las políticas, normas y procedimientos de MDO y Kinross.

Responsabilidades del puesto

• Desarrollar los planes mineros semanales, mensuales y anuales que den cumplimiento al plan minero presupuestado; el cargo ejecuta el presupuesto, no lo elabora.

• Generar y evaluar alternativas de extracción y estrategias de secuenciamiento que mejoren el desempeño operacional, la eficiencia en costos y la seguridad, dentro del marco del plan aprobado.

• Desarrollar el diseño de detalle del horizonte de corto y mediano plazo: definición de bancos y polígonos de extracción, diseño de rampas y accesos, y detalle operacional de fases y líneas de avance, en consistencia con los diseños de fases de largo plazo.

• Calcular los requerimientos de flota, las productividades y el movimiento de material del horizonte del plan, e identificar dónde la disponibilidad de equipos restringe el cumplimiento del plan.

• Proponer, asesorar y coordinar con otras áreas para que las operaciones mineras (perforación, tronadura, carguío, transporte, caminos y labores auxiliares) sean consistentes con el plan en los distintos horizontes de planificación.

• Entregar los antecedentes de plan y de secuenciamiento que requiera el equipo de geometalurgia, sin asumir la responsabilidad principal del análisis geometalúrgico. 

• Administrar y mantener el ciclo de planificación de corto y mediano plazo: cadencia, plazos, insumos requeridos de cada área y secuencia de entregas.

• Definir y mantener los estándares, convenciones y plantillas de planificación (nomenclatura, codificación, convenciones de sólidos y bloques, versionamiento y control de emisión), de modo que los planes sean trazables y reproducibles.

• Coordinar los insumos de los que depende el ciclo —Topografía, Geología y control de leyes, restricciones geotécnicas, retroalimentación de Operaciones y programas de perforación y tronadura— y escalar cuando dichos insumos lleguen fuera de plazo o incompletos.

• Mantener la documentación y la trazabilidad de los archivos de los planes emitidos, incluidos los archivos de diseño y las superficies sobre las cuales se construyó cada plan.

• Conducir las rutinas de revisión y entrega de plan con Operaciones, asegurando que el plan emitido sea comprendido en terreno.

• Identificar e impulsar oportunidades de mejora continua en el flujo de trabajo de planificación. 

• Mantener operativo y actualizado el hardware y software de planificación, incluido el entorno Deswik, sus licencias, versiones de módulos y configuración, en conjunto con el/la Ingeniero/a Planificación Mina Senior.

• Mantener, en conjunto, una base topográfica y de as-built confiable y actualizada de la mina, asegurando registros oportunos y exactos del avance minero.

• Apoyar la migración desde las plataformas heredadas hacia Deswik, incluyendo la reconstrucción de flujos de trabajo, el desarrollo de plantillas y la transferencia de conocimiento. 

Formación y experiencia

Ingeniero Civil Minas.

4 años o más en planificación minera, con experiencia demostrable en rajo abierto en horizontes de corto y/o mediano plazo.

• Construcción y secuenciamiento de planes mineros en horizontes semanal, mensual y anual.

• Detalle de fases, diseño de bancos, polígonos de extracción, rampas y accesos.

• Cálculo de requerimientos de flota y modelamiento de productividades para el horizonte del plan.

• Reconciliación plan versus real y análisis de desviaciones respecto del plan minero presupuestado.

• Conocimiento de costos suficiente para evaluar la factibilidad operacional de un plan. 

Deswik es la plataforma principal de planificación de este cargo. Se considera altamente deseable el dominio de Deswik.CAD, Deswik.LHS, Deswik.Sched y Deswik.OPSTS; las capacidades en Deswik.Sched y Deswik.LHS son centrales para la entrega diaria.

Licencia de conducir Clase B.

Kinross es una empresa minera de oro senior global con sede en Canadá con operaciones y proyectos en los Estados Unidos, Brasil, Mauritania, Chile y Canadá. Nuestro enfoque en la entrega de valor se basa en nuestros principios básicos de minería responsable, excelencia operativa, crecimiento disciplinado y solidez del balance. Kinross cotiza en la Bolsa de Valores de Toronto (símbolo: K) y en la Bolsa de Valores de Nueva York (símbolo: KGC).

jobs.title: Condition Monitoring Technician
jobs.description:
Steelmaking coal is an essential ingredient in blast-furnace steel manufacture, producing steel used for critical building and infrastructure around the world. In Australia, we operate five steelmaking coal mines in Queensland’s Bowen Basin, and have additional joint venture interests in steelmaking coal and manganese, as well as copper exploration projects underway in North West Queensland and Western Australia.

Anglo American Steelmaking Coal is seeking an experienced Condition Monitoring Technician to join the Engineering and Maintenance team at Moranbah North Mine. This hands on reliability role involves monitoring surface and underground mining equipment, identifying developing defects and recommending practical maintenance actions to improve equipment availability and reduce unplanned downtime.

Using vibration analysis, oil and fluid analysis, inspections and technical data, you will work with maintenance, planning, reliability, engineering and operational teams across longwall, development, coal clearance, workshops and fixed plant.

Key Responsibilities

Complete condition monitoring inspections and collect accurate equipment data.

Analyse vibration, oil and fluid results to identify developing equipment defects.

Assess equipment health and identify issues that may affect safety, reliability or production.

Provide practical advice on repairs and maintenance requirements.

Prepare clear condition monitoring reports for maintenance and operational teams.

Create or support SAP work notifications for identified defects.

Escalate critical equipment conditions and follow actions through to completion.

Work with maintenance, planning and reliability teams to prioritise repairs.

Support equipment failure investigations and root cause analysis.

Identify repeat failures and contribute to long-term defect elimination.

Maintain accurate equipment histories, monitoring records and asset health information.

Support improvements to monitoring routes, alarm limits, measurement frequencies and reporting processes.

Follow all site safety systems, standards, work instructions and statutory requirements.

About you

To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:

A mechanical trade, engineering qualification or another relevant technical qualification.

Previous experience in condition monitoring, predictive maintenance or equipment reliability.

Practical experience collecting and interpreting vibration analysis data.

Experience with oil or fluid analysis.

Experience working with underground mining equipment, fixed plant or heavy industrial assets.

Strong mechanical knowledge and equipment fault-finding skills.

The ability to turn technical findings into clear and practical maintenance recommendations.

Experience using SAP or a similar maintenance management system.

Strong attention to detail and accurate technical reporting skills.

A sound understanding of isolation, risk management and safe maintenance practices.

The ability to work effectively with tradespeople, planners, engineers and operational teams.

A current Australian driver’s licence.

The ability to meet site medical and fitness-for-work requirements.

Experience with thermography, ultrasound, online monitoring systems, predictive maintenance software or root cause analysis would be highly regarded.

Monday to Friday roster

jobs.title: Commercial & Scientific Analyst/Lead
jobs.description:
About the company

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear – even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models—alongside our novel sensors—to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. Since our founding in 2018, KoBold has become by far both the largest independent mineral exploration company and the largest exploration technology developer. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 60 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

We’re hiring a Commercial & Scientific Analyst/Lead to accelerate our mission.

About the position

In this role, you will report to a Lead or Manager within the Commercial Analytics team, and work closely within a remote team of 5 - 7 (across North America and Europe) to structure ambiguous problems, build financial and operational models, and provide recommendations to the C-suite for key decisions.

The work will span a variety of topics and include traditional market analyses such as creating supply/demand forecasts and writing commodity outlook reports, and non-traditional analyses as-needed to advance KoBold’s mission – e.g., operational and financial modeling for KoBold’s exploration programs, build vs. buy decisions for KoBold’s technology, mine economics modeling, and scientific communication materials for external audiences s, to name a few.

This is an ideal role for a recent graduate looking to acquire a wide range of skills very quickly. The learning curve will be steep, and the work will be varied and intellectually demanding.

Responsibilities

The Commercial & Scientific Analyst/Lead will:

Aggregate existing research and/or conduct original research to build forecasts and models related to commodity markets, KoBold operations, mine development, and more

Work with the Commercial Analytics and Financial Planning & Analysis team to answer strategic questions from leadership

Prepare materials for the Board of Directors and investors or partners

Use a first-principles approach in collaboration with various KoBold functions to help make decisions or improve operational efficiency (e.g., cost models for technology, HR, exploration programs, carbon emissions reporting, trade-off/sensitivity analyses)

Conduct analytics for critical workstreams in mine development and exploration

Build and maintain financial models assessing project economics

Support others on the Commercial Analytics team on various analytical assignments

Qualifications

A great candidate will have:

Education in a STEM discipline or economics (physics, chemistry, astronomy/astrophysics, or mathematics is preferred)

At least 1 year of experience in technology, natural resources, finance, or professional services

Experience with Python or other scientific computing language and/or financial modeling

Excitement about working on a wide array of problems

Excellent communication and organizational skills

Regardless of formal training, a strong orientation toward thinking from first principles with respect to science, technology, economics, and business

Work practices and motivation:

Demonstrated ability to quickly absorb and synthesize complex information, with a keen eye for detail and intellectual rigor

Exceptional curiosity and eagerness to learn, with a proactive approach to exploring new concepts and technologies

Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on a range of responsibilities

Ability to independently prioritize multiple tasks effectively

What to Expect

Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.

KoBold Metals is an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunities for people of any race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or veteran status.

This position is full-time, exempt.

The US base salary range for this full-time exempt position is $105,000 - $190,000 + 401K and equity.

Location: KoBold is a remote first workplace, we are open to candidates currently residing anywhere in the United States, Canada, or United Kingdom. All candidates must be authorized to legally work in either the United States, Canada, or United Kingdom.

jobs.title: Data Scientist - (Global)
jobs.description:
Data Scientist (Senior Staff, Staff, & Senior roles available)

About the company

KoBold Metals is a mineral exploration company using AI to explore for the metals we need for our transition to a low-carbon economy. KoBold’s business is discovering, defining, expanding, and developing mineral resources, and KoBold’s objective is to achieve a step-change improvement in exploration success: we aim to discover more tier 1 resources, faster, and with fewer failures.

KoBold has a global portfolio of more than 80 exploration properties targeting nickel, copper, cobalt, and lithium, which range from 100%-owned to partnerships with both majors, junior explorers, and prospectors.

Our team includes the best of the industry in exploration geoscience, data science, software engineering, operations, and business personnel. Prior to joining KoBold, KoBold team members have made nearly 20 discoveries. Our exploration programs are co-led by our geoscientists and data scientists, who develop exploration hypotheses, rigorously quantify uncertainty in our understanding of the subsurface, and design data collection programs that most effectively reduce uncertainty, drawing upon a large suite of proprietary exploration technology built by our data scientists and software engineers. Our field programs validate and improve the system and have demonstrated material improvements over conventional exploration methods

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

We are hiring a Data Scientists to help accelerate our mission.

About the position

In this role, you will build predictive models and apply a wide range of scientific computing, statistical, and physics-based methods to find places where there is evidence of ore-forming processes at work and to predict the locations of ore-grade mineralization in 2D and 3D. You will help build a worldwide dataset that underlies our exploration program, with careful attention to identifying and quantifying uncertainty in the data and in our predictions. You will create models and develop software to accelerate discovery of critical battery metals.

You will join an outstanding team of data scientists and engineers and will work closely with KoBold’s world-renowned geoscientists to incorporate our best understanding of the chemical and physical processes that create ore deposits. Working with your geoscience colleagues, you will create 2D and 3D geologic predictions, identify exploration targets, design field programs to collect data, and use that data to reduce the uncertainty in our predictions and guide the next phase of field work.

Ultimately, your role is to help KoBold make valuable discoveries by building data tools to solve scientific problems. As one of the early members of this team, you will help build these tools from the ground up.

Responsibilities

The Data Scientist will:

Help develop KoBold’s proprietary software exploration tools.

Find and curate geophysical, geochemical, geologic, and geographic data and integrate it into KoBold’s proprietary data system.

Build models to make statistically valid predictions about the locations of compositional anomalies within the Earth’s crust.

Create effective visualizations for evaluating model performance and enabling rapid interaction with the underlying data and key features.

Develop and apply data processing, statistical, and physics-based techniques to geoscientific data — from computer vision to geophysical inversions — and use the results to guide our targeting efforts and inform our acquisition and exploration decisions.

Present to and collaborate with our external partners and stakeholders.

Qualifications

A great Data Scientist candidate will have:

Technical skills, including extensive experience with:

Python’s data science packages and general software engineering practices.

Collaborative software development (git), and familiarity with software engineering best practices like unit test / integration test suites, and CICD pipelines.

Cloud computing resources.

Building predictive models, applying them to different problems, and evaluating and interpreting the results.

Data from a variety of physical systems.

Geospatial analyses and visualizations.

Technical knowledge:

Broad skills in and knowledge of applied statistics and Bayesian inference

Substantial understanding of machine learning algorithms

Training and work experience:

An advanced degree in the physical sciences, engineering, computer science, or mathematics.

A minimum work experience of 4 years post PhD or 8 years post MS, ideally as a data scientist or data engineer.

Experience leading technical teams to apply novel scientific approaches to core business problems

Work practices and motivation:

Ability to take ownership and responsibility of large projects.

Ability to explain technical problems to and collaborate on solutions with domain experts.

Communicates well on a collaborative, cross-functional team.

Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on a range of responsibilities.

Ability to independently prioritize multiple tasks effectively.

Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain.

Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights through using our tools in exploration and willing to work directly with geologists in the field.

Keen not just to build cool technology, but to figure out what technical product to build to best achieve the business objectives of the company.

Director of Mineral Processing

About the Company

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear – even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 60 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the Role

The Mineral Processing Lead will contribute to and lead the development and execution of mineral processing strategy across KoBold’s portfolio, with an initial focus on the Mingomba copper project in Zambia. Reporting to the CTO, this role is responsible for all aspects of process engineering from early-stage metallurgical testwork through feasibility study design and operational readiness. You will define the flowsheet, drive geometallurgical characterization, evaluate processing routes (concentration, hydrometallurgy, smelting), and ensure that mineral processing considerations are integrated into mine planning and economic modeling from the earliest stages.

Responsibilities

Process Engineering & Flowsheet Development

Own the process flowsheet design for Mingomba and future KoBold projects, from scoping through feasibility.

Work hands on and with your team to define and manage metallurgical testwork programs: comminution characterization, flotation optimization, hydrometallurgical evaluation, and pilot-scale campaigns.

Evaluate and recommend processing routes including froth flotation to concentrate, SX-EW, pressure oxidation, and smelter/refinery toll arrangements. Quantify the economic trade-offs of each.

Develop process design criteria, mass and water balances, and equipment specifications for feasibility-level engineering.

Lead the assessment of tailings characteristics, reprocessing potential, and environmental implications of process residues.

Geometallurgy & Integration

Build and maintain a geometallurgical framework that links ore variability (mineralogy, texture, grade distribution) to processing performance with first principles and statistical models.

Collaborate with geologists and data scientists to integrate geometallurgical statistics into resource models, mine schedules, and economic analyses.

Define sampling protocols for metallurgical characterization of drill core and ensure adequate coverage of ore variability.

Ensure mineral processing assumptions are reflected in techno-economic models including TC/RC structures, payable metal calculations, and concentrate penalty elements.

Technical Leadership & Team Building

Build, lead, and mentor a mineral processing function within KoBold’s Advanced Technology Group.

Direct and manage relationships with metallurgical consultants, contract laboratories, and engineering firms.

Serve as one of KoBold’s internal experts and external representatives on mineral processing for investor presentations, partner discussions, and technical reviews.

Contribute to feasibility study management and preparation of technical reports (NI 43-101 / JORC-compliant as applicable).

Identify and evaluate emerging processing technologies relevant to KoBold’s target commodities (copper, lithium, nickel, cobalt) along with the existing team.

Cross-functional Collaboration

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models—alongside our novel sensors—to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

This role is a key ingredient to this strategy. As an early Engineering Manager on the Data Systems Engineering team, you will have the opportunity to shape how we build our product and organization to realize this vision. Through development of our robust data systems, we will empower KoBold to unlock invaluable insights and streamline intricate scientific processes. Collaborating with our exceptional team of data scientists and geologists, you will have the opportunity to tackle complex scientific problems head-on and collectively pave the way for the discoveries of vital energy transition metals like lithium, copper, nickel, and cobalt.
