About the company:

In the coming decades, our world needs substantially more critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt, to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. The mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago, because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.

KoBold is a leading scientific mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to make discoveries faster—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. We made our first discovery—Mingomba, one of the world’s largest undeveloped high-grade copper deposits—after spending materially less than the industry average. This asset is expected to operate for decades, and be a leading global copper supplier. KoBold is actively running exploration programs in 8 countries worldwide, all with the potential for another high-quality discovery.

We are developing Mingomba by applying the same technical rigor to resource development and mine planning as we do to exploration. Mingomba is also a scientific laboratory where we prototype new technology and workflows, combined with the expertise of veteran engineers. Our multidisciplinary team consists of mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. We want to develop world-class mining projects that are safer and have more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the role

This is a senior Engineering leadership role for the development of a significant Copper mining complex in Zambia. The Mingomba deposit contains over 10 million tonnes of copper more than half of which exceeds 6% grade. This role will help turn that world class deposit into a world class mine.

The Senior Engineering & Integration Manager is the primary technical authority for the Mingomba copper project through its design and construction phase. Reporting to the Project Director, this role carries end-to-end accountability for the quality, integrity, and integration of all engineering across the owner's team, the EPCM and specialist contractors. The role is the technical decision-maker and design authority for the project, responsible for safeguarding Kobold’s interests through stage gates, design reviews, and construction handover to operations. The Senior Engineering & Integration Manager sets the direction for engineering delivery, resolves complex cross-discipline technical issues, and directly influences how the Mingomba project is designed and built.

What this role is accountable for delivering

This role exists to ensure against common failure modes on major capital projects, with particular emphasis on scope creep driven by unresolved technical decisions, design quality that does not survive construction, and an owner's team that cannot effectively challenge or govern its engineering service providers.

The successful candidate will be judged on:

Engineering delivered on time, within sanction cost, and to the standard required for safe, operable, and maintainable facilities.

A design that has been constructability-reviewed, value-engineered, and operability-tested before it is frozen.

An EPCM that is technically directed, not just administered, with KoBold holding design authority.

A project that passes independent technical assurance reviews and stage-gate approvals without material qualification.

A technical risk register that is live, owned, and actively driven down.

Key responsibilities

Technical authority and design governance

Hold and exercise design authority on behalf of KoBold. Making and recording binding technical decisions across all disciplines, with a clear escalation path to the Project Director for issues that affect schedule, cost, or safety.

Establish the basis of design, engineering standards, and design criteria for the project, and enforce them with both the owner's team and the EPCM.

Own the technical risk register: identify, quantify, and drive the resolution of engineering risks before they become scope changes or construction rework.

Approve key engineering deliverables including P&IDs, design criteria, equipment datasheets, and technical specifications.

Direct the scope freeze process: define what decisions must be made to freeze design at each stage, own the timeline for those decisions, and prevent scope growth after sanction.

EPCM direction and performance management

Act as KoBolds senior technical interface to the EPCM as an active director of engineering scope, priorities, and performance.

Monitor engineering service provider progress against the engineering management plan using earned value metrics and escalate deviations in quality, schedule, or cost before they compound.

Direct EPCM and specialist contractor technical performance by challenging design solutions, enforcing design and lifecycle cost requirements, and proactively mitigating interface risks to ensure scope alignment.

Constructability, operability, and value engineering

Lead formal constructability reviews at FEL 2 and FEL 3, ensuring construction knowledge is embedded in the design before it is frozen.

Drive operability and maintainability reviews with the operations and maintenance readiness team at each design milestone, ensuring the facility can be safely operated and maintained as designed.

Generar condiciones sociales para la viabilidad y continuidad de nuestras operaciones, aprobación de permisos, contribuyendo con los resultados esperados en la Unidad Minera y en el desarrollo de sus proyectos.

Areas internas y externas de la UM.

Key Responsibilities

Support the Project Superintendent and Field Supervisors in delivering earthworks and field-based scopes safely and efficiently.

Assist with the installation, maintenance and monitoring of water supply and water monitoring assets.

Support the delivery of Approvals and Studies activities across Heritage, Environment, Surface Water, Hydrogeology and Engineering.

Assist with field activities, stakeholder coordination and contractor support.

Ensure work is completed safely, compliantly and in accordance with Fortescue requirements, approvals and study conditions.

Collect, record and maintain accurate field data and documentation.

Work collaboratively with study managers, project teams, geologists, scope owners, consultants and drilling contractors.

Build respectful and effective working relationships with Traditional Custodians and Indigenous team members.

Share knowledge, mentor technicians and identify opportunities to improve safety, reliability and efficiency.

Qualifications and Experience

Proven Pilbara fieldwork experience, including remote and helicopter-supported operations.

Strong commitment to safety, practical problem-solving and mechanical aptitude.

Experience working respectfully with Traditional Custodians, Indigenous team members, contractors and consultants.

Competence using Microsoft Office, acQuire, ArcGIS, Trimble and GPS systems.

Knowledge of Fortescue’s Land Use Certificate and Heritage Compliance processes.

Current WA Class C manual driver’s licence, 4WD and Senior First Aid certificates.

Highly regarded:
HR licence, rigging and dogging, crane operations, Remote Pilot Licence, earthmoving tickets, and experience in drilling, exploration, environmental, heritage, hydrogeological or engineering fieldwork.

jobs.title: Sourcing Specialist
jobs.description:
The Power of Now

Be part of something big. Fortescue is leading the world with our plan to decarbonise our iron ore operations, projects that harness renewable energy and the development of technology that will change our planet forever.

An opportunity has arisen for a Sourcing Specialist to join the Contracts & Procurement department.

About the role

To manage all contracting and procurement activities to support the efficient delivery of the Catapult Formula E programme. The role must ensure all goods, services and works are procured in a cost-effective, transparent and compliant manner, while aligning with group, legal and industry standards. 

What you will do

C&P Planning & Execution

To manage and update catapult Formula E specific CSR/PSR, sourcing register and/or PO log (as appropriate) that align with the programme schedule and budget requirements.

Implement sourcing strategies for catapult Formula E categories and minimise supplier complexity and quantity where possible to enable the develop of supplier relationships and supplier management through key performance indicators.

Contract Management

Execution of all planned purchase orders for the catapult Formula E programme.

Deliver RFQ, sourcing and DFX to the catapult Formula E programme.

Responsible for Supplier identification, prequalification and shortlisting.

Implement NDA’s and T’s and C’s with suppliers

Prepare supplier performance data and working with supplier quality assurance team to ensure effective supplier development plans are in place and executed.

Foster strategic supplier relationships to ensure continuous supply, innovation and cost optimization.

Lead the resolution of supplier quality concerns when non-conforming product is identified, ensuring root cause analysis is carried out and robust corrective action implemented

Carry out commercial negotiations covering terms and conditions, etc.

Evaluate and recommend supplier awards based on total cost of ownership and strategic value.

Support the reporting of contracts and procurement status to senior management

Develop supplier performance measures in conjunction with supplier quality assurance and logistics.

Identify and evaluate key risks at prior to award and seek input from other functions as appropriate (e.g. engineering, legal, quality etc.)

Preparation of Contract Award Recommendations and onboarding suppliers to ensure efficient award.

Contract administration to support execution, including correspondence and contract notices and claims assessment.

Responsible for resolving any invoices queries arising from Contracts & PO’s

Cost Initiatives

Identify and activity promote cost reductions associated with the delivery of catapult Formula E to meet financial goals and report versus target monthly.

Support for  Business Development with estimates and costings for new programme proposals, where feasible.

Team Management

Provide engaging leadership and mentorship of the team, ensuring the team is motivated, driven and clearly directed.

Support, lead, guide and train C&P team members regardless of Programme.

Promote effective communication between C&P team and other departments ensuring alignment on programme goals and timelines.

Ensure the teams C&P activities are in accordance with established Contracts and Procurement policies and procedures and continually focus on improving process and procedure, where possible.

Collaboration & Stakeholder Relationships

Build and develop interdepartmental relationships within Fortescue to provide overall business improvement

Actively facilitate the coordination and communications between different departments, team members and stakeholders to ensure effective alignment.

Management Reporting

Management Reporting on Programme/Category performance to ensure that the C&P activities are happening on a proactive basis assisting with delivering programmes in tight time frames.

Reporting on key KPI’s, and performance metrics to ensure the company is meeting its financial goals

Systems & Processes

Drive the development, uptake and usage of key processes and systems, (such as ERP for all C&P and planning activity), ensure that the C&P teams are leveraging the tools and processes are being followed.

Execution of all PPO’s and digital requisitions for motorsports.

Maintain MRP Purchasing master data for products and within BoM management tools

Maintain parts delivery status

Maintain and update C&P records and generate reports on C&P activity to meet organisation compliance and provide access to C&P information.

About you

5+ years’ experience in direct procurement, technical buying, expediting and purchasing functions in a motorsport or related industry sector

Proven track record of C&P success, preferably in motorsports or across a similar industry sector

Proven ability to learn and adopt new ways of working

Team player with the ability to work independently and under minimal supervision.

Solid knowledge of contract law associated with services and commercial agreements, C&P principles and negotiation techniques.

Solid pre contract experience and commercial / contract terms negotiation skills

Technical and / or commercial education to a minimum of degree level, membership of CIPS would be advantageous.

Ability to work in a fast-paced environment across multiple packages, and drive the work to ensure successful outcomes

Travel to international locations maybe required.

Ability to bring a flexible, problem-solving mindset, challenging traditional thinking and be prepared to work outside of comfort zone.

Strong data driven and visual reporting skills, ensuring quantified status and risk is communicated.

High level experience and knowledge in the use of MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint.

Excellent prioritising, organisation, interpersonal, communication and analytical skills

What is in it for you?

Our UK benefits include:

Bonus scheme

Aviva Pension

Group Life Assurance

Group Income Prote

jobs.title: EOI: Project Geologist - Morocco Exploration
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location:
Morocco

Roster:
 Monday to Friday

Employment Engagement:
Local engagement preferred, however welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates outside of Morocco

We have an exciting opportunity to join the Fortescue Morocco Exploration team as Project Geologist.

Fortescue is undertaking a large-scale regional exploration program across Morocco focused on copper, gold, iron ore and other critical minerals.

This role offers the opportunity to work alongside experienced exploration professionals on frontier exploration projects with genuine district-scale discovery potential.

You will be accountable for supporting project generation, regional geological assessments and field exploration programs while contributing to the evaluation and advancement of new mineral discoveries.

Reporting to the Senior Geologist, you will work closely with multidisciplinary technical teams to generate exploration targets and progress projects from early-stage assessment through to drill testing.

Key Responsibilities

•    Compiling, validating and interpreting geological datasets. 
•    Undertaking regional geological reviews and project generation studies. 
•    Generating and prioritising exploration targets using geological, geochemical and geophysical datasets. 
•    Completing geological mapping, sampling and field investigations. 
•    Supervising drilling contractors and undertaking geological logging. 
•    Supporting the planning and execution of exploration programs. 
•    Preparing technical reports, presentations and exploration recommendations. 
•    Working collaboratively with multidisciplinary technical teams to solve geological challenges. 
•    Promoting safe and environmentally responsible exploration practices. 

Qualifications and Experience

•    Degree in Geology or a related Earth Science discipline. 
•    Approximately 5 - 7 years' exploration experience. 
•    Experience in greenfields mineral exploration will be highly regarded. 
•    Strong geological mapping, logging and data interpretation skills. 
•    Ability to integrate geological, geochemical and geophysical datasets to support exploration decisions. 
•    Strong technical writing, communication and teamwork skills. 
•    Experience working in international exploration environments will be highly regarded. 
•    Experience using ArcGIS, Leapfrog, ioGas and geological database software will be advantageous. 
•    Fluent French is required for this role. 
•    English language proficiency will be highly regarded. 
•    Current valid driver's licence.

About Woodside Energy

We know great results come from our people feeling valued, getting the support they need to reach their full potential and working in a positive work environment. We recognise that enduring, meaningful relationships with communities are fundamental to maintaining our licence to operate.

Technology and innovation are essential to our long-term sustainability. We are growing our carbon and new energy businesses using technology to reduce emissions and the carbon footprint of our products. We are working to improve energy efficiency, offset emissions, reduce emissions intensity and explore options for lower-carbon energy. Woodside led the development of the LNG industry in Australia and is applying this same pioneering spirit to solving future energy challenges globally.

Refer to our corporate website for more information about our different locations and projects: 
https://www.woodside.com/what-we-do

About the Program

The Environmental Summer Internship Program is part of Woodside’s USA Early Career Pathways initiative and sits within Woodside’s broader Health, Safety & Environment organization. The program is designed to build a sustainable pipeline of future environmental and HSE talent.

The program provides undergraduate students with hands-on, real-world experience supporting environmental stewardship and regulatory priorities across Woodside’s U.S. business. Depending on business needs and academic background, projects may include environmental compliance, emissions and sustainability initiatives, environmental data and reporting, permitting, waste management, water management, biodiversity, regulatory research, environmental risk assessment, and operational environmental performance.

Interns will work alongside experienced HSE and Environmental professionals while gaining exposure to Woodside’s operating environment, environmental management systems, regulatory obligations, safety culture, and commitment to responsible operations.

The internship serves as a primary feeder into Woodside’s future graduate and early-career programs and supports Woodside’s broader workforce and capability planning strategy in the United States.

Qualifications

Pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Sustainability, Environmental Health, or a related field

Rising junior or senior with an expected graduation date of Spring 2028 through Spring 2029 

Enrolled in an accredited college or university for the full duration of the 2027 internship 

Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.30 

Available for a minimum of twelve (12) consecutive weeks during Summer 2027 

Authorized to work in the United States and must not require current or future sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., F-1) 

Agree to complete pre-employment screening and understand that correspondence will primarily be conducted via email 

Agree not to utilize AI or AI-assisted tools during any part of the application or interview process

Recognition and Reward

What you can expect from us:

Commitment to your ongoing development, including on-the-job opportunities, formal programs and coaching

Values led culture with a focus on creating a psychologically and physically safe work environment

Active employee-led working groups driving initiatives to build an inclusive culture.

A competitive remuneration package featuring performance-based incentives

jobs.description:
About Woodside Energy

We know great results come from our people feeling valued, getting the support they need to reach their full potential and working in a positive work environment. We recognise that enduring, meaningful relationships with communities are fundamental to maintaining our licence to operate.

Technology and innovation are essential to our long-term sustainability. We are growing our carbon and new energy businesses using technology to reduce emissions and the carbon footprint of our products. We are working to improving energy efficiency, offset emissions, reduce emissions intensity and explore options for lower-carbon energy. Woodside led the development of the LNG industry in Australia and is applying this same pioneering spirit to solving future energy challenges globally.

Refer to our corporate website for more information about our different locations and projects: 
https://www.woodside.com/what-we-do

About the Role:

To aspire to be a trusted business partner that anticipates Trion operational needs and delivers seamless supply chain outcomes through exceptional people, processes, and systems. In accordance with business processes outlined in the Woodside Management System (WMS), the Inventory Adviser is responsible for the operation spares materials being ordered, tracked, stored and supplied as per the country strategy. The Inventory Adviser manages the life cycle of the company owned property and rentals for the Project allowing them to carry out their planned and unplanned activities. The position requires liaising with internal and external stakeholders to ensure material requirements are met while ensuring safe, efficient and on-time execution.   

Duties & Responsibilities:

Core Responsibilities:  

Serve as local WIL focal point for respective campaign (Materials Management)  
with customers to ensure requirements can be met within agreed KPI’s  

 Communicate logistics strategic plan to internal & external stakeholders  

 Coordinate material movements in accordance with project requirement timelines   

 Manage project inventory, executing enterprise transactions and consumption   

 Manage actual & potential issues impacting timely equipment delivery   

 Daily activities completed in line with project and company requirements

jobs.title: Production Maintenance Technician
jobs.description:
About Woodside

We know great results come from our people feeling valued, getting the support they need to reach their full potential as well as bring their whole self to work. We also recognise that enduring, meaningful relationships with communities are fundamental to maintaining our licence to operate.

Technology and innovation are essential to our long-term sustainability. We are growing our carbon and new energy businesses using technology to reduce emissions and the carbon footprint of our products. We are working to improving energy efficiency, offset emissions, reduce emissions intensity and explore options for lower-carbon energy. Woodside led the development of the LNG industry in Australia and is applying this same pioneering spirit to solving future energy challenges.

Our global headquarters are based in Perth and our state-of-the-art campus reflects the quality of life Perth is known for - with a six Green Star rating, advanced wellness features and flexibility in how you work.

About the Role

The Ngujima Yin FPSO is the offshore production facility for the Vincent oil field and Greater Enfield development, receiving multiphase fluids from subsea wells and processing, storing and offloading stabilised crude oil for export.

A Production Maintenance Technician (PMT – Operations) on the Ngujima‑Yin FPSO is a multi‑skilled technician responsible for the safe operation, monitoring, and first‑line maintenance of the offshore production facility. Reporting to the Production Superintendent. The applicant will work a FIFO roster (3 wks on- 4 wks off - 3 wks on – 5 wks off) mobilising from point of hire Perth.

Duties and Responsibilities

•    Safely operate and monitor production plant and utilities in accordance with approved procedures and operating limits
•    Maintain stable production by responding to process upsets, alarms, and deviations
•    Conduct field operations and plant walk‑downs to verify equipment condition and identify hazards
•    Execute routine operational tasks including valve operations, sampling, line‑ups, start‑ups, and shutdowns
•    Work within the Integrated Safe System of Work (ISSOW), including permits, isolations and SSICs, 
•    Support maintenance activities through equipment preparation, isolation, testing, and reinstatement
•    Accurately complete shift logs, handovers, and production reporting
•    Participate as a member of the Emergency Response Team, providing initial response during incidents
•    Communicate effectively with the control room, maintenance teams, and supervisors to support safe, reliable operations

Skills and Experience

•    PMA Cert III or IV or relevant knowledge and skill in Oil & Gas Production
•    Previous Operations or Maintenance experience
•    Familiarity with Woodside operational systems and processes including SAP, ISSoW, ESP and others
•    Embrace Woodsides’ values and support team diversity and inclusivity
•    Personal responsibility regarding fitness for work, Process Safety and Health, Safety & Environment
•    Informal leader of peers, apprentices and trainees

Recognition and Reward

What you can expect from us:

Commitment to your ongoing development, including on-the-job opportunities, formal programs and coaching

Industry-leading 18 weeks paid parental leave for primary carer, and maintenance of superannuation or retirement benefits at the current rate during any period of unpaid parental leave for up to 24 months (plus secondary carer leave entitlements)

Values led culture with a focus on creating a psychologically and physically safe work environment

Active employee-led working groups driving initiatives to build an inclusive culture

Community volunteering opportunities

Relocation assistance (if required)

A competitive remuneration package featuring performance-based incentives

Woodside is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workforce culture, which is supported by our Values. Our aim is to attract, develop and retain a truly diverse and high-performing workforce. 

Diversity encompasses various differences, including but not limited to differences in age, nationality, race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, sex, sexual orientation, intersex status, gender identity or expression, relationship status, disability, neurodiversity, veteran status, cultural background, thinking styles, experience, family background, including caregiving commitments, and education. Inclusion centres on all employees creating a climate of respect, trust and belonging, where people feel enabled to be their best and authentic version of themself.

We offer supportive pathways for all employees to grow and develop leadership skills. We encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples and those seeking a more flexible working environment, including part-time opportunities.

jobs.description:
Job Introduction

Regional Lead based in APAC, managing a technical team of mining engineers and geologists tasked with identifying, developing, optimising and maintaining Graymont's mineral resources in the region.

Australia - NSW - North Sydney

Regional Manager, Mineral Resources Development (APAC)

Position Purpose

The Regional Manager, Mineral Resources Development (APAC) leads Graymont's regional Mining and Geology function, providing strategic and technical leadership to a team of mining engineers and geologists responsible for the identification, evaluation, development, optimisation, and stewardship of the Company's mineral resources.

The role partners closely with Operations, Commercial, Environment, Projects and Executive Leadership to ensure Graymont maintains a sustainable, long-term mineral resource portfolio while supporting operational excellence, regulatory compliance, rehabilitation, decarbonisation and continuous improvement initiatives across the APAC region.

Key Responsibilities

Health, Safety & Leadership

Champion Graymont's Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) policies, procedures and standards, promoting a strong safety culture across the Mineral Resources Development (MRD) team.

Demonstrate visible safety leadership by embedding HSE expectations into daily operations and decision-making.

Ensure HSE objectives form part of annual performance planning and reviews for all direct reports.

Lead in accordance with Graymont's Values and contribute to strengthening the One Graymont culture.

Foster a collaborative, accountable and high-performing team environment through coaching, mentoring and professional development.

Functional Leadership

Lead the regional Mining and Geology teams to provide high-quality technical support to operational sites across APAC.

Align geological and mining engineering activities with regional business priorities and operational requirements.

Ensure consistency with global MRD standards, systems and best practices while sharing knowledge and lessons learned across regions.

Develop team capability through succession planning, technical training and career development initiatives.

Build effective relationships with Operations, Environment, Finance, Projects, external consultants, contractors, government agencies and industry stakeholders.

Promote effective communication across functions to ensure timely delivery of business objectives.

Mineral Resources Management

Develop and execute strategies that maintain a minimum 30-year Mineral Reserve life across Graymont's quarry operations.

Lead exploration, resource evaluation and reserve definition programs, including greenfield and brownfield exploration opportunities.

Oversee geological modelling, resource estimation and reserve reporting in accordance with company standards.

Lead technical due diligence activities for acquisitions, divestments and strategic growth opportunities.

Ensure timely, accurate and reliable geological and mining information is available to support operational and strategic decision-making

Mine Planning & Technical Services

Oversee the development and delivery of annual and five-year mine plans that optimise resource extraction while meeting operational and statutory requirements.

Provide technical leadership in mine design, sequencing, grade control and resource optimisation.

Support operational sites through geological interpretation, mine planning advice and technical problem solving.

Ensure mine planning activities align with long-term business objectives and sustainable resource management principles.

Budget & Capital Planning

Develop, monitor and manage operating and capital budgets relating to Exploration Resource development, Drilling campaigns, Mine planning, Stripping programs

Provide recommendations and business cases for capital investment and resource development activities.

Environmental Stewardship & Sustainability

Support progressive rehabilitation, mine closure planning and environmental management initiatives across operational sites.

Prepare annual rehabilitation liability estimates and disturbance reporting in accordance with company requirements.

Support Graymont's sustainability and decarbonisation strategies through responsible resource planning and operational improvements.

Continuous Improvement

Drive continuous improvement through innovation, technology adoption and optimisation of mining and geological processes.

Ensure geological databases, mine planning systems and technical documentation are effectively maintained and secured.

Lead or contribute to regional and global strategic projects as required.

Ensure accurate, professional and timely reporting of departmental activities and performance metrics.

People Leadership

Lead, coach and develop a geographically dispersed team of mining engineers and geologists.

Set clear objectives, monitor performance and provide regular feedback.

Foster collaboration, accountability and continuous learning.

Build capability and succession within the regional technical team.

Qualifications

Essential

Bachelor's Degree in Mining Engineering, Geology or a related discipline.

Minimum 15 years' experience in mining engineering or geology within an operational mining environment.

Demonstrated leadership experience managing multidisciplinary technical teams.

Extensive experience in mineral resource evaluation, Reserve estimation, Mine planning

Exploration and resource development

Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across multiple organisational levels

Current driver's license

Valid passport with the ability to undertake international travel.

Desirable

Postgraduate qualifications in Mining Engineering, Geology or Business.

Experience working across multiple countries or regions.

Experience within industrial minerals, limestone or quarrying operations.

Knowledge of relevant mining legislation across the APAC region.

jobs.title: Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
WHAT DOES AGNICO EAGLE VALUE?

At Agnico Eagle, our values never waver. We believe in trust, respect, equity, family and responsibility. Why? Because they express who we are, and they have helped us succeed in business for over 60 years. We value
you
- your unique set of skills and experience. We value your willingness to build those skills and make a meaningful contribution to our company. And, we value your commitment to treat every person on our team with respect, helping us to operate safely, protect the environment and make a positive contribution to our local communities.

ABOUT OUR OPERATION

Canadian-based and led, Agnico Eagle is Canada's largest mining company and the second largest gold producer in the world. It produces precious metals from operations in Canada, Australia, Finland and Mexico and has a pipeline of high-quality exploration and development projects. Agnico Eagle is a partner of choice within the mining industry, recognized globally for its leading sustainability practices. Agnico Eagle was founded in 1957 and has consistently created value for its shareholders, declaring a cash dividend every year since 1983.

Agnico Eagle Mines' Detour Lake Mine is situated on the traditional homelands of the Apitipi Anicinapek Nation, Moose Cree First Nation, and Taykwa Tagamou Nation. In honoring our relationships with and commitments to our Partner Nations, Agnico Eagle prioritizes the hiring of members from these Nations. Additionally, Agnico Eagle has entered into an agreement with the Métis Nation of Ontario, and therefore, we also prioritize citizens of the Métis Nation of Ontario. To support this commitment, members from these Nations seeking employment opportunities at the Detour Lake Mine are encouraged to self-identify during the job application process. This ensures that we can consider your application appropriately in line with our dedication to supporting our Partner Nations.

Want to learn more about Detour Lake Mine?
Click here
!

In compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, Agnico Eagle Mining (AEM) is committed to providing accommodation for people with disabilities. Accommodation is available, upon request, for candidates participating in the recruitment process.

YOUR NEXT CHALLENGE:

Reporting to the Planning & Reliability Supervisor you will be part of the Mobile Maintenance Department. You will ensure that the goals and objectives are achieved while promoting and respecting Agnico Eagle’s values, Health & Safety Code of Conduct and the environment.

Oversee condition monitoring activities related to all Mine Maintenance equipment;

Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to equipment reliability, uptime, and maintenance effectiveness;

Review equipment performance and elaborate action plans with suppliers to achieve production goals;

Prepare regular reports and presentations on reliability performance, highlighting areas for improvement and recommendations for action;

Conducts an analysis of reliability problems and investigates to determine the required reliability approach for failures;

Recommend purchase of mechanical equipment/parts, tools and the modification of mechanical equipment; and procedures, as appropriate, consistent with our commitment to continuous improvement;

Provide analysis and interpretation of maintenance trends and variances;

Analise / interpret oil analysis results and take the required actions;

Development and implementation of a reliability program which maximizes profit / production by minimizing equipment downtime;

Implement preventative, predictive maintenance procedures and improve designs and/or installation criteria to minimize overall cost by reducing failures and maintenance manpower requirements;

jobs.title: Electrical Lead Commissioning
jobs.description:
Our client is seeking an experienced Electrical Lead to plan, coordinate, and execute electrical pre-commissioning and commissioning activities for a major Tailings Storage Facility project in Bagdad, Arizona. Reporting to the Commissioning Manager, this position will lead the safe and timely testing, energization, startup, and handover of critical electrical systems.

The role covers medium- and low-voltage systems, substations, switchgear, transformers, motor control centers, power-distribution networks, backup power, and electrical protection systems. The successful candidate will combine strong field leadership with hands-on technical expertise and disciplined control of safety, schedule, quality, and commissioning documentation.

Key Responsibilities

Commissioning Planning and Readiness

* Ensure contractors follow approved electrical commissioning procedures, inspection and test plans, method statements, and test protocols.
* Review single-line diagrams, schematics, wiring diagrams, cable schedules, load lists, and related technical documentation.* Develop commissioning schedules, manpower plans, test-equipment requirements, switching procedures, and isolation plans.
* Lead system walkdowns and readiness reviews, verify mechanical completion, and ensure inspection test records and punch-list items are closed before energization.* Manage the orderly handover of electrical systems from construction to commissioning and ultimately to operations.

Electrical Testing and Energization

* Lead commissioning of MV and LV switchgear, power and distribution transformers, motor control centers, UPS systems, battery banks, diesel generators, and backup power systems.
* Supervise installation verification, pre-energization inspections, controlled energization, load testing, and system stabilization.* Verify correct phasing, grounding, interlocks, control circuits, protection settings, and equipment functionality.
* Oversee insulation-resistance, continuity, cable, VLF, Hi-Pot, relay-protection, and other required electrical testing.* Lead switching and energization activities safely and in accordance with approved plans and permits.

Protection, Controls, and Startup

* Validate overcurrent, differential, distance, motor-protection, relay-logic, and trip-circuit schemes.
* Coordinate with the instrumentation and controls team on SCADA and DCS integration.* Support plant startup, load testing, ramp-up, and early operations while maintaining system reliability.
* Troubleshoot electrical faults, equipment malfunctions, and commissioning issues to support timely resolution.

Safety, Documentation, and Coordination

* Enforce client HSE requirements, permit-to-work controls, LOTOTO procedures, and safe execution of high-risk energization, high-voltage testing, and switching activities.
* Lead toolbox talks, risk assessments, and pre-task planning while promoting a strong field safety culture.* Ensure accurate completion of test reports, commissioning records, energization permits, switching logs, and relay-settings documentation.
* Verify red-line drawings and as-built documentation and ensure work complies with applicable IEC, IEEE, NFPA, project, and site standards.* Coordinate daily activities with mechanical, I&C, process commissioning, construction, QA/QC, vendors, OEM specialists, client representatives, and operations teams.
* Participate in progress meetings and provide clear reporting on system status, schedule, risks, constraints, and required actions.

Leadership Responsibilities

* Lead, supervise, and provide technical direction to electrical commissioning technicians and contractors.
* Allocate work, monitor progress against the commissioning schedule, and address performance or resource constraints.* Drive accountability, safe execution, quality, and timely completion across the electrical commissioning team.
* Make sound decisions during critical testing, switching, energization, and startup phases.

jobs.title: Head of ESG
jobs.description:
Globe 24-7, in partnership with a leading copper and cobalt mining company, is recruiting a Head of ESG for an expatriate leadership opportunity in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

This senior appointment will lead the development and delivery of the Company s ESG strategy across its operations, with particular responsibility for international ESG standards, lender requirements, environmental and social action plans, and ESG assurance. The successful candidate will play a critical role in strengthening the Company s ESG capability as the business enters its next phase of growth and investment, working closely with executive leadership, the Board, international lenders and external stakeholders.

The Role

The Head of ESG will lead the Company s alignment with international ESG standards, with particular focus on the IFC Performance Standards, while owning the development and delivery of the ESG roadmap across its operations.
The role will lead ESG engagement with lenders, technical advisors, independent monitors and external E&S stakeholders, translating lender requirements and independent gap assessments into practical, costed and time-bound implementation plans.
A key priority will be building the internal ESG capability required to deliver the Company s long-term objectives, while developing and managing a strong network of specialist environmental and social consultants.
The Head of ESG will work closely with the existing CSR and External Relations function, alongside HSE, HR, Procurement, Legal and Finance, to ensure effective ESG implementation and assurance across the business.
This is an expatriate opportunity in the DRC, supporting operations across Lubumbashi and Kolwezi.

The Responsibilities

Develop and drive the Company s long-term ESG strategy across its operations.

Own the IFC Performance Standards PS1-PS8 compliance roadmap and ensure effective implementation across operating sites.

Lead and manage the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP), including implementation priorities, budgets, milestones, evidence requirements and close-out.

Lead ESG engagement with international lenders, lender ESG teams, technical advisors and independent engineers.

Manage lender reviews, site visits, reporting, ESAP verification and independent monitoring.

Translate lender requirements, independent assessments and identified ESG gaps into practical internal action plans.

Build, develop and lead the Company s internal ESG capability, including the recruitment and development of specialist ESG professionals.

Scope, appoint and manage specialist environmental and social consultants across key ESG workstreams.

Serve as the Company s subject matter expert on IFC Performance Standards, Equator Principles, OECD Due Diligence Guidance and the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights.

Lead the preparation, submission and regulatory approval of ESIAs, ESHIAs and associated environmental and social management plans.

Develop and implement ESG policies, procedures and management systems aligned with international standards.

Provide regular ESG reporting to executive leadership and the Board.

Partner with CSR, HSE, HR, Procurement, Legal and Finance to ensure effective ESG implementation across the organisation.

Establish and lead ESG assurance programmes, including internal audits, contractor audits and independent verification.

Support ESG requirements associated with future project finance, refinancing, offtake, equity and other strategic transactions.

Develop internal ESG capability and reduce reliance on external consultants over time.

The Requirements

Bachelor s Degree in Environmental Science, Social Science, Engineering or a related discipline.

Relevant Master s Degree preferred.

Minimum 10 years ESG and sustainability experience within the mining sector, including at least 5 years in a senior role with direct lender interface responsibility.

Extensive hands-on experience owning IFC Performance Standards PS1-PS8 compliance roadmaps from development through to implementation and close-out.

Proven experience managing ESAP delivery against lender requirements and agreed milestones.

Direct experience leading ESIA and ESHIA preparation, submissions and regulatory engagement within mining operations.

Strong experience scoping, selecting, contracting and managing specialist environmental and social consultants.

Direct lender interface experience within Equator Principles or IFC-aligned project finance, including lender reviews, site visits, independent engineer engagement and ESAP verification.

Deep working knowledge of international ESG standards and lender requirements.

Proven experience building and leading ESG teams within mining environments.

Previous experience within African mining, with exposure to the DRC or Central African Copperbelt highly advantageous.

Exposure to artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) challenges within African mining environments.

Experience with PS5 resettlement and Livelihood Restoration Plans advantageous.

GISTM and tailings management experience advantageous.

Experience supporting ESG components of project finance, refinancing or M&A transactions advantageous.

Fluent English essential, with working French strongly preferred.

Comfortable working within an expatriate arrangement in the DRC, supporting operations across Lubumbashi and Kolwezi.

The Rewards

This is an exceptional opportunity to take ownership of the ESG agenda within an established copper and cobalt mining business during a significant period of growth and investment.

The successful candidate will have direct exposure to executive leadership, the Board, international lenders and key external stakeholders while playing a central role in strengthening the Company s ESG capability and alignment with international standards.

An attractive expatriate remuneration and benefits package will be offered to the successful candidate.

jobs.title: Commercial Finance Coordinator
jobs.description:
Steelmaking coal is an essential ingredient in blast-furnace steel manufacture, producing steel used for critical building and infrastructure around the world. In Australia, we operate five steelmaking coal mines in Queensland’s Bowen Basin, and have additional joint venture interests in steelmaking coal and manganese, as well as copper exploration projects underway in North West Queensland and Western Australia.

Anglo American is seeking a motivated and detail-focused
Commercial Finance Coordinator
to join the team at Moranbah North Mine.

This site based role is offered Monday to Friday, with FIFO or DIDO options available. It will suit someone who is accurate, proactive and confident engaging with both operational and finance stakeholders.

Reporting to the Commercial Finance Manager, you will support month end reporting, forecasting and financial performance analysis. You will help turn financial data into clear, practical insights that support informed business decisions.

About the role

In this role, you will be responsible for:

Coordinating accurate and timely month-end financial reporting.

Supporting forecasting, budgeting and financial planning activities.

Reviewing cost performance, investigating variances and identifying financial risks

Working with cost centre owners to understand expenditure, commitments and forecast requirements.

Preparing financial reports, presentations and supporting information for business reviews.

Providing clear, practical financial advice to operational and functional stakeholders.

Supporting business cases and capital expenditure requests.

Maintaining accurate financial records, trackers and supporting documentation.

Improving financial reporting, data quality and finance processes.

Ensuring financial governance, approvals and internal controls are followed.

About you

To be successful, you will bring:

A qualification in accounting, finance, commerce, business or a related discipline.

CA or CPA qualifications, or progress towards them.

Experience in financial reporting, month end, forecasting, budgeting or management accounting.

Strong Excel skills and confidence working with financial data.

A high level of accuracy, attention to detail and the ability to identify errors or unusual results.

Strong communication skills and confidence engaging with operational leaders and cost centre owners.

A proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to manage competing priorities.

Experience with SAP or another large financial system would be advantageous.

Experience in mining, resources, heavy industry or another operational environment would be highly regarded.

If you are an accurate and proactive finance professional who enjoys working with operational stakeholders and providing practical commercial support, we would like to hear from you.

What we offer

A site based Monday to Friday role with FIFO or DIDO arrangements available.

The opportunity to build your commercial finance experience within a large mining operation.

Exposure to operational leaders, cost centre owners and experienced finance professionals.

Experience across month end reporting, forecasting, budgeting and commercial analysis.

The opportunity to influence financial performance and support informed business decisions.

A collaborative team environment focused on safety, accountability and continuous improvement.

Who we are

We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies. As the custodians of coal and other precious natural resources diamonds (through De Beers), copper, platinum and other precious metals, iron ore and nickel our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively, with the utmost consideration for local communities, our customers and the world at large.

Background checks

Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

Inclusion and Diversity

Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How we are committed to your safety

Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies from drones to data analytics that are helping to make mining safer.

Employee referral

Do you know someone who would fit this role? Employee referrals will be accepted for this job. Refer to your local Referral Guidelines for policy conditions and amounts.

How to apply

To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. You will have the opportunity to upload your CV and other relevant documentation as part of this process.

jobs.description:
Be part of the team. The team that makes it happen.

We are the world’s leading diamond company, powered by thousands of people around the world who are driven to support thriving local communities, protect the natural environment, and stand with women and girls, focused on Building Forever.

If you like chasing demanding targets, thrive on making decisions in the pursuit of brilliance, and enjoy the support of the world’s finest experts, we have a place for you.

De Beers Group of Companies has an exciting opportunity for strong and committed individual to join the Mine Operations Department that will include vacation entitlement, benefits and bonus opportunity at the Gahcho Kué Mine Site based in the Northwest Territories. Reporting to the Mining Supervisor and working a two (2) week in/ two (2) week out rotation, this position is responsible for operating heavy mobile equipment such as mine haul trucks, large track dozers, large wheel loaders, excavators, and shovels to maximize the mine production of ore and waste in the mine pit. The ideal candidate is one who is committed to safe work practices and strives for zero harm. If you are looking for the opportunity to work for a stable company, at a safe and established mine, we want to hear from you.

This is a fixed term contract position with an end date April 2027.

Key responsibilities:

Safely and skillfully operating a variety of heavy mobile equipment and attachments to excavate, grade and/or move hard rock;

Conducting daily safety checks and inspections of the equipment before operating;

Monitoring equipment and reporting any problems according to mine operating procedures;

Following company procedures and standards such as safety, environmental, and code of conduct; and

Communicating effectively via two-way radio.

Reporting to the Mine Supervisor, the role is based in the Mine Operations department. This is a site-based position with a 14 days in/14 days out rotation.

Formal qualifications:

High school diploma or equivalent life skills;

On-the-job training and experience, resulting in being qualified to run at least three of the following pieces of equipment:

Excavators/Shovel (PC5500/2000/1250/390/210) Loaders (WA1200/900/600/500), Dozers/Rubber Tire Dozers, Graders, and/or Haul Trucks (980/930/830)

Three (3) years’ experience in the mining industry - at remote sites and/or in open pit mines.

Ability to safely work 12-hour day and night shifts on a rotational basis; and

Ability to work in a safety-oriented, fast-paced, cross-cultural environment.

This is not a training position and only those that meet the above requirements will be considered;

Preference will be given to Members of the Deninu Kué, Lutsel K’e Dene First Nation, North Slave Métis Alliance, Northwest Territory Métis Nation, Tlicho Government, or Yellowknives Dene First Nation, followed by non-indigenous residents of the Northwest Territories.

Safety first is a way of life for us. We are unconditional about the safety, health, and the well-being of our colleagues, at work and at home, and about that of the communities where we work. We aim to lead the industry by investing in innovation to protect people, who are at the heart of our business. .

At BHP we support our people to grow, learn, develop their skills and reach their potential.

Technology Supervisor

Demonstrated leadership or supervisory experience in mining, infrastructure, telecommunications, technology, processing, or related operational environments.

Experience supporting critical technology and communications systems within a mining, industrial, or operational setting.

An understanding of operational technology (OT), communications infrastructure, and technology asset management.

Proven ability to lead a team through a safety-first culture whilst driving reliability, productivity, and continuous improvement outcomes.

jobs.description:
Provide and control technical expertise for the department and the Tailings River Management Project as required for PTFI to demonstrate a world class Tailings Management System that complies with both applicable permits approved or issued by the Government of Indonesia and to World Environmental Mine Management standards, while minimizing risk and at a minimum cost for PTFI.

Additional Responsibilities:

1. Develop Tailings Management Plan policies and guidelines to provide a clear direction to all PTFI's divisions regarding tailing management issues, in line with company visions, values and strategies.

2. Provide technical expertise in the management of the TRMP Department, associated contractors/consultants, and to PTFI Senior Management to ensure that PTFI TRMP provides for the Tailings Management Plan (TMP) as required and is in accordance with the PTFI policy and relevant GOI approvals/permits.

3. Provide technical expertise in the direction, management and control of all field construction work activities -including cost control/cost scheduling, administration and RKL/RPL reporting to ensure that all construction works are done according to the project plan, in a most efficient cost, in a satisfactorily and timely manner.

4. Provide technical expertise in the direction, management and control investigation work of the levee design and the overall system design, material monitoring and long-term prediction.

5. Provide technical expertise in the direction, management and control of all survey equipment and activities, monitor whether they are working properly and according to the set schedules to ensure that accurate and timely data are acquired.

6. Provide technical expertise in the direction, management and control of all laboratory tests and other activities to ensure that valid and accurate physical and geochemical data analysis are consistently produced, as a basis of necessary decision making.

7. Provide technical expertise in the direction, management and coordination related to any improper tailing materials composition to come up with correction suggestions and/or actions.

8. Provide technical expertise with the support of the Chief Technical Advisor to PTFI Senior Management to further develop the PTFI Tailings Management policy to reflect changing operational, environmental and political impacts/circumstances.

9. Provide technical expertise in the direction, management and control of division budget including the cost control process, cash flow forecast and forecasting of final cost in each project to ensure all expenditures are at the maximum efficiency.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering with fifteen (15) years of experience in construction, geotechnical, hydro-geological, environmental and mining engineering as part of key core requirement.

Suitable senior engineering and project management background, education, and titles to support the background required.

Demonstrable record of senior achievement in a mining, construction or industrial company.

Measurable skills in working with multidisciplinary teams.

Demonstrable background working within a multicultural environment.

Physical capacity to allow for stressful work situations and for outdoor work in extreme rain and heat.

Extensive experience in heavy equipment machine application.

Strong supervisory and leadership skills.

Concern for safety and environment.

Willingness to work in a team environment.

Strong computer skills.

jobs.description:
About Us

Fortescue is both a proud West Australian company and a global green solutions business. We are recognised for our culture, innovation and industry-leading development of infrastructure, mining assets and green energy initiatives.

Our Opportunity

Work Location:

Perth Office – Fortescue’s Perth office is located on the traditional lands of the Whadjuk Noongar people

Roster:

 Monday to Friday

We are seeking an Automation Projects Specialist to support the practical delivery of automation and field technology projects, with a strong focus on site execution, supplier coordination, installation readiness, commissioning and handover. The successful person will coordinate system installations on site, manage inputs from internal teams and vendors, and ensure works are planned and delivered safely with minimal operational disruption.

This is a Perth-based role with regular site travel required. During active installation and commissioning periods, site attendance will be required.

Key Responsibilities

Establish project scopes, develop scopes of work and prepare project delivery documentation

Coordinate internal inputs across Engineering, Mining Operations, Maintenance, Procurement & Contracts, IT/OT and other relevant teams

Manage supplier and vendor interfaces, including technical deliverables, planning and scheduling, installation support and issue resolution

Track milestones, dependencies, risks and actions, escalating issues early to drive practical resolution

Drive change management to ensure operational readiness, stakeholder engagement, training and implementation planning are delivered in accordance with Fortescue requirements

Oversee system installations on site, including vendor mobilisation, job setup and readiness validation

Support commissioning activities, including system energisation, functional testing, interface validation, fault-finding and handover readiness

Act as the site-facing project representative during installation, commissioning, testing and early operational support phases

Ensure operational feedback is captured and directed towards improvement opportunities for future deployments.

Qualifications and Experience

Experience in mining operations, maintenance or project delivery with site-based execution

Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and drive work through to completion

Experience with Autonomous Haulage Systems (AHS) or mining automation

Experience in electrical installation, commissioning or maintenance

Digger Electrician or field electrical background, including engineering or electrical experience

Experience with industrial automation, control systems, operational technology networks or field technology deployments

Experience with LiDAR, machine vision, image recognition, HMI systems or networked field systems

Experience with remote operations, control rooms or HIVE operations

Strong communication, follow-through and action management skills

Strong practical problem-solving skills.

Our Commitment

Fortescue is deeply committed to providing a safe culture that builds respect, fosters inclusiveness, and values diversity. We celebrate individual strengths and team members from all backgrounds are encouraged to bring their whole selves to work. Our global workforce drives and promotes an inclusive culture, both within our organisation and throughout the communities we interact with across the world. Diverse backgrounds include First Nations Peoples, people with differing abilities, LGBTIQ+ community, gender, neurodiverse, cultural diversity, all age groups, and those with an intersectional or multiple diverse characteristics.
We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

The Senior Project Geologist is responsible for implementation of the projects exploration work program and coordinating resources across multiple exploration sites.  They should have sufficient geological experience and skill to solve complex problems and ensure effective targeting.

Key Responsibilities

Provide ongoing supervision, mentoring and coaching to Project Geologists

Lead the design and implementation of exploration programs, including mapping, surface sampling, and RC and core drill programs.

Manage and deploy assets across multiple exploration sites across within the Project.

Lead the development of robust geological, geochemical, and geophysical data into three-dimensional models using appropriate software leading to the generation of new targets by visualisation, interpretation and interrogation of these models.

Lead in depth geological studies and workflows, research and analysis.

Lead site teams to deliver accurate geological models, data, forecasts, and associated reports within agreed timeframes to provide management guidance with progress/status against forecast timeframes.

Ensure all activities are undertaken in accordance with the company’s policies and procedures, in particular drilling in sampling data and QAQC procedures

Ensure activities are undertaken in accordance with the company’s land management system and regulatory compliance

Qualifications and Experience

Skills

Strong geological knowledge with ability to solve complex problems and ensure effective targeting.

Ability to design and implement project schedules.

Strong report writing, presentation and computer skills

Strong ability with ESRI’s Arc GIS Pro, Field Maps, Database platforms, IMDEX’s ioGAS and Seequent’s Leapfrog.

Experience across different geological terrains and commodities preferred.

Exceptional interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills

Excellent leadership skills

Proven experience in managing remote exploration works or mining activities.

High personal integrity and discretion with strong adaptability.

Experience

Relevant experience in exploration, mining, drilling or field operations (5-10 years).

Experience supervising drilling and data collection programs (3-5 years at Project Geologist level).

Ability to work safely and effectively in remote site conditions.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Geology required, Master's Degree in Geology preferred.

Supplementary training and course work preferred.

jobs.title: Mining Operator
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Mining Operator

Work Location: Christmas Creek

Roster:7D7N14OFF

As a Mining Operator, you will be directly involved in the day-to-day operations of our iron ore mine. You will be responsible for operating mobile equipment at maximum efficiency, contributing to the safe and efficient production of iron ore. You will work closely with your team and under the guidance of supervisory staff to meet production targets and uphold the highest standards of workplace safety.

At Fortescue, we value work-life balance, and offering a lifestyle roster supports balancing professional commitments with personal life. We prioritise family, providing support to ensure you can be present for both your Fortescue team and your loved ones at home.

Key Responsibilities

As a 
 Mobile Operator
, you will safely and efficiently operate heavy mining equipment to support production and operational requirements.

Safely and efficiently operate heavy mobile equipment, including:

D10T / D11T Dozers

854 Wheel Dozers

16M / 24M Graders

993 / 994 Wheel Loaders

Conduct pre-start checks and routine equipment inspections to ensure machinery is safe and operationally ready.

Identify and promptly report safety hazards, equipment faults, damage, or wear and tear to relevant maintenance and supervisory personnel.

Follow all applicable safety procedures, workplace instructions and operating requirements.

Actively participate in safety briefings, meetings and required training.

Work collaboratively with team members to safely achieve production targets and operational objectives.

Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety, operational efficiency and team performance.

Qualifications and Experience

• Ability to skilfully operate some or all the equipment above
• Mobile equipment operation in the mining industry is essential
• Ability to read mine plans
• Knowledge of Mine Safety & Inspection and OHS Act Regs
• WA Class HR Driver's License
• Communication and interpersonal skills - two-way operation

jobs.title: Shutdown Services Scheduler
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Location:
 Fortescue’s Iron Bridge project is located on the traditional lands of the Nyamal people.

Roster:
8D/6R ex Perth 

Reporting to the Shutdown Superintendent, this critical site-based role plays a key part in the successful delivery of large-scale shutdown events within a complex magnetite processing operation.

Working within a high-performing Shutdown Team, you will coordinate the shutdown readiness activities that enable safe, efficient, and reliable shutdown delivery. From workforce mobilisation and contractor coordination through to shutdown facilities, resource and accommodation engagement, equipment, and cost management, you will help ensure every shutdown is set up for success.

Supporting major 240-hour shutdowns and modular 288-hour shutdowns involving up to 1,200 personnel, this role offers an exciting opportunity for an organised and proactive shutdown professional who thrives in fast-paced environments and enjoys coordinating the many moving parts that underpin successful execution.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate workforce, equipment, and vendor mobilisation requirements to support the safe and successful delivery of major shutdown events.

Engage with internal stakeholders to ensure shutdown readiness requirements are achieved.

Liaise with vendor partners and labour providers to secure resources, equipment, and services required for shutdown execution.

Manage the end-to-end purchasing process, including purchase requisitions, goods receipting, and invoice reconciliation activities.

Monitor contractor timesheets, cost tracking, and commercial reporting to support budget compliance and effective cost control.

Maintain shutdown resource registers, equipment tracking systems, and readiness dashboards.

Coordinate site logistics, including shutdown facilities, laydown areas, access requirements, and workforce support arrangements.

Support the management and tracking of hired and internal equipment throughout shutdown planning and execution phases.

Provide execution support during shutdown events, assisting leaders to resolve resource, logistics, and equipment-related issues in a fast-paced operational environment.

Contribute to shutdown reviews and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance future shutdown performance.

Qualifications and Experience

Demonstrated experience in shutdown, maintenance, operations, project coordination, or resource planning within mining, processing, heavy industry, or similar environments.

Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to work effectively across operations, maintenance, contractors, vendors, and support departments.

Highly developed organisational and coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities within tight deadlines.

Experience managing contractor mobilisation, workforce logistics, equipment coordination, or shutdown support activities.

Sound commercial awareness, including experience with purchase requisitions, invoice processing, cost tracking, and contractor administration.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Outlook, and Teams.

Experience using SAP

Strong problem-solving capability and the ability to adapt within a dynamic and time-critical shutdown environment.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to engage with personnel at all organisational levels.

jobs.title: Senior ERP Technical Specialist
jobs.description:
About Woodside

We know great results come from our people feeling valued, getting the support they need to reach their full potential as well as bring their whole self to work. We also recognise that enduring, meaningful relationships with communities are fundamental to maintaining our licence to operate.

Technology and innovation are essential to our long-term sustainability. jobs.title: Senior Geologist, Resource Estimation
jobs.description:
The Company

B2Gold is a responsible international gold producer headquartered in Vancouver, Canada. Founded in 2007, today, B2Gold has operating gold mines in Canada, Mali, Namibia and the Philippines, and numerous development and exploration projects in various countries.

Position

Senior Geologist, Resource Estimation

Introduction

Reporting to the Director, Technical Services – Exploration, this role plays a key part in advancing B2Gold’s global resource portfolio by delivering high quality mineral resource models that support exploration strategy, project evaluation, drill program planning, and mine planning. Working within a collaborative corporate environment, this position will contribute technical expertise across multiple assets and jurisdictions, partnering closely with Exploration, Technical Services, Geoscience, Operations, and site management teams. The successful candidate will be a responsible and self-directed professional who is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where there is frequent change. International and domestic travel will be required.

Location

This is a full-time position based at B2Gold’s Corporate Office in Vancouver, Canada. The role follows our hybrid work model of four days in-office and one day remote each week.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Develop lithology, alteration, structural and mineralization models to support mineral resource estimates;

Prepare mineral resource estimates in accordance with industry best practices, including validation of all inputs and outputs;

Identify and communicate risks, uncertainties, and opportunities within geological and resource models;

Coordinate with exploration teams including field staff on geological interpretations, data integrity, QA/QC, and drill hole planning;

Support the preparation of internal and external technical reports and disclosures, including compliance with internal procedures, and relevant reporting standards and guidelines (e.g. NI 43-101 or as applicable);

Support the application of modifying factors and the development of resource models for mine planning purposes;

Work closely with operations and engineering teams on mine planning and model reconciliation;

Conduct internal peer reviews of models developed by colleagues and provide constructive feedback to support continuous improvement;

Manage third-party contractors or consultants as required; and,

Perform other duties as required in support of corporate and site objectives.

Requirements:

Degree in Geology, Geological Engineering or relevant discipline from a recognized university;

Minimum of 10 years of experience in the mining industry, including significant experience in mineral resource estimation (typically 5+ years);

Professional Geoscientist registered in British Columbia or another province or eligibility for registration;

Demonstrated experience in core logging, geological interpretations, 3D modeling and mineral resource estimation;

Experience in operating mining environments, including resource and reserve reconciliation;

Proven ability to work effectively both independently and within multidisciplinary teams in a fast-paced environment;

Strong analytical, problem-solving and organizational skills;

Communicate effectively in English with technical teams and senior management, both verbally and in writing; and,

Proficiency in industry-standard software (e.g. Datamine, Surpac, Micromine, Leapfrog Geo, Supervisor, MS Office Suite)

Additional Desired Qualifications:

Experience contributing to NI 43-101 compliant resource reporting;

Experience working with and/or managing consultants and teams directly and remotely is an asset;and,

Experience with challenging jurisdictions a strong asset.

Job Demands/Physical Requirements:

This position is based out of our Vancouver head office with frequent domestic and international travel required which may be on short notice and for long durations (approximately 20-25% of the time annually)

Compensation

B2Gold prioritizes local employment, supports empowerment initiatives and continuously works towards a people profile that matches the demographics of the respective national settings in which we operate, while appreciating our inclusive culture that attracts talent from around the world. As an equal-opportunity employer, B2Gold values diversity and we encourage all qualified candidates to apply.

B2Gold offers a competitive compensation package, including base salary commensurate with the candidate’s experience, knowledge and skill set, and a comprehensive benefit package for employees and their eligible dependents. The base salary range for this position is CAD $175,000 – 190,000 per annum, which is the anticipated pay at the time of hire but does not reflect similar future job opportunities. Details of the total compensation package will be shared during the interview process.

We thank all applicants for their interest in B2Gold Corp., however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
