jobs.title: Safety Supervisor
jobs.description:
Safety Supervisor

Sukari is located approximately 750km from Cairo and 25km from Marsa Alam on the Red Sea. First gold was poured in June 2009 and commercial production began in April 2010, making Sukari the first modern gold mine in Egypt, a country which in ancient times was a prolific producer of the precious metal. Sukari conducts both open-pit and underground mining operations, each employing specialized mining methods tailored to the orebody characteristics and operational requirements.

Location: On-site in Marsa Alam

Contract Type: Permanent, full-time

Schedule: 6 / 3 working roster

Compensation: Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package

The Role

We are looking for a qualified experienced
Safety Supervisor
to manage frontline safety operations, supervise field safety personnel, and drive safety compliance across site operations. Reporting to the Safety Superintendent, you will coordinate HSE activities, evaluate site hazards, lead safety campaigns, and ensure adherence to local regulations and international management systems.

The Key Responsibilities

Field Leadership & Supervision:
Manage and coach frontline field safety officers, oversee day-to-day roster coverage, and conduct regular safety meetings for employees and contractors.

Risk Management & Inspections:
Conduct risk assessments, Job Safety Analyses (JSA), area inspections, and evaluate high-risk management plans (e.g., electrical, lifting, liquid oxygen).

Incident Analytics & CAPA:
Analyze leading and lagging indicators, lead incident investigations, and track Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) through to completion.

Compliance & Audits:
Prepare and presenting regular HSE reports, monitor compliance with Egyptian HSE legislation, and execute internal audit plans.

Training & Awareness:
Deliver site inductions, issue toolbox talks, and identify departmental safety training requirements.

Contractor & Supply Chain Support:
Review contractor safety plans, evaluate tender specs and Scopes of Work (SOW), and approve personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements.

The Requirements

Education:
Bachelor s degree in Science, Engineering, Agriculture, or a related field.

Certifications:
NEBOSH IGC, ASP, CSP, or equivalent safety certification; Train-the-Trainer certification preferred.

Experience:
3 to 10 years of professional safety experience, ideally within mining, construction, or heavy industrial environments.

Technical Skills:

   Strong knowledge of Egyptian HSE legislation and international safety standards.
   Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and incident management software.
   Valid Light Vehicle (LV) site/mine driver’s license.

Language & Communication:
High-level English proficiency (written and spoken) with excellent reporting skills.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Technician
jobs.description:
Element Six, part of De Beers Group, is a global leader in the design, development and production of synthetic diamond and tungsten carbide supermaterials.

With research and development facilities and manufacturing sites in the UK, Ireland, Germany, South Africa and the US, we have been pushing the boundaries of synthetic diamond innovation for more than 60 years. We utilise the extreme properties of synthetic diamond to open up new possibilities in exciting areas such as quantum optics, acoustics and thermal conductivity.

Our success comes from building strong, collaborative relationships, both internally in our extraordinary teams, and externally with our customers. We strive to deliver extreme performance and we seek talented, ambitious people who will thrive in an environment that fosters individuality, inclusivity, innovation and creativity.

We offer an exciting and varied career, with opportunities to work in various locations and teams, and across different functions and projects.

If you like the idea of an exciting variety of work in a diverse global team, then we want you to get in touch.

Job overview

Following a successful recruitment program in 2022, we are looking to further expand our small and friendly manufacturing team based in Santa Clara, California.

In our laboratories, a team of skilled scientists and technicians develop and produce novel, high-performance diamond products for the global market.

This is an integral role in supporting our end-to-end manufacturing activities and will involve using a range of polishing, lapping, measuring and inspection tools.

The successful candidate will carry out key processes for our post-production operations to meet operational needs.

The role will suit a diligent and autonomous individual with good attention to detail who enjoys a structured approach to their work.

The successful applicant will be trained and supported by subject experts in each area.

The role is considered flexible and the successful applicant may train into other processes as business requirements dictate. We have a “skills-based pay” program to reward such cross training.

Safety culture is a priority given the inherent higher risks and hazards of our industrial processes and working environment.

The ideal candidate will look to support continuous improvement across production.

Duties and tasks

Delivering work safely and to a standard that ensures the health and safety of others.

Undertaking work in diamond wafer processing (lapping, polishing, quality control checks) as well any other ad-hoc requirements as requested.

Using lappers, polishing tools and precise measurement tools to ensure products are finished to the specification required.

Maintain equipment and work area to a high standard of neatness & cleanliness.

Working as an integral member of the production team to ensure Promise Adherence of delivery to customer.

Be a role model for our Company values.

The applicant is required to work to very exacting standards and expectations – these are critical processes applied to very high value parts.

A diligent & careful worker with a keen eye for detail.

The ideal applicant has machining or lapping/polishing skills or has demonstrated competence in an artisanal trade. This is not a requirement as enthusiastic and diligent candidates can be highly successful in the role.

Good interpersonal and communication skills.

Able to work both independently and as part of a team.

Basic computer literacy to use QC tools/equipment and perform data acquisition.

jobs.title: Analista de Sistemas de TI Sênior - Exclusiva para Mulheres
jobs.description:
A Anglo American é uma empresa global de mineração com sede em Londres, presente em diversos países e com uma história de mais de 100 anos, com o propósito de reimaginar a mineração para melhorar a vida das pessoas.

Na América Latina, nossas operações desempenham um papel estratégico no fornecimento responsável de recursos essenciais para o desenvolvimento do mundo – com atuação no Brasil, Chile e Peru, sempre pautadas por inovação, segurança, sustentabilidade e alto desempenho.

No Brasil, operamos o sistema Minas-Rio, que integra mina, usina, mineroduto e porto. As operações do Peru e do Chile se concentram na produção de cobre em larga escala, reforçando nosso compromisso com uma transição energética sustentável.

Acreditamos que nossas pessoas são o maior diferencial competitivo. Investimos no desenvolvimento de talentos, promovendo ambientes inclusivos e colaborativos, onde diferentes perspectivas constroem soluções melhores para os desafios do presente e do futuro.

Na Anglo American, valorizamos quem deseja crescer com propósito e gerar impacto real.

Você será responsável por garantir a continuidade, disponibilidade e evolução dos sistemas técnicos de mineração, atuando na análise, priorização e implementação de soluções tecnológicas. Realizar suporte avançado (L2/L3), gestão de demandas, projetos, governança de aplicações e fornecedores, assegurando conformidade com os padrões da Anglo American. Atuar na melhoria contínua dos processos, com foco em segurança, desempenho, confiabilidade e suporte às operações.

Veja abaixo as principais atividades:

Prestar suporte avançado (L2/L3) para sistemas de mineração, processamento, confiabilidade e integridade operacional.

Gerenciar incidentes, problemas, mudanças e demandas seguindo práticas ITIL.

Conduzir análises de causa raiz (RCA) e implementar ações corretivas e preventivas.

Liderar tecnicamente fornecedores AMS, acompanhar backlog, entregas e níveis de serviço.

Desenvolver e manter procedimentos operacionais, documentação técnica e bases de conhecimento.

Levantar requisitos, elaborar especificações técnicas e propor melhorias para sistemas e processos.

Planejar e acompanhar releases, patches, upgrades e roadmap das soluções.

Executar e suportar processos de testes, homologação e implantação de sistemas.Gerenciar contratos, licenças, conformidade e evidências de auditoria dos sistemas.

Executar processos de governança de TI e apoiar auditorias e controles internos.

Planejar e executar atividades técnicas em projetos e iniciativas estratégicas.Identificar necessidades de treinamento e promover capacitação dos usuários.

Desenvolver aplicações de baixa complexidade, dashboards e relatórios gerenciais.

Aplicar conceitos de Data Literacy e promover o uso de dados nas áreas de negócio.

Participar de eventos, fóruns e comunidades técnicas do segmento.

O perfil que estamos buscando para essa posição:

Ensino superior em Engenharia, Sistemas de Informação,Ciência da Computação/ ou afins.

Desejável Pós-graduação em áreas afins.

Power BI, Banco de dados, Linguagem de programação.

ITIL, COBIT.

Experiência sólida em sustentação L2/L3 aplicações industriais.

Inglês avançado.

Por que fazer parte do nosso time?

Somos uma empresa empenhada em fazer nossas crenças e valores acontecerem de verdade. O objetivo é proporcionar a você um ambiente de qualidade, diverso e seguro para que você desenvolva o seu melhor. Para isso, oferecemos os melhores benefícios:

·
Para cuidar da sua saúde física e mental:

Gympass, Plano de Saúde e Odontológico (extensivo a você e seus dependentes), além de Assistência Psicológica e Aplicativo Saúde Emocional

·
Especial para você e sua família:

Auxílio Creche, Programa Família, Brinquedo de Natal e Vale Alimentação!

· Espaço para ser você mesmo:

Fique à vontade para participar de nossos Grupos de Afinidades e dos eventos incríveis da Semana da Diversidade!

· Para seu futuro:

Plano de Previdência Privada diferenciado

· E ainda:

Transporte fretado, refeições no local de trabalho, remuneração variável, Seguro de Vida, Apoio e orientação: Jurídico, financeiro, social e psicológico.

Como estamos comprometidos com a sua segurança?

Nada é mais importante para nós do que garantir que você volte para casa com segurança após um dia de trabalho. Para que isso aconteça, temos os padrões de segurança mais rigorosos do setor. Além disso, também estamos investindo continuamente em novas tecnologias, de drones a análise de dados, que estão ajudando a tornar a mineração mais segura.

Inclusão e Diversidade

Temos o compromisso de promover um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo e diversificado, no qual valorizamos e respeitamos cada colega por quem ela/ele é. Acolhemos e celebramos todas as identidades de gênero, etnias, idades, espiritualidades, orientações sexuais, deficiências, classes sociais, estilos de vida e habilidades. E foi para escutar todas essas vozes que criamos os Grupos de Afinidades: espaços seguros para discutir, refletir e construir ações de inclusão e diversidade no âmbito da equidade de gênero, LGBTQIAP+, etnia, pessoas com deficiência e geracional.

Nós queremos colegas que se sintam valorizados, respeitados e sintam-se abertos para trazer seu “verdadeiro eu” para o trabalho.

*Reforçamos que todas as vagas estão abertas para pessoas com deficiência (PcD) e reabilitados do INSS.

Nosso processo seletivo

Para se candidatar a essa vaga, realize seu cadastro on-line, e anexe seu currículo no ato da inscrição.

Nosso processo seletivo, de forma geral, é constituído das seguintes etapas: inscrição, análise dos currículos, dinâmica/entrevista, avaliação comportamental, exame médico e admissão.

Fique atento à página da/do candidata/candidato, assim como aos meios de comunicação (e-mail, telefone, WhatsApp), pois todo o processo será mediado por essas plataformas.

Venha com a gente construir o futuro da mineração!

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Element Six is a global leader in the design, development and production of synthetic diamond and tungsten carbide supermaterials. Part of the De Beers Group, we employ over 1,700 people. Our primary manufacturing sites are located in the USA, UK, Ireland, Germany and South Africa.

Our mission

We put our customers first. Using our technological expertise and industrial leadership we deliver innovative solutions to achieve competitive advantage.

Our vision

With access to the most sophisticated R&D technology and the best minds in the business, the future is full of possibilities…

Lead the production organisation in a 24/7 environment, with direct accountability for the safety and occupational health of all department employees.

Act as second-in-command to the General Manager for operational matters, providing visible leadership, clear decision-making and effective site coordination; deputise when required.

Own Utilisation performance and the associated operating routines, measures and improvement plans, ensuring available capacity is converted safely and reliably to technically compliant product.

Translate demand and capacity requirements into robust production plans, schedules and resource priorities; maintain disciplined execution, recovery and escalation routines.

Lead, motivate and develop a production team of ca. 40 people, including the Production Manager and front-line leaders; set clear objectives, build capability and hold the organisation to account.

Work in close partnership with the Engineering & Maintenance Manager, who owns Availability, and the Process Engineering Manager, who owns Yield, to improve overall equipment effectiveness and remove systemic constraints.

Be a key member of the site leadership team, contributing to site HSE performance, strategy implementation, investment planning, operational excellence, organisational effectiveness and long-term capability development.

Hold responsibility for production volumes, labour and operational cost, planning adherence, quality and delivery KPIs, and delivery of the department budget.

Establish clear performance-management routines and use data to identify losses, prioritise actions and drive sustained continuous improvement using Business Excellence principles and tools.

Build effective interfaces with Supply Chain, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, R&D, external suppliers and other CVD sites so that ORTEC provides in-spec material in line with agreed customer and downstream-site requirements.

jobs.title: Senior Maintenance Planner (Maintenance Coordinator)
jobs.description:
Anglo American Australia

In Australia, we operate five steelmaking coal mines in Queensland’s Bowen Basin, and have additional joint venture interests in manganese, as well as copper exploration projects under way in North West Queensland. Steelmaking coal is an essential ingredient in blast-furnace steel manufacture, producing steel used for critical building and infrastructure around the world. 

We are seeking a
Maintenance Coordinator
to join our team at Capcoal Surface Operations in Middlemount, Queensland. Capcoal is an open cut coal operation producing approximately 5.1 Mtpa, utilising a fleet that includes a rope shovel, five excavators, two draglines and three drills.

As the Maintenance Coordinator you will report to the Maintenance Superintendent and will manage a team of 5 Maintenance Planners responsible for developing and executing the short-term maintenance plans and schedules for our mobile and field fleet, in addition to light vehicles and ancillary equipment.

Alongside your leadership responsibilities, you will be responsible for the development of long-term maintenance plans and budgets covering timeframes of up to 18 months. You’ll help shape equipment strategies, contribute to capital planning, manage key technical information and ensure forecasts are consistent and up to date.

To be successful in this position you will ideally have experience in the following:

You will possess a mechanical trade qualification, engineering degree or have experience in asset management.

Demonstrated experience working in a leadership / supervisor capacity within a maintenance team at a large, open cut mining operation

Previous maintenance planning experience for field and / or mobile equipment and a well-developed understanding of maintenance strategies

Ability to focus on long-term solutions, ongoing innovation, maintenance costs, workplace efficiencies

Knowledge in SAP, Obzervr, Link One and OEM parts systems are highly desirable

Industry experience in maintenance budgeting, asset management systems and familiarity with mining equipment lifecycle strategies

Knowledge of the QLD Coal Mining Legislation and Coal Mining practices

Monday to Friday role with 9-day fortnight available

Full-time permanent position based at Capcoal Surface Operations, Middlemount QLD

Residential, DIDO and FIFO (company funded) options

Subsidised Housing (residentially) and/or Camp Accommodation (company funded)

Attractive Salary + 12% Superannuation

Discounted Gym membership

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) available for employees

What we offer

When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package and a range of flexible work arrangements that support the balance of work, family and individual circumstances. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programs, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too.

Who we are

We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies.  Anglo American is a leading global mining company focused on the responsible production of copper, premium iron ore and crop nutrients – future-enabling products that are essential for decarbonising the global economy, improving living standards, and food security. Our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively to unlock enduring value from precious natural resources for our shareholders, for the benefit of the communities and countries in which we operate, and for society as a whole. Anglo American is re-imagining mining to improve people’s lives.

Background checks

Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

Inclusion and Diversity

Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How we are committed to your safety

Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies – from drones to data analytics – that are helping to make mining safer.

How to apply

To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. You will have the opportunity to upload your CV and other relevant documentation as part of this process.

REF78293Q

CLOSING DATE

14 September 2026

Please note, screening and interviews may take place prior to closing date – applications may also close before this date.

Recruitment Agencies

Anglo American Australia does not accept unsolicited applications from recruitment agencies.

jobs.description:
About BHP

At BHP we support our people to grow, learn, develop their skills and reach their potential. With a global portfolio of operations, we offer a diverse and inclusive environment with extraordinary career opportunities. Our strategy is to focus on creating a safe work environment where our employees feel strongly connected to our values and objectives, and where the capability of our people is key to our success.

Come and be a part of this success.

About BHP Operations Services

BHP Operations Services delivers industry leading mining services across BHP operations Australia-wide with specialist capabilities in load and haul, fixed plant maintenance and mobile maintenance.

BHP Operations Services has a strong focus on people capability and culture. Our people are our greatest asset and are at the centre of everything that we do. We focus on high performance safety and productivity through our people. With world-class training that is unmatched in the industry and the opportunity to advance your career across locations and commodities, join the team and make your place in BHP.

We are investing in our team to take your skills and career to places you never thought possible. This is an exciting time for BHP. Are you ready to make your place? 

About the Opportunity

Mining maintenance means helping keep large mobile equipment safe, reliable and ready to operate. This can include checking equipment, replacing parts, identifying faults, completing servicing tasks and assisting tradespeople with repairs.

Maintenance Traineeships
are a 11-month training program based at the BHP FutureFit Academy in Mackay designed to provide you with the skills necessary to undertake this maintenance work on our mine sites.

Trainees study to become skilled Maintenance Associates with BHP, completing a Certificate II in Engineering.

Our Traineeships will provide you with exciting opportunities including:

Learning from some of the mining industry’s most experienced mechanical tradespersons / Trainer Assessors, at BHP’s own FutureFit Academy.

Learning about the equipment that we use to mine commodities. Some equipment you will learn about are; Bulldozers, Graders, Loaders, Excavators and Dump Trucks.

Learning how to identify equipment issues, understand what may have caused them, and support safe repairs under supervision. 

Participating in a mixture of classroom and theory learning, as well as practical workshop training. You will learn to interpret mechanical drawings, the basics of hydraulics and about the variety of tools we use to maintain these machines.

Paid training which is undertaken at our training academy in Mackay. While training you will be working a roster of 7 Days / 7 Off / 7 Nights / 7 Off, day shift hours are 6am to 4:30pm and night shift hours are 1:30pm to 12:00am.

At BHP, nothing matters more than the safety of our people. To support our Fatigue Management Plan, we require all 
applicants to live within a 45-minute commute of our Mackay Academy
.

Accommodation and transportation is not provided and candidates would need to relocate to the Mackay area if they do not already live locally. BHP has sites across Australia and it is important to understand that you may be required to relocate (including interstate) once you complete your training. This is based on demand for your trade or skillset across our mine sites.

The Mackay academy is currently offering Heavy Diesel Traineeship roles
 planned to commence in February, 2027. 
If you are interested in applying, we highly recommend you visit our website 
here
 for more information on the program.

About You

No mining experience is required, we’ll teach you the technical skills. What matters most is your commitment to safety, willingness to learn, practical mindset and interest in how equipment works.

To set you up for success, you will need:

You must be 18 years or older to apply

A high commitment to safety

A strong desire to learn and develop a range of new skills

Motivation to achieve goals & enjoy a mixture of classroom and workshop learning

Ability to live a safe travelling distance to the training centre - this is not a FIFO/DIDO role (whilst studying at the academy).

Ability to attend a roster that rotates across early mornings, evenings, weekends and public holidays 

To have the necessary personal support networks available to assist you in working the above roster

Experience working on machinery/vehicles through a hobby or work is highly regarded, but not essential

About Our Process

At BHP, we are committed to employing individuals who align with the BHP Charter Values and meet the requirements of the role. As part of the recruitment process, there are a number of checks which may be conducted to demonstrate applicants suitability for a role including police / criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks.

Supporting a Diverse Workforce

The size, stability and magnitude of our business not only provides significant opportunity for professional development, but also attractive salary packages with performance-based bonuses and a best-in-class employee share program. We know there are many aspects of our employees' lives that are important, and work is only one of these, so we offer benefits to enable your work to fit with your life. These benefits include flexible working options, a generous paid parental leave policy, other extended leave entitlements and parent rooms. 

At BHP, we know that we are strengthened by diversity. We are an Equal Opportunity employer that is committed to making BHP a safe and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive and be at their best every day. We are focused on creating a workforce that’s more diverse and represents the communities where we work and live. providing a work environment in which everyone is included, treated fairly and with respect. Chino is an open-pit copper mining complex located 15 miles from the historic mining community of Silver City in southwestern New Mexico. The historic Chino mine was among the world's first low-grade, open-pit copper mines. Today, the operation consists of a 36,000-metric-ton-per-day concentrator that produces copper and a 150-million-pound-per-year solvent extraction/electrowinning plant that produces copper cathode from solution generated by run-of-mine leaching.    

The community of Silver City boasts various restaurants, arts, entertainment, cliff dwellings, festivals and much more. Adequate score on Companywide assessment test to demonstrate knowledge.

Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Accelerate Your Career

Jaguar TCS Racing is at the forefront of electric motorsport innovation, competing in the electrifying Formula E Championship. As part of the legendary Jaguar brand, our team is dedicated to pioneering advancements in electric vehicle technology, sustainability, and performance. With a rich heritage in racing and a commitment to pushing the boundaries of electric mobility, Jaguar TCS Racing combines passion, expertise, and cutting-edge technology to compete at the highest levels of motorsport.

An opportunity has arisen for a Composite & Team Mechanical Support to join the Jaguar TCS Racing department in a rapidly expanding and exciting work environment.

About the role

To provide composite component assembly, repair and mechanical support for the Jaguar Formula E Team.

What you will do

Primary function:

To bring the expertise, process and hands-on ability necessary to provide the Jaguar Formula E Team with composite component assembly and repair on event and at the factory.

Support the Race, Test and factory teams in their operational goals, being able to assist with other hands on team requirements as required.

Assemble, adjust, repair and disassemble the team’s composite components on event and at the factory.

Assemble / repair / maintain components, pit and garage equipment and car hardware as required.

Assemble and maintain race and test garage infrastructures and hardware both on event and when at the factory.

Provide hands on support for factory operations as required

Ideally, possess a good vehicle wrapping skillset; able to confidently wrap complex bodywork and garage infrastructure components.

Adequate composite trackside assembly and on event repair experience, in a motorsport environment.

A confident team player, familiar with the fast paced and ever-changing requirements of a race and test team.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Controller
jobs.description:
About Us

Fortescue is both a proud West Australian company and a global green solutions business. We are recognised for our culture, innovation and industry-leading development of infrastructure, mining assets and green energy initiatives.

Our Opportunity

Work Location:

Perth – Fortescue’s Perth office is located on the traditional lands of the Whadjuk Noongar people

Roster: 

Monday to Friday

Fortescue has multiple opportunities for experienced Senior Cost Controllers to join our Major Projects team, supporting a diverse portfolio of significant projects across the business.

These roles offer the opportunity to contribute across a suite of major projects, including our decarbonisation program and greenfield mining expansions. Working across projects at different stages of development and delivery, you will play an important role in maintaining strong financial discipline, cost visibility and project performance.

As a Senior Cost Controller, you will partner with project teams to provide accurate budgeting, forecasting, cost reporting and analysis, while strengthening cost management systems and processes. You will bring commercial insight to project decision-making and help ensure our major projects are delivered with effective financial oversight and control.

This is an opportunity to build your experience across a varied and evolving major projects portfolio while contributing to projects that support Fortescue's operational growth and decarbonisation ambitions.

Key Responsibilities

Implement and maintain cost management systems, processes, and procedures to support consistent project cost control, budgeting, forecasting, and performance analysis.

Manage project cost and progress reporting, ensuring accurate, timely insights and identification of actions to maintain baseline targets

Apply and maintain the project Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) to ensure alignment across systems, reporting, and cost tracking

Deliver monthly cost reporting, variance analysis, and performance insights using earned value management (EVM) techniques

Manage Value of Work Done (VOWD), commitments, resource forecasting, and Estimate at Completion (EAC) / Estimate to Complete (ETC) processes

Oversee work packages to ensure cost compliance with the Project Controls Plan and validate contractor progress and invoicing

Review contractor claims, purchase orders, and payment certificates, ensuring alignment with contracts and project performance

Manage accruals, cost allocations, and financial close processes, ensuring accurate recording against cost centres and WBS

Ensure effective change management processes (PCN) are applied and reflected in cost forecasts and reporting

Monitor and audit cost systems and SAP data, supporting procurement activities and mentoring junior cost controllers to ensure accuracy and continuous improvement.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Commerce, Finance, or a related discipline, with project management or recognised project controls certification desirable

Minimum 5 years’ experience in project controls roles across complex construction, engineering, resources, or renewable energy environments

Demonstrated experience delivering project controls across full project lifecycles, from early estimates through to execution and close-out

Proven capability managing cost control functions for mid to large-scale capital projects, including development of progress reporting methodologies

Strong understanding of project controls principles, including budgeting, cost tracking, and cashflow forecasting and analysis

Experience working on major or mega projects, including exposure to international interfaces or multi-stakeholder environments

Sound knowledge of project services, contracting, and procurement disciplines and their integration with cost engineering activities

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to apply practical solutions in dynamic project environments

Highly effective communication and reporting skills, with the ability to present insights and recommendations to stakeholders at all levels

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and MS Office tools, with experience in project systems such as Omega PIMS advantageous.

Our Commitment

Fortescue is deeply committed to providing a safe culture that builds respect, fosters inclusiveness, and values diversity. We celebrate individual strengths and team members from all backgrounds are encouraged to bring their whole selves to work. Our global workforce drives and promotes an inclusive culture, both within our organisation and throughout the communities we interact with across the world. Diverse backgrounds include First Nations Peoples, people with differing abilities, LGBTIQ+ community, gender, neurodiverse, cultural diversity, all age groups, and those with an intersectional or multiple diverse characteristics.
We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

About Us

Are you looking for the next step in your career and want to be a part of something big?

Established in Western Australia in 2003, Fortescue is a global green technology, energy and metals company, recognised for its culture, innovation and industry leading development of infrastructure, mining assets and green energy initiatives.

As we move towards a more sustainable future and work towards decarbonising our iron ore mining operations, we’re seeking passionate, driven individuals who are eager to contribute to our Real Zero mission and help shape the future.

Our Opportunity

We are seeking Expressions of Interest from passionate and capable 
Emergency Services Officers (ESO’s)
to join our growing talent community and become part of a high-performing Emergency Response Team across our Pilbara mine sites.

This is more than just an ESO role — it’s an opportunity to work alongside a respected team that plays a critical role in protecting our people, operations and communities. Our Emergency Services team is built on teamwork, resilience, professionalism and a genuine commitment to safety and emergency preparedness.

As an ESO, you will respond to emergency incidents onsite while supporting the day-to-day operations of the emergency services and medical team. You’ll work in a dynamic environment where no two days are the same, continuing to build your capability across emergency response, rescue, firefighting, medical and incident management disciplines.

Work Location:
FIFO opportunities available from Perth, Busselton, Karratha, Port Hedland, Fitzroy Crossing or Kununurra to our Pilbara WA mine operations.

Roster:
8D6R7N7R

Respond to all onsite emergency incidents as part of the Emergency Response Team

Maintain emergency response equipment and complete compliance inspections and reporting

Conduct fitness for work testing in accordance with site and company Alcohol & Other Dugs (AOD) policies

Plan, coordinate and participate in emergency response drills and training exercises

Provide onsite medical support and maintain medical facilities in an operationally ready state

Deliver leadership, mentoring and training support to ERT members and site personnel

Maintain the required level of operational fitness to safely perform the role

Qualifications & Experience

Demonstrated operational experience within a mine site ESO team and/or State Emergency or Fire Service environment

jobs.title: Mining Engineer - Tijeras, NM Plant
jobs.description:
This Mining Engineer position is located at GCC's Tijeras, NM plant, just 15 minutes from Albuquerque, NM. Relocation assistance is available.

We are seeking a Mining Engineer with a Bachelor's degree in Mining Engineering and 3-5 years of mining industry experience. The ideal candidate has expertise in mine planning, permitting, regulatory compliance, and project management, including experience working with local, state, and federal regulatory agencies. Proficiency in AutoCAD, Carlson, Trimble, and related mining software is required, along with strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

The successful candidate will support mine planning, engineering projects, permitting activities, and operational improvements while ensuring regulatory compliance and maintaining a strong commitment to safety. They will have experience managing projects, coordinating contractors and stakeholders, preparing technical reports and cost estimates, and driving cost-effective solutions for mining operations.

PE or E.I.T. certification, or the ability to obtain certification within one year, is preferred. The ideal candidate is a collaborative, safety-focused professional who combines technical expertise, leadership, and a continuous improvement mindset to support the successful operation and long-term growth of mining and quarry assets.

Required Education:

Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.) in Mining Engineering

Required Experience and Skills:

3 to 5 years' experience in mining.

Minimum three years' experience with permitting submittals, compliance and negotiations with local, state and federal regulatory agencies.

3+ years project management experience.

Proficiency in current AutoCAD and Carlson software, along with other relevant industry software, is required at an intermediate to advanced level.

PE or E.I.T. Certification, or ability to obtain within 1 year.

What you will do:

The incumbent in this position has responsibility for mine planning, permitting (local, state & federal), construction projects, site engineering, and assisting mine management in solving, in the soundest and economic way possible, a wide variety of engineering and mine planning issues as they arise, while ensuring compliance with all regulatory agencies.

Coordinate mine-related engineering projects, including managing internal project employees, external contractors and support.

Support Raw Materials Manager in assigned mine planning and processes and additional engineering projects as they arise; including but not limited to site issues, safety issues and structural - geological troubleshooting.

Inspect mining areas for unsafe structures, equipment and working conditions.

Support management in planning and executing successful mine planning, ventilation, roof control, mining advancements (power center, ventilation, & belts), specifying processes and equipment, advancing miner tracking system, shooting sights, and maintaining mine/quarry map.

Work with Raw Materials Manager in preparing schedules, reports, and estimates of the costs involved in developing and operating the mine(s).

Prepare technical reports for use by management and outside engineering.

Design, develop and implement computer applications using programs such as AutoCAD, Carlson software and Trimble for use in mining operations such as mine design, modeling or mapping or for monitoring mine conditions

Support safety and "Safety as a Value" by assisting the GCCE management team in the deployment and sustaining of the GCCE Master Safety Plan; timely review of plan and assisting in necessary updates, monitoring, and training.

Conduct studies of methods to reduce mining and site costs by utilizing engineering techniques involving design modifications, energy applications, conservation, and best practices management.

Assist in long-term capital expenditure planning for mine, quarries, etc.

Support quarry department by monitoring costs and working closely with the Raw Materials Manager to control undesirable cost impacts.

Perform other duties, as assigned.

Who we are:

GCC is a world-class company that produces, distributes and markets cement, ready-mixed concrete, aggregates, and innovative products related to the construction industries in Mexico and the United States. We take pride in being a market leader with a culture of innovation, high performance and safety. GCC offers a very competitive benefits program including paid time off, medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability insurance plans, and a 401K.

You will love working here because:

At GCC, employees are our most important resource. As a part of the GCC family, you'll be welcomed into a culture that promotes the company vision and internal career growth. Our company vision is to have our customers recognize us as a business partner that generates the most value for their construction projects. We're a sustainable growing company, a great place to work, and a solid investment for our shareholders. GCC is an enterprise with a global and sustainable approach. Our production is mainly devoted to the manufacture and sale of gray Portland cement, mortar, premixed concrete, concrete blocks, plaster, aggregates, and other construction materials. Join the family!

An Equal Opportunity Employer

GCC does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, genetic information, or any other status protected by law or regulation. It is our intention that all qualified applicants be given equal opportunity and that selection decisions are based on job-related factors.

We hold each other accountable to live our core values of health and safety, attitude of service, integrity, teamwork, innovation and excellence. GCC employees demonstrate these values every day. The Processing Production Outflow Team plays a critical role in supporting the WAIO supply chain by ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of ore to rail. jobs.description:
Why You Should Apply for This Job  

At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing an employment package that recognizes excellence, encourages safe production and a culture supported by our core values. Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority, all opinions are valued, and people are empowered to grow in their career.
Apply Today!

Where You Will Work    

Our global headquarters is in Phoenix, Arizona. Several hundred employees support global operations in finance, human resources, information technology, planning and more from the main office, satellite offices or online. As a Hybrid employee, you’ll engage in virtual collaboration as well as attend in-person meetings at our Collaboration Hub in Phoenix or at one of our site locations. The Collaboration Hub provides an open, flexible workspace for individuals and teams to come together for various business needs. Amenities at the Hub include a working café, phone booths and meeting rooms with technology tools for virtual and in-person collaboration. In-person attendance may vary based on the position and department requirements. 

Phoenix is the capital of the Grand Canyon State and enjoys mostly bright skies throughout the year. It is the perfect place if you enjoy the outdoors, love sports, concerts and other big city amenities or technology. There are great neighborhoods around Phoenix, with easy access to a major city, nature, the arts and many more amenities.  

What You Will Do

Ensuring field instrumentation, including sensors and final process control elements such as valves and actuators, across the Americas remains reliable, safe, and fit for purpose throughout its full lifecycle—from initial deployment through operation, maintenance, and eventual retirement. This role is accountable for developing, enhancing, and implementing the strategy and technical standards that govern the selection, maintenance, monitoring, and replacement of instrumentation to consistently support safe, stable, and compliant operations. In partnership with site maintenance and operations leadership, the role establishes standardized work processes, performance indicators, and clear accountability across multiple locations, operating through influence within a matrixed organization to promote best practices, enable resource sharing, and drive cost‑effective, risk‑mitigating maintenance outcomes. Success is demonstrated through instrumentation systems that perform as designed, reduce unplanned failures, and deliver continuous availability of accurate, trusted operational data, including the effective adoption of innovative technologies that strengthen reliability, enhance asset health monitoring, and improve data‑driven decision making. You will align stakeholders on standardized field instrument deployment practices, deliver technical training on installation, commissioning, and configuration, and assess internal engineering and maintenance capacity to determine the need for third‑party technical services. In this role, you conduct instrumentation needs assessments across surface and underground mining assets, define key and operational performance indicators, and standardize sensor models, specifications, and installation procedures supported by complete, controlled technical documentation. As the Director Instrumentation Effectiveness, you monitor sensor lifecycle performance aligned with site asset management plans, establish end‑of‑life and decommissioning criteria, and implement proactive, risk‑based replacement strategies informed by condition monitoring, geotechnical risk, and reliability analysis. You utilize mine planning tools and digital twin environments to model instrumentation requirements, optimize deployment, and validate system integration. Implement standardized installation kits, interoperable integration platforms, and clear commissioning, testing, and acceptance criteria. Emphasize workforce training, role clarity, safety, and compliant end‑of‑life disposal practices. Implement criticality‑based inspections, condition monitoring, incident reporting workflows, and calibration routines. Leverage SAP, AI‑driven analytics, PlantESP, and mobile tools to support advanced sensor diagnostics, forecasting, and centralized configuration control, ensuring traceability, version control and consistent documentation. Support compliant retirement and replacement using asset, e‑waste, and procurement systems, and perform other duties as requested.

What You Bring To Freeport

Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering (or similar),
and
fifteen (15) years of maintenance experience in the mining industry,
including
mobile and fixed plant equipment

OR

Master’s Degree (M.Eng, M.Sc., MBA),
and
twelve (12) years of maintenance experience in the mining industry,
including
mobile and fixed plant equipment

Previous maintenance management experience

Experience leading and managing large, diverse work groups

Understanding and experience with SAP Maintenance Module

Knowledge and experience with CMMS programs

Working knowledge and experience with low and medium‑voltage Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs)

Strong working knowledge and experience with industrial instrumentation—selection, installation, configuration, calibration, maintenance, communication networks, and process control systems

Strong understanding of ISA standards 

Knowledge and experience with commissioning protocols

Experience implementing lifecycle programs for instrumentation field devices and systems

Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA) process knowledge and experience

Experience in financial and project management, including cost‑control methods

Understanding of mine and processing operational needs and requirements

Computer proficiency, including MIMS and Microsoft Office Suite

Knowledge of NEC, NESC, MSHA/OSHA legislation, and safety regulations

Preferred Qualifications

Working knowledge of applicable employmen

jobs.title: Engineer, Geotechnical (Fly-In Fly-Out)
jobs.description:
WHAT DOES AGNICO EAGLE VALUE?

At Agnico Eagle, our values never waver. We believe in trust, respect, equity, family and responsibility. Why? Because they express who we are, and they have helped us succeed in business for over 60 years. We value you - your unique set of skills and experience. We value your willingness to build those skills and make a meaningful contribution to our company. And, we value your commitment to treat every person on our team with respect, helping us to operate safely, protect the environment and make a positive contribution to our local communities.

ABOUT OUR OPERATION

Canadian-based and led, Agnico Eagle is Canada's largest mining company and the second largest gold producer in the world. It produces precious metals from operations in Canada, Australia, Finland and Mexico and has a pipeline of high-quality exploration and development projects. Agnico Eagle is a partner of choice within the mining industry, recognized globally for its leading sustainability practices. Agnico Eagle was founded in 1957 and has consistently created value for its shareholders, declaring a cash dividend every year since 1983.

Want to learn more about the Meadowbank Complex?
Click here
!

YOUR NEXT CHALLENGE:

Reporting to the Water Management & Geotechnical Engineering Supervisor, you will be part of the Environment and Critical Infrastructure Department. You will ensure that the goals and objectives are achieved while promoting and respecting Agnico Eagle’s values, Health & Safety Code of Conduct and the environment.

You will be responsible for the management and performance of dewatering systems, tailings storage facility dikes and dams, and associated infrastructure at both the Meadowbank and Whale Tail sites. The ideal candidate enjoys field-based work, technical problem-solving, and seeing projects through from concept to implementation. Working closely with a small but diverse team, you will identify challenges, develop practical engineering solutions, and lead the planning, design, and execution of projects that support the safe and efficient operation of critical water and tailings management infrastructure.

Ensure the performance of the tailings and water management infrastructure as per OMS manual procedure;

Perform field inspection and analyze geotechnical instrumentation data (i.e piezometers, thermistors);

Ensure internal and external recommended actions are implemented, following surveillance activities such as the Annual Dam Safety Inspection;

Prepare engineering documents (specifications, design report, drawings) for tailings deposition & water management infrastructure;

Design of various earthwork infrastructures as needed, such as channels, ditches, roads, culvert crossing, ponds, berms, finger dikes, and other remediation works;

Provide technical expertise and implement engineering solutions to ensure the performance of the water & tailings management infrastructure;

Project management, QA/QC, and as-built reporting for the construction and maintenance of water & tailings infrastructures;

Plan and coordinate geotechnical investigations and geotechnical instrumentation campaigns;

Plan and coordinate construction sequencing for progressive closure activities;

Plan tailings deposition activities with Muk3D software;

Analyze the performance of the tailings deposition to the deposition plan;

Project management of geotechnical mandates with consultants, including review of detailed design packages;

Prepare and present yearly Independent Review Board presentations;

Complete various projects assigned by the Water Management & Geotechnical Engineering Supervisor.

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED

Bachelor’s degree in Geological Engineering, Civil Engineering, Mining Engineering, or related field;

3-5 years of experience in geotechnical engineering applied to the mining industry;

Experience with earthwork construction and field work is a strong asset;

Experience with permafrost environment is considered an asset;

Knowledge of design software and computer assisted drawing software (CAD) is considered an asset;

Member of a Canadian Engineering society and eligible to NAPEG membership;

Excellent working knowledge of all Microsoft Office Suite applications especially Outlook, Excel, Word & PowerPoint.

Note that the official working language at Meadowbank Complex is English.

Your Work Schedule:

Schedule: 14 days of work, followed by 14 days for transportation and rest;

Accommodations and meals are provided on site at no cost to the employee. Agnico Eagle provides charter flights to and from the mine site and will accommodate to cover other travelling expenses according to your location of residence in Canada.

jobs.title: Analista de Business Intelligence (BI)
jobs.description:
¿Te apasiona analizar datos y descubrir lo que pueden decir sobre nuestros socios y el negocio?
En nuestra institución, el análisis de información es clave para comprender mejor a nuestros socios y generar información que facilite la toma de decisiones. Por eso, buscamos incorporar a nuestro equipo un Analista de Business Intelligence (BI) que disfrute investigar, analizar datos, desarrollar modelos y convertir información en recomendaciones.
Si te interesa llevar tu experiencia en análisis, modelado y visualización de datos a proyectos con impacto, este reto es para ti.
Sede: Blvd. Aeropuerto No. 843, Local. 103, Piso 1, Col. Predio Santa Anita, León, Guanajuato. C.P. 37295.
Modalidad: Teletrabajo de lunes a jueves y presencial los viernes.
Horario: Lunes a viernes de 9:00 a 18:00 hrs.
¿Qué harás en este reto?
Investigar y analizar información de nuestros socios y del entorno para comprender comportamientos, necesidades y tendencias.
Integrar y analizar información para atender las necesidades de las diferentes áreas.
Ejecutar estudios cuantitativos y generar conclusiones y recomendaciones a partir de sus resultados.
Desarrollar modelos descriptivos, predictivos y prescriptivos para anticipar comportamientos y apoyar iniciativas estratégicas.
Aplicar técnicas de minería de datos, georreferenciación y modelado predictivo para identificar patrones y oportunidades.
Crear herramientas y visualizaciones para monitorear KPIs y facilitar la interpretación de resultados.
Desarrollar soluciones automatizadas y aplicar Machine Learning e Inteligencia Artificial en proyectos de la institución.
Para este reto es importante contar con:
Licenciatura concluida en Matemáticas, Ciencia de Datos, Actuaría, Investigación de Mercados, Economía, Finanzas.
2 a 3 años de experiencia en análisis de información, inteligencia competitiva y de negocio, modelado y manejo de bases de datos.
Experiencia en estadística y pronósticos, con capacidad para interpretar información y generar recomendaciones.
Manejo de R a nivel medio y SQL a nivel básico.
Complementa tu perfil el manejo de herramientas como: Python · Power BI · Tableau · Qlik · SPSS.
¿Qué te ofrecemos?
Sueldo competitivo.
Prestaciones superiores a las de ley.
Estabilidad laboral en una institución con más de 70 años de trayectoria.
Oportunidades de crecimiento y desarrollo profesional.
Beneficios para ti y tu familia!
Si disfrutas encontrar lo que los datos están diciendo y convertirlo en información que ayude a tomar mejores decisiones, queremos conocerte.
¡Postúlate y forma parte de nuestro equipo!.

jobs.title: Technical Coordinator - Maintenance Support - Multiple Locations
jobs.description:
Freeport-McMoRan
is a leading international mining company with headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona. We operate large, long-lived, geographically diverse assets with significant proven and probable reserves of copper, gold, and molybdenum. The company has a dynamic portfolio of operating, expansion and growth projects in the copper industry. Freeport-McMoRan is one of the world’s largest publicly traded copper producers, the world’s largest producer of molybdenum and a significant gold producer. We have a long and successful history of conducting our business in a safe, highly efficient and socially-responsible manner.

We have the assets, the talent, the drive and the financial strength to provide attractive and rewarding careers of our employees. We encourage you to take the time to explore the opportunity to advance your career at Freeport-McMoRan.

What You Will Do

This position will be based in one of the following locations: Safford or Bagdad with expected travel to support other FMI locations. Travel frequency dependent on business needs

Acts as technical expert in general areas of past and present operations and maintenance. Provides technical expertise to support maintenance and commissioning/decommissioning. Will have broad and deep background, knowledge and understanding of industrial processes and associated equipment. 

Serves as a project lead and collaborates with maintenance/operations teams to achieve equipment reliability and run time. This work includes, but is not limited to, asset preservation, commissioning, and rebuilds. Team members may be internal or external (vendors or contractors). 

Reviews maintenance documentation for plant and equipment, to help identify potential and existing problems and facilitate maintenance best practices. Having identified a problem, determines the root cause and takes action to resolve and/or prevent production/maintenance issues. 

Collaborates with Planners, Operations, and others involved in the planning of critical maintenance activities. 

Champion safety and environmental processes to support and improve maintenance working practices. Mentor personnel on best practices (process, tooling, specifications, etc.) 

Collaborate to develop and utilize standard maintenance templates to achieve equipment reliability. 

Perform other duties as requested. 

What You Bring To Freeport

High school diploma or GED and seven (7) years journeyman level mechanical maintenance repair/rebuild experience with industrial equipment (pumps, motors, gearboxes, pulleys, etc.) including project management experience. 

Journeyman level ability to read, understand and apply information from technical manuals and other reference materials, including blueprints. 

Ability to add, subtract, multiply and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. 

Ability to work around industrial equipment safely, including all relevant adverse conditions, with all applicable PPE. 

Ability to manage multiple tasks and troubleshoot problems. 

Effective written, verbal, and communication skills to satisfy training, safety, and electronic message transmission policies of the company. 

Alignment training certification. 

Completed a Mechanical Maintenance Apprenticeship or equivalent.

Critera/Conditions

Ability to work any shift, including weekends and holidays (shifts may be rotating in a 24/7/365 operation).

At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing an employment package that recognizes excellence, encourages safe production and a culture supported by our core values. Where You Will Work    

Our global headquarters is in Phoenix, Arizona. Several hundred employees support global operations in finance, human resources, information technology, planning and more from the main office, satellite offices or online. As a Hybrid employee, you’ll engage in virtual collaboration as well as attend in-person meetings at our Collaboration Hub in Phoenix or at one of our site locations. The Collaboration Hub provides an open, flexible workspace for individuals and teams to come together for various business needs. Amenities at the Hub include a working café, phone booths and meeting rooms with technology tools for virtual and in-person collaboration. In-person attendance may vary based on the position and department requirements. 

Phoenix is the capital of the Grand Canyon State and enjoys mostly bright skies throughout the year. It is the perfect place if you enjoy the outdoors, love sports, concerts and other big city amenities or technology. There are great neighborhoods around Phoenix, with easy access to a major city, nature, the arts and many more amenities.  

What You Will Do

Under general supervision, provides technical support and guidance for environmental projects and programs at assigned site.

As the Environmental Scientist II, you install, operate, and maintain environmental and emission monitoring instruments and testing equipment and analyze data for compliance with regulatory requirements.

In this role, you evaluate and assess environmental risk and develop programs for risk reduction while collaborating in recommending appropriate action to management in compliance with regulations.

Review and/or prepare and maintain detailed records and files of environmental data and communications and evaluate and administer contracts with vendors for the provision of services and equipment.

You will maintain basic working knowledge of national, regional and local environmental, occupational health, and other applicable regulations, as well as knowledge of site environmental policies and procedures, and may provide leadership to less experienced engineers and technicians.

Serve as Project Manager or technical expert on small to medium-sized environmental projects such as compliance, remediation, or reclamation and lead or participate in regular audits and inspections of operational areas to ensure compliance with site environmental policies, procedures, and Environmental Management System requirements.

Coordinate the timely recycling and disposition of materials and other company assets in compliance with applicable legal and other requirements, track and report these activities as directed, and perform other duties as requested.

What You Bring To Freeport

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Technology, Earth Science or related natural science (such as Biology, Chemistry, Geology, Hydrology, Forestry, Agriculture, Meteorology, Environmental/Natural Resource Management) or Mathematics/Computer Science including Accounting and Finance, or Business Management or other Bachelor’s degree, and at least three (3) years environmental or related experience;
OR

Master’s degree in a related field and at least one (1) year environmental or related experience.

Additional certification or licensure appropriate to the job may be required or preferred including HAZWOPER, Method 9, DOT, EMS Auditor, Asbestos, Water Treatment Operator, or CHMM.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge or experience with Federal and Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado water quality regulation and programs including CWA, NPDES, APP, drinking water.

Familiarity with hydrogeologic field methods such as well installation, aquifer testing, water sampling.

Experience with data analysis, databases such as EQuIS and data validation.

Understanding of groundwater modeling software such as MODFLOW and FEFLOW.

Familiarity with well development techniques and well health programs.

Project management experience.

Strong communication and organizational skills.

Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

jobs.description:
Responsible for planning, implementing, and maintaining the technical and engineering aspects of underground mine ventilation systems. This role requires advanced analysis and conceptual expertise to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant operations. The incumbent will also mentor counterparts to support knowledge transfer, skill development, and continuous improvement.

Ensure strict adherence to all safety and environmental standards to minimize incidents and equipment damage.

Promote a proactive safety culture through consistent monitoring and guidance.

Coach, mentor, and motivate counterparts through structured on‑the‑job training (e.g., Pressure Quality Surveys) and other developmental programs.

Strengthen team competency in ventilation engineering and operational best practices.

Provide engineering solutions for underground fans, ventilation controls, and related systems, including design, installation, maintenance, QC/QA, cost estimation, and spare‑parts planning.

Lead or co‑lead air quality initiatives, including Diesel Particulate Matter (DPM) and dust‑reduction strategies, covering planning, procurement, and field execution.

Develop medium‑ and long‑term ventilation plans, including scientific calculations for shafts, drifts, fans, doors, and other requirements.

Build and calibrate mine ventilation models using tools such as Ventsim; validate simulations through field data comparisons

Prepare AFEs (Authorization for Expenditure) for capital projects with proper justification, forecasting, cost control, and compliance with company standards.

Manage administrative tasks related to capital projects, including construction QC, punch lists, commissioning documentation, and reporting.

Support project management tasks such as project scoping, tendering, product selection, and stakeholder coordination.

Evaluate and enhance the Ventilation On Demand (VOD) system, including optimization studies and rollout strategies.

.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mining, Mechatronics, Mechanical, Electrical, or similar), with a minimum of eight (8) years of relevant experience.

Strong understanding of environmental hazards, monitoring, and control strategies.

Ability to design and maintain sustainable underground ventilation systems.

Demonstrated capability in preparing AFEs, reports, and technical documentation.

Experience in project management and stakeholder coordination.

Ability to develop reports, conduct scenario analysis, and support decision‑making processes.

Familiarity with regulatory requirements and the ability to implement them in operational areas.

Proficiency with Ventsim or equivalent ventilation software.

Strong communication, presentation, leadership, and supervisory skills.

Ability to work effectively in a culturally diverse workforce.

Fluent in English (oral and written); willingness to learn Bahasa Indonesia.

Highly proactive, analytical, customer‑focused, and results‑oriented.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in engineering (Mining, Mechatronics, Mechanical, Electrical, or similar).

This position provides technical leadership across production allocation, measurement, emissions integration, regulatory compliance, commercial agreements, and reporting systems to ensure accurate and auditable allocation results that support operational, commercial, financial, and regulatory requirements. This role also drives standardization and continuous improvement across global LNG and Woodside assets.

Skills and Experience

Lead the design, implementation, and operation of LNG production allocation processes and systems. 

Ensure production allocation results are accurate, timely, reconciled, and compliant with corporate standards. 

Develop and maintain allocation methodologies aligned with joint venture agreements, LNG sales agreements, and commercial contracts. 

Provide governance and oversight of allocation calculations, reporting workflows, and data quality controls. 

Support month-end and year-end production accounting and reconciliation processes. 

Interface with Operations, Commercial, Marketing, Finance, Reserves, and Regulatory stakeholders regarding allocation matters. 

Project Delivery & Operational Readiness

Lead production allocation workstreams for LNG developments, brownfield expansions, and new asset startups. 

Manage allocation-related projects through concept, design, testing, commissioning, and operational handover phases. 

Coordinate business readiness activities to ensure allocation systems, procedures, and personnel are prepared for first production. 

Drive integration activities for acquisitions, divestments, and new venture opportunities. 

Develop project schedules, manage risks, and ensure milestone achievement. 

Act as business lead for production allocation systems, including Energy Components (EC), ECaaS, or equivalent solutions. 

Define business requirements and support system configuration, testing, and deployment. 

Lead system enhancements, automation initiatives, and reporting solutions. 

Work closely with digital, data, and vendor teams to optimize functionality and standardize global processes. 

Compliance, Assurance & Governance

Ensure compliance with internal policies, SOX controls, regulatory reporting requirements, and industry standards. 

Support internal and external audits related to production reporting and hydrocarbon accounting. 

Establish performance metrics, governance processes, and assurance frameworks. 

Maintain documentation, procedures, and allocation methodologies. 

Stakeholder Engagement

Build strong relationships with Operations, Engineering, Commercial, Finance, HSEC, and Technology teams. 

Facilitate alignment between project teams and business stakeholders. 

Provide technical mentorship to allocation specialists and analysts. 

Continuous Improvement

Identify opportunities to improve allocation accuracy, efficiency, and scalability. 

Standardize reporting and allocation practices across Woodside for LNG. 

Lead lessons-learned reviews and implementation of best practices. 

Support enterprise-wide initiatives related to production reporting, emissions reporting, and hydrocarbon accounting. 

Required Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Petroleum Engineering or related discipline. 

Experience

10+ years of experience in production allocation, hydrocarbon accounting, production reporting, or LNG operations. 

Experience supporting LNG facilities, gas processing plants, or upstream production assets. 

Demonstrated success leading complex projects and cross-functional initiatives. 

Experience implementing or supporting production allocation software platforms. 

Strong understanding of measurement, metering, production accounting, commercial agreements, and reporting

JOB DESCRIPTION

Title: Mine Surveyor A, B, or C

Reports To: Technical Manager, Conventional Operations

Dept: Technical Services FLSA Status: Exempt

GENERAL PURPOSE:

Energy Fuels is a leading producer of critical materials, including rare earth elements and uranium, with a growing domestic and international footprint.

Energy Fuels is seeking a Mine Surveyor to join our team. This role is responsible for delivering accurate survey data, maintaining survey control and producing reliable survey plans that support safe, efficient, and compliant mine development and production activities.

Why Join Energy Fuels

Direct exposure to leadership

Broad scope of responsibility across domestic and international operations

Competitive compensation and benefits, commensurate with experience

This position is based in Energy Fuels' La Sal Complex in La Sal, UT. A combination of fieldwork and office-based data processing. Work schedule may include extended hours or rotational shifts depending on operational needs, but typically is a standard 4-10 schedule.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

Perform underground and surface 3D as-built surveys using total stations and related survey equipment (Leica TS16/MS60 experience a plus)

Establish, verify, and maintain survey control

Execute layout for mining operations, including drill hole alignment, face drilling and blasting (azimuth, grade, and dimensions), and development reference lines

Survey completed development and production areas to ensure compliance with mine designs

Update and maintain survey drawings and mine plans using Vulcan/AutoCAD (or similar software)

Prepare monthly production reports, including development footage and volumetric calculations

Calculate volumes for ore, waste, and surface stockpiles

Provide survey support for mine planning, engineering, and geology teams

Assist in alignment and positioning of surface and underground exploration drilling

Ensure all work is conducted in compliance with company safety standards and MSHA regulations

Other duties as assigned

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS/EDUCATION/SKILLS:

Practical, solutions-oriented mindset with strong ownership and accountability

0-2 years of surveying experience, preferably in underground mining - for level C

3-7 years for level B

7+ years for level A

Bachelor's degree in Mining Engineering counts for 2 years of experience.

Valid Driver's License

Proficiency with survey equipment (total stations required, GPS and laser scanning a plus)

Experience with Vulcan or similar mine planning software preferred

Strong organizational and time management skills

Ability to work independently and adapt to changing field conditions

Solid mathematical, spatial reasoning, and data interpretation skills

Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy

Effective written and verbal communication skills

Working knowledge of safe work practices, MSHA standards, and hazard recognition

Demonstrated ability to work independently in active mining environments

PHYSICAL/SENSORY DEMANDS:

Ability to travel to company sites as needed

Ability to work in underground and surface environments, including confined spaces, uneven terrain, and varying weather conditions.

Must be able to lift 75lbs

Colorado Compliance Notices

Compensation Transparency (Colorado Compliance)

Salary Range:

$62,000 - $75,000 annually for level C

$76,000 - $95,000 annually for level B

$96,000 - $110,000 annually for level A

*Actual compensation may vary based on experience, qualifications, location, and internal equity.

Bonus Eligibility: This position may be eligible for an annual discretionary performance bonus.

Benefits

Medical, dental, and vision insurance

401(k) retirement plan with company match

Paid time off and company holidays

Life and disability insurance

Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Additional voluntary benefits may be available

jobs.description:
Introduction

Brunel is seeking a Project Manager to support the execution of large-scale mining and metallurgical process facilities projects. This is a contract, engineering home-office-based role located in Vancouver, Canada, with the potential to follow projects through site execution. The role will manage projects from early definition through commissioning, with a strong focus on health and safety, environmental performance, constructability, schedule, and cost control. Occasional travel to site in Indonesia may be required.

Responsibilities

Manage day-to-day execution of major mining and metallurgical process facilities projects from early project definition through field execution, commissioning, and handover to operations.

Lead project development activities including scope definition, execution planning, phasing strategies, scheduling, constructability reviews, and commissioning readiness.

Assemble and manage internal and external project resources to ensure accurate scope definition, cost estimates, and execution schedules.

Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities to ensure safe, compliant, and efficient project delivery.

Interface closely with corporate and site-based stakeholders including operations, supply chain, finance, environmental, risk management, and health and safety teams.

Secure and manage third-party engineering firms, consultants, contractors, and EPCM partners to support engineering studies, investigations, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities.

Establish project governance, communication plans, and productive working relationships across all project stakeholders.

Direct and monitor project team performance to ensure deliverables meet schedule, budget, quality, and safety requirements.

Work closely with project controls teams to monitor progress, manage budgets and schedules, and implement corrective actions as required.

Lead the development of execution strategies with a strong emphasis on constructability, QA/QC, and compliance with health, safety, environmental, and community requirements.

Implement comprehensive health, safety, and environmental programs and take accountability for project HSE performance.

Maintain full accountability for project cost, schedule, execution quality, contractor performance, and overall delivery outcomes.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related discipline with a minimum of eight (8) years of progressive experience in project and construction management; or

High School diploma or GED with a minimum of thirteen (13) years of progressive experience in project and construction management.

Demonstrated experience managing mining and metallurgical process facilities projects.

Strong knowledge of project management principles, engineering, project controls, procurement, contract administration, construction, and commissioning.

Proven ability to manage complex, large-scale projects with significant budget and schedule responsibility.

Proficiency with MS Word, Excel, Outlook, and general business systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing projects valued over USD $500M, particularly large mineral processing facilities.

EPCM and design office project management experience.

Heavy industrial construction project management background.

Experience with Lean Construction practices and advanced construction planning.

Experience managing large workforces and driving productivity and performance improvements.

Solid background in heavy machinery and industrial equipment installations.

Understanding of labour planning, forecasting, and workforce management.

Experience developing KPIs and tracking performance metrics.

Previous experience acting as an Owner's team representative.
