jobs.description:
En Mafort Service S.A.C. nos encontramos en la búsqueda de un Ingeniero Electricista con un perfil eminentemente técnico-operativo y de gestión. El rol requiere capacidad para participar directamente en campo, diagnosticar problemas complejos, y coordinar equipos técnicos y proveedores en proyectos de infraestructura eléctrica crítica, UPS y bancos de baterías.

No buscamos exclusivamente un profesional de diseño o administrativo; necesitamos un ingeniero capaz de pasar de la ingeniería a la ejecución bajo la premisa: Analizar, diagnosticar, planificar, ejecutar, supervisar, documentar.

Principales Responsabilidades

Supervisar y ejecutar proyectos de instalaciones eléctricas y sistemas UPS (monofásicos y trifásicos).
Realizar levantamientos técnicos en campo y elaborar informes detallados.
Revisar planos eléctricos, diagramas unifilares, especificaciones técnicas y memorias.
Coordinar instalaciones, pruebas, puesta en marcha y mantenimiento de UPS y bancos de baterías.
Supervisar trabajos de técnicos electricistas, contratistas y personal especializado.
Ejecutar y supervisar pruebas eléctricas, de transferencia, bypass, autonomía y funcionamiento.
Realizar diagnóstico avanzado de fallas en sistemas eléctricos y UPS.
Elaborar procedimientos de trabajo, protocolos de pruebas, dossiers técnicos y documentación de cierre.
Participar en reuniones técnicas con clientes, fabricantes (ej. Vertiv) y contratistas.

Requisitos Indispensables

Formación: Titulado y Colegiado en Ingeniería Electricista o Ingeniería Mecánica Electricista (habilitación profesional según requerimiento del proyecto).
Experiencia: Mínimo 5 años de experiencia general en instalaciones eléctricas, mantenimiento eléctrico, UPS o infraestructura crítica, con experiencia sólida y comprobada en campo.
Sistemas Críticos: Deseable experiencia en Data Centers, salas eléctricas, centros de datos, sector bancario, clínicas, minería o industria.

Conocimientos técnicos sólidos:

Sistemas UPS monofásicos y trifásicos (10 kVA a 600 kVA o superiores), bypass y transferencia.
Bancos de baterías (Norma IEEE 1188 para mantenimiento y evaluación VRLA).
Tableros eléctricos, sistemas de distribución, puesta a tierra y protección.
Lectura e interpretación de planos y diagramas unifilares.
Normativa: Familiaridad con normas IEC, IEEE y NFPA.

Herramientas y Software

AutoCAD: Nivel intermedio como mínimo.
Microsoft Office: Excel intermedio, Word y PowerPoint.
Planificación: MS Project u otras herramientas de gestión (deseable).
Manejo de instrumentos de medición eléctrica.

Competencias y Habilidades

Capacidad de diagnóstico y resolución de problemas.
Liderazgo técnico en campo.
Criterio técnico para la toma de decisiones.
Comunicación efectiva con clientes y capacidad de trabajar bajo presión.
Orientación a resultados y proactividad.

Horario: Lunes a viernes de 9:00 a.m. a 6:00 p.m. y sábados de 9:00 a.m. a 1:00 p.m.
Disponibilidad: Para visitas técnicas, supervisiones en campo, viajes a provincias y trabajos programados según la naturaleza del proyecto.
Lugar de trabajo: Empleo presencial en surco.

jobs.locationRaw: Springer Mine and Milling Complex, Imlay, Nevada, USA
jobs.description:
Position Title:
Environmental Services Technician

Department:
Operations

Reports To:
Site Services Superintendent

Position Summary

The Environmental Services Technician is responsible for maintaining clean, safe, and sanitary facilities across the Blue Moon Metals project site. This position performs routine cleaning, sanitation, and light facility support to ensure offices, shops, lunchrooms, restrooms, and common areas provide a safe and welcoming environment for employees, contractors, and visitors.

The successful candidate is dependable, detail-oriented, and committed to maintaining high standards of cleanliness while supporting Blue Moon Metals' safety-first culture.

Key Responsibilities

Clean and sanitize offices, restrooms, lunchrooms, meeting rooms, and other common areas.

Sweep, mop, vacuum, dust, and disinfect floors, furniture, fixtures, and high-touch surfaces.

Empty trash and recycling containers and dispose of waste in designated areas.

Restock restroom and breakroom supplies, including paper products, soap, and cleaning materials.

Clean windows, doors, and interior glass surfaces as needed.

Maintain clean and organized entrances, walkways, and common areas.

Assist with meeting room setup and cleanup for training sessions and company events.

Notify supervisors of maintenance needs, safety concerns, or damaged equipment.

Support housekeeping efforts in shops, warehouses, and other operational facilities as assigned.

Follow all Blue Moon Metals safety policies and procedures.

Safely use cleaning products, equipment, and personal protective equipment (PPE).

Maintain proper storage and handling of cleaning supplies and chemicals.

Report unsafe conditions, spills, or hazards promptly.

Promote a clean and organized workplace that supports safe operations.

Qualifications

Education

High school diploma or GED preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Previous janitorial, custodial, housekeeping, or facility cleaning experience preferred.

Experience in industrial, mining, construction, or commercial environments is an asset but not required.

Knowledge of standard cleaning methods, materials, and equipment.

Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.

Ability to work independently and manage daily responsibilities.

Good communication and teamwork skills.

Dependable, punctual, and committed to maintaining a professional work environment.

Physical Requirements & Work Environment

Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, and perform repetitive cleaning tasks throughout the shift.

Ability to lift and carry up to 40 pounds.

Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions when supporting site facilities.

Ability to safely wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).

Preferred Qualifications

Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.

Experience operating commercial cleaning equipment such as floor scrubbers or carpet cleaners.

jobs.title: Warehouse Technician
jobs.description:
Job Title: Warehouse and Logistics Operator

Location: Springer Tungsten Mine

Reporting Line: Materials Management & Warehouse Lead

The role requires a structured and hands-on operator responsible for supporting warehouse and logistics activities for both the project and future operations. The position ensures safe handling, storage, inventory control, and distribution of materials and equipment required for site activities. The role will develop into an operational position and will work closely with the Materials Management & Warehouse Lead to build competence, systems understanding, and best practices for long-term operations.

Scope & Accountability

Support receipt, storage, handling, and distribution of materials, equipment, and consumables

Verify incoming deliveries against purchase orders and report discrepancies

Perform safe handling of materials including mining equipment, spare parts, and consumables

Support implementation of inventory control principles (FIFO, stock levels, traceability)

Maintain accurate inventory records and stock levels in SAP

Support warehouse layout, storage optimization, and housekeeping

Assist with picking, packing, and issuing materials to construction and operations

Coordinate with logistics and expediting for receipt and tracking of deliveries

Participate in cycle counts and inventory verification activities

Support preservation and storage requirements for equipment and materials

Report damaged goods, discrepancies, or risks impacting inventory or operations

Ensure compliance with HSE, company procedures, and warehouse standards

Support continuous improvement of warehouse and logistics processes

Learn and develop competencies under guidance of Warehouse Lead

Submit warehouse and inventory reports as required.

Authorities

Execute warehouse and logistics activities within defined procedures

Stop or report unsafe handling or storage practices

Reject or report non-compliant deliveries and discrepancies

Ensure data accuracy in SAP for inventory and movements

Escalate risks impacting inventory, safety, or operations

Support enforcement of warehouse processes and standards

Initiate corrective actions for inventory discrepancies under guidance

Operate warehouse systems and tools within defined authority.

What We Offer

Competitive compensation and benefits package

Opportunity to work in a global, dynamic mining organization

Exposure to executive leadership and Board-level operations

Professional development and career growth opportunities

About the Company

Blue Moon is a junior mining company advancing 5 brownfield polymetallic projects, including the Nussir copper-gold-silver project in Norway, the NSG copper-zinc-gold-silver project in Norway, the Blue Moon zinc-gold-silver-copper project in the United States, the Springer tungsten-molybdenum project in the United States and the Apex germanium-gallium-copper in the United States.

With operations across multiple jurisdictions, we are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Corporate Secretary (Paralegal) to support our Board of Directors and legal function.

Pay range and compensation package

Compensation details will be discussed during the interview process.

Equal Opportunity Statement

We are committed to diversity and inclusivity in our hiring practices and encourage applications from all qualified individuals.

jobs.description:
Convocatoria Operadoras/es Mina Rajo - Plazo Fijo
 - 
División Andina

¿Quieres ser parte del desarrollo sostenible de Chile y el mundo?

¡Únete a la empresa más importante del país y construyamos juntos(as) la minería del futuro!

Nuestra estrategia de negocio es maximizar de forma competitiva y sustentable el valor económico de Codelco y su aporte al Estado de Chile. Si compartes nuestro propósito, te invitamos a participar del concurso

Convocatoria Operadoras/es Mina Rajo - Plazo Fijo

, para impulsar juntos(as) la transformación y sostenibilidad de nuestra Corporación.

Buscamos a personas comprometidas(os) con el progreso del país, líderes que desafíen el status quo, que muestren su mejor versión e impulsen el trabajo colaborativo para enfrentar el futuro de la compañía.

Diversidad e Inclusión

En Codelco estamos llamados a ser líderes en diversidad e inclusión por nuestro rol social y productivo para el país. En términos de equidad de género aspiramos alcanzar 35% de representación femenina al 2027 y generar igualdad de oportunidades para todas las personas, porque tenemos convicción en el valor de los equipos diversos (esta oferta se enmarca en la ley 21.015 que incentiva la inclusión de personas con discapacidad). 

¡Te invitamos a ser parte del mejor lugar para desarrollar tus talentos!

Propósito del Cargo:  

Desarrollar todas y cada una de las funciones requeridas para llevar adelante el proceso productivo de una mina rajo (operar equipos y otras funciones) aportando al máximo rendimiento de los activos, con seguridad, calidad y oportunidad. Velando por la calidad de vida de las personas y la sustentabilidad del negocio, ocupándose de cumplir y hacer cumplir las políticas, normas y procedimientos establecidos en la División y en la Corporación, relacionados con seguridad, salud ocupacional, medio ambiente y diversidad e inclusión.

¡Porque aquí el despliegue de tus talentos se pondrá al servicio De Chile!

Funciones Principales:

Desarrollar las tareas y operaciones necesarias para el proceso productivo de la mina.

Ejecutar correctamente las maniobras de posicionamiento y aculatamiento del CAEX en equipos de carguío, incluyendo palas eléctricas, palas hidráulicas y cargadores frontales, cumpliendo los estándares operacionales y de seguridad establecidos.

Operar los equipos mineros de acuerdo a estándares de seguridad y productividad establecidos en la operación Mina Rajo

Mantener contacto con su Supervisor y compañeros para coordinar actividades, solicitar apoyo, informar condiciones de riesgo o anomalías detectadas en el área de trabajo.

Detectar fallas en los equipos asignados, deteniendo el equipo en caso de peligro inminente o desperfecto que puedan ocasionar daños, e informando a su Supervisor oportunamente.

Cumplir con los procedimientos internos, reglamentos e instructivos establecidos para la operación minera en la Mina Rajo, así como las normas de calidad, seguridad y salud ocupacional y medio ambiente.

Realizar cualquier otra actividad de índole similar a los anteriores que su jefatura le requiera.

Requisitos de Postulación:

Titulado/a de al menos Enseñanza media completa.

Al menos 2 años de experiencia en la operación de camiones de extracción de alto tonelaje (280 toneladas mínimo), en mina rajo.

Licencia de conducir clase B vigente

Licencia de conducir clase D con al menos 2 años de antigüedad, comprobable.

Salud compatible con el cargo

Condiciones Ofrecidas:

Contrato: Temporal

.

Posibilidad de habitabilidad: División Andina podrá ofrecer alojamiento a las personas con residencia que vivan fuera de las comunas de Los Andes y San Felipe, sujeto a la disponibilidad del área.

Lugar de trabajo: División Andina

Jornada laboral: 4x4 rotativo de 12 horas, donde los primeros dos días del turno son de día y luego los últimos 2 días son de noche.

jobs.title: Specialist Operations & Maintenance
jobs.description:
About BHP

At BHP we support our people to grow, learn, develop their skills and reach their potential.

With a global portfolio of operations, we offer a diverse and inclusive environment with extraordinary career opportunities.  Our strategy is to focus on creating a safe work environment where our employees feel strongly connected to our values and objectives, and where the capability of our people is key to our success.

Come and be a part of this success.

Why BHP?

At BHP, we are transforming the way mining is done. We embrace innovation, sustainability, and inclusion to build a smarter, safer, and more human future. 

We are proud to be recognized as 
one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers for 2026
, a testament to our dedication to fostering a positive, diverse, and rewarding work environment. At BHP, you’ll be part of a team that values safety, integrity, performance, and collaboration.

Work Location

This role will be based in Elliot Lake, Ontario, Canada.  

BHP offers domestic relocation assistance to support the successful incumbent in transitioning, if required. Benefits offered as part of the relocation program include (but are not limited to) new home purchase assistance, temporary accommodations, home finding trip and a resettlement allowance. 

Total Rewards

The starting annual salary range for this role is $115,000 - 144,000 CAD.  Additional rewards includes a short-term incentive bonus program, health plan, personal spending account, dental, life insurance, and pension.

The Challenge Ahead

This role will support the Operations and Maintenance Lead in the management of the Legacy Assets sites in Elliot Lake. The successful candidate provides support through coordination across line and functional teams. The position is based in Elliot Lake, Ontario, Canada.

In this role you will:

Saraji Mine are seeking capable, and safety‑minded High Voltage Electricians who are ready to take the next step in their career. You'll play a key role in keeping our operation running smoothly by carrying out inspections, preventative maintenance, and repairs on our heavy field mining equipment.

Key Duties:

Performing preventative and breakdown maintenance on surface field mining equipment, including draglines and electric shovels.

Performing preventative and breakdown maintenance on High Voltage infrastructure and systems.

Diagnosing faults and conducting repairs and servicing on surface field equipment.

Supporting continuous improvement through proactive problem solving.

A strong commitment to safety and looking out for your teammates

Strong diagnostic and troubleshooting capabilities

QLD Electrical Fitter/Mechanic licence

High Voltage switching qualification and demonstrated experience in HV operations

Sound knowledge of electrical safety legislation, standards and isolation procedures

Demonstrated prior experience working with draglines/rope shovels and electrical infrastructure.

About Our Process 

At BHP, we are committed to employing individuals who align with the BHP Charter Values and meet the requirements of the role. As part of the recruitment process, there are a number of checks which may be conducted to demonstrate applicants suitability for a role including police / criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks, and/or reference checks. 

Please note as part of this recruitment process the successful applicant will need to conduct a Queensland legislated coal mine workers’ health assessment.

The size, stability and magnitude of our business not only provides significant opportunity for professional development, but also attractive salary packages with performance-based bonuses and a best-in-class employee share program. These benefits include flexible working options, a generous paid parental leave policy, other extended leave entitlements and parent rooms.  

At BHP, we know that we are strengthened by diversity. We are an Equal Opportunity employer that is committed to making BHP a safe and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive and be at their best every day. We are focused on creating a workforce that’s more diverse and represents the communities where we work and live. providing a work environment in which everyone is included, treated fairly and with respect. We are an Equal Opportunity employer and recognise that true diversity includes gender, age, race, disability status, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, education levels, and many more aspects of your identity.

BHP is committed to providing a recruitment process that is fair, equitable and accessible for all. If you have a disability, we know that it may be helpful for us to adjust our process to make it equitable for your individual situation. If you would like to reach out to someone about your situation and our recruitment process, please email us at 

inclusion@bhp.com

.

jobs.title: Environmental Engineer II
jobs.description:
Why You Should Apply for This Job  

At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing an employment package that recognizes excellence, encourages safe production and a culture supported by our core values. Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority, all opinions are valued, and people are empowered to grow in their career.
Apply Today!

Where You Will Work    

Our global headquarters is in Phoenix, Arizona. Several hundred employees support global operations in finance, human resources, information technology, planning and more from the main office, satellite offices or online. As a Hybrid employee, you’ll engage in virtual collaboration as well as attend in-person meetings at our Collaboration Hub in Phoenix or at one of our site locations. The Collaboration Hub provides an open, flexible workspace for individuals and teams to come together for various business needs. Amenities at the Hub include a working café, phone booths and meeting rooms with technology tools for virtual and in-person collaboration. In-person attendance may vary based on the position and department requirements. 

Phoenix is the capital of the Grand Canyon State and enjoys mostly bright skies throughout the year. It is the perfect place if you enjoy the outdoors, love sports, concerts and other big city amenities or technology. There are great neighborhoods around Phoenix, with easy access to a major city, nature, the arts and many more amenities.  

What You Will Do

Under general supervision, provides technical support and guidance for environmental projects and programs at assigned site.

As the Environmental Engineer II, you install, operate, and maintain environmental and emission monitoring instruments and testing equipment and analyze data for compliance with regulatory requirements.

Evaluate and assess environmental risk and develop programs for risk reduction while collaborating in recommending appropriate action to management in compliance with regulations.

In this role, you review and/or prepare and maintain detailed records and files of environmental data and communications and evaluate and administer contracts with vendors for the provision of services and equipment.

You will maintain basic working knowledge of national, regional and local environmental, occupational health, and other applicable regulations, as well as knowledge of site environmental policies and procedures.

Provide leadership to less experienced engineers and technicians and may serve as Project Manager or technical expert on small to medium-sized environmental projects such as compliance, remediation, or reclamation.

Lead or participate in regular audits and inspections of operations areas to ensure compliance with site environmental policies, procedures, and Environmental Management System requirements.

Coordinate the timely recycling and disposition of materials and other company assets in compliance with applicable legal and other requirements and track and report these activities as directed.

Perform other duties as assigned.

What You Bring To Freeport

Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Environmental, Civil, Chemical, Agricultural, Mining, Metallurgical, Geological or similar)
and
at least three (3) years environmental or related experience;
OR

Master’s degree in Engineering in a related field 
and
at least one (1) year environmental or related experience.

Additional certification or licensure appropriate to the job may be required or preferred such as HAZWOPER, Method 9, DOT, EMS Auditor, Asbestos, Water Treatment Operator, or CHMM.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge or experience with Federal and Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado water quality regulation and programs including CWA, NPDES, APP, drinking water.

Familiarity with hydrogeologic field methods such as well installation, aquifer testing, water sampling.

Experience with data analysis, databases such as EQuIS and data validation.

Understanding of groundwater modeling software such as MODFLOW and FEFLOW.

Familiarity with well development techniques and well health programs.

Project management experience.

Strong communication and organizational skills.

Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

Willingness to travel and perform fieldwork under varying conditions.

jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location:
Christmas Creek – Fortescue’s Christmas Creek mine is located on the traditional lands of the Nyiyaparli peoples. 

Roster:
8D/6R FIFO ex Perth

We are seeking a highly motivated Mine Surveyor to join the Operations Planning team at Christmas Creek. Reporting to the Senior Mine Surveyor, you will use innovative surveying technologies including RPAS and laser scanning tools to safely, accurately and efficiently capture and supply spatial data to support mining operations.

This role will suit someone with strong technical capability, attention to detail and excellent interpersonal, communication and teamwork skills. 

Key Responsibilities

Complete weekly and monthly survey deliverables, including pit and waste as-built models.

Undertake design checks and resource definition surveys.

Complete machine calibrations and environmental surveys.

Conduct end-of-month surveys and volumetric reconciliation processing.

Capture and provide accurate spatial data to support operational requirements.

Utilise RPAS and laser scanning technology to complete survey activities.

Ensure all survey equipment is maintained, serviceable and operating within required tolerances.

Bachelor’s degree, Advanced Diploma or equivalent qualification in Surveying.

Experience working in large-scale open pit mining environments.

Current WA C-Class Driver’s Licence.

Remote Pilot Licence (RePL) and Aeronautical Radio Operator Certificate (AROC) are desirable.

Proficiency in Trimble GPS and Leica Total Stations.

Experience using DJI RPAS and laser scanning technologies.

Proficiency in Maptek Vulcan and PointStudio.

Experience using Agisoft, Terrain and Microsoft Excel.

Strong interpersonal, communication and teamwork skills.

jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location: 
Fortescue’s Solomon mine is located on the traditional lands of the Eastern Guruma and Yindjibarndi peoples.

Roster:
8D6R7N7R - FIFO ex Perth

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for experienced High Voltage Electricians looking to work on large-scale electric mining equipment and play a key part in the transition to a greener, more technology-driven fleet.

Reporting directly to the High Voltage Electrical Supervisor, you will be responsible for managing the high voltage power supply to 9400E Excavators and PV271E Pit Viper Drill Rigs, working closely with mining operations and cable handling teams to keep critical production equipment running safely and efficiently.

You will be trusted to carry out high voltage switching, statutory inspections, fault finding, repairs, and compliance activities across the mining fleet, with a strong focus on safety, quality, reliability, and machine availability.

Key Responsibilities

Support the transition to the incoming green fleet by developing new skills, embracing emerging technology, and contributing to a high-performing maintenance team as the site moves toward a larger battery-electric and low-emissions mining fleet.

Safely energise and de-energise high voltage power supply to 9400E Excavators and PV271E Pit Viper Drill Rigs.

Ensure all statutory testing, inspections, and compliance checks are completed on relevant high voltage assets.

Diagnose faults and respond to breakdowns efficiently to reduce downtime and optimise machine availability.

Maintain, inspect, and support new fixed electrical infrastructure associated with the green fleet transition, including charging stations, high voltage supply systems, distribution equipment, and associated protection systems.

Work closely with mining operations and cable handling teams to maintain safe working conditions for personnel and mobile equipment operating in proximity to high voltage trailing cables and power supply systems.

Verify that safety controls are in place, effective, and fully compliant with statutory inspection and testing requirements.

Collaborate with mobile maintenance and cable management teams to support safe execution of work and achieve schedule compliance.

Qualifications and Experience

A Grade Western Australian Electrical Licence.

Current High Voltage Switching Ticket.

Demonstrated high voltage switching experience.

Experience working safely in small teams on critical-path maintenance activities.

Experience with electric HME, fixed electrical infrastructure, charging systems, or battery-electric equipment will be highly regarded.

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location: 
Perth - Fortescue's Perth office is located on the traditional lands of the Whadjuk Noongar people.

Roster: 
Monday to Friday.

As an AI Engineer within Fortescue’s Data & AI Platform team, you will help design, build and operate secure, scalable AI solutions and platform capabilities across machine learning, generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agentic workflows. 

You will translate business problems into production-ready solutions, develop reusable services and integrations, and support end-to-end MLOps and LLMOps. Working closely with data scientists, engineers, architects, cyber security, product and operational teams, you will balance delivery speed with reliability, governance, cost and measurable business value.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and maintain reusable AI components, APIs, microservices, model-serving capabilities and orchestration patterns.

Implement machine learning, generative AI and RAG solutions using architectures appropriate to the business need.

Build capabilities for automated testing, deployment, evaluation, monitoring, cost management and lifecycle management across MLOps and LLMOps.

Design and implement bounded agentic workflows using approved enterprise data, tools and APIs.

Apply appropriate patterns for tool calling, context and state management, orchestration, human approval, guardrails and safe fallback behaviour.

Evaluate and monitor AI and agent workflows for task success, reliability, safety, latency, cost and operational value.

Integrate AI services and agents into enterprise business workflows in alignment with architecture, cyber security, data governance and responsible AI requirements.

Build secure integrations using appropriate identity, authorisation, secrets management, least-privilege access and auditability controls.

Prototype and experiment to validate technical feasibility, user value and operational impact before scaling solutions.

Monitor and troubleshoot production AI services, support incident resolution, assess emerging technologies and contribute reusable patterns and operational procedures.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Minimum 2+ years’ experience designing, developing and delivering AI/ML or cloud-native software systems, including solutions from prototype through to production.

Proficiency in Python, including clean code, testing, API development, debugging and software design fundamentals.

Practical understanding of machine learning and LLM concepts, model APIs, prompting, structured outputs, embeddings, vector search and RAG.

Practical experience or strong applied understanding of agentic systems, including tool/function calling, workflow orchestration, context or state management, guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls.

Experience evaluating AI quality and reliability, monitoring production behaviour, tracing model and tool activity, and managing latency, configuration and cost trade-offs.

Working knowledge of AWS or Azure, containers, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, automated testing and observability practices.

Experience with SQL, data pipelines, object storage, REST APIs, event-driven or microservices architectures and governed enterprise data integration.

Understanding of authentication, authorisation, secrets management, data privacy, secure tool use, AI risk controls and responsible deployment practices.

Strong analytical, systems-thinking, problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across disciplines and communicate technical options, risks, costs and outcomes clearly.

About Us

Be part of something big. Fortescue is leading the world with our plan to decarbonise our iron ore operations, projects that harness renewable energy and the development of technology that will change our planet forever.

The Operations Superintendent is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the Louisiana LNG Plant. Demonstrated skills to identify, report on and resolve project and people strategic issues.

jobs.description:
WHAT DOES AGNICO EAGLE VALUE?

At Agnico Eagle, our values never waver. We believe in trust, respect, equity, family and responsibility. Why? Because they express who we are, and they have helped us succeed in business for over 60 years. We value
you
- your unique set of skills and experience. We value your willingness to build those skills and make a meaningful contribution to our company. And, we value your commitment to treat every person on our team with respect, helping us to operate safely, protect the environment and make a positive contribution to our local communities.

ABOUT OUR OPERATION

Canadian-based and led, Agnico Eagle is Canada's largest mining company and the second largest gold producer in the world. It produces precious metals from operations in Canada, Australia, Finland and Mexico and has a pipeline of high-quality exploration and development projects. Agnico Eagle is a partner of choice within the mining industry, recognized globally for its leading sustainability practices. Agnico Eagle was founded in 1957 and has consistently created value for its shareholders, declaring a cash dividend every year since 1983.

The Support and Development Center provide services to Agnico Eagle's various Canadian and / or international mining operations in a variety of areas, including administration, financial services, IT, supply chain, human resources, communications, construction as well as technical services (geology, engineering, metallurgy, infrastructure, marketing, innovation, and digital transformation).

YOUR NEXT CHALLENGE:

Reporting to the Superintendent of H&S Construction, the candidate will play a vital role in ensuring worker safety and compliance with safety standards during the construction phases of mining projects. Assisting the Canadian health and safety teams throughout all phases of construction. This position requires strong communication skills to interact with various stakeholders, contractors, site supervisors, project managers. In addition, the H&S Coordinator will collaborate closely with multiple teams across all construction projects to develop synergies, improve processes and optimize the use of existing tools.

Responsibilities:

Safety Planning and Implementation: Assist in developing and implementing safety corrective action plans based on the needs of each site

Inspection, Audit and Monitoring: Conduct regular inspections/audits of construction sites to identify potential hazards and ensure proper use of safety equipment. Monitor work practices to ensure compliance with safety protocols.

Coordination with Construction Teams: Work closely with site H&S site Coordinators, Site managers and other construction team members to Ensure all construction activities comply with established safety standards.

Incident Management: Support investigations in the event of an accident or incident on the construction site to determine the causes and implement corrective measures.

Continuous Improvement: Analyze safety BBO’s data and trends to identify activities or areas for improvement. Support in the implementation of continuous safety initiatives to reduce risks.

Reporting and Documentation: Assisting for accurate documentation of safety activities, inspections, incidents, and training.

Risk Management and Monitoring System (RMMS): Oversee the implementation and engagement of RMMS thru our project by identifying actions to be putted in place to comply with the company expectation.

Risk Assessment: Conduct and/or assist detailed risk assessments for each construction project to identify potential hazards and implement preventative measures.

Promoting Safety Culture: Encourage a proactive safety culture among workers by rewarding safe behaviors and emphasizing the importance of safety in all construction activities.

Training and Awareness: Support construction management of all sites to organize training sessions for to inform them of specific construction-related hazards, new regulation and appropriate safe practices.

#L1-WA1

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED

Certificate in Occupational Health & Safety

Minimum of 5 years industrial construction project.

Essential for interacting with various stakeholders, contractors, team supervisors, and project managers.

Working closely with multiple teams across all construction projects to develop synergies, improve processes, and optimize the use of existing tools.

Prioritizing proactive management to ensure safety measures are always ahead of potential risks.

Travel to sites will be required.

Compensation Statement

In accordance with applicable legislation, the expected compensation includes base salary and potential bonus opportunity. Your individual pay will reflect your skills and experience while remaining competitive within the local market.

jobs.title: Specialist, Treasury - 12 Month FTC
jobs.description:
The strategy of Anglo American is to secure, develop and operate a portfolio of high quality and long-life resource assets to deliver leading shareholder returns. This can be achieved through innovative practices and technologies, in the hands of our world-class people, working towards a common purpose of re-imagining mining to improve people’s lives.

Treasury technology, process improvement and effective governance are key enablers of Treasury’s objectives, helping to improve efficiency, resilience and business insight. The Treasury Consultant will support these objectives by providing specialist treasury expertise, project delivery capability and practical experience across Treasury Management Systems, treasury accounting, controls and reporting.

Safety, Health & Environment

Demonstrate behaviour in line with health, safety and environmental standards and with the Group's values.

Participate in relevant safety initiatives and address matters appropriately as part of demonstrating safety leadership.

Performance & Delivery – Treasury Systems & Technical Expertise

Act as a key subject matter expert for Treasury Management Systems with knowledge of a range of treasury technology products including FIS Quantum.

Provide specialist guidance on Treasury Management System capabilities, configuration, controls, accounting set-up, data management and reporting in line with leading practices.

Support the effective management of Treasury Management Systems and associated applications.

Provide specialist expertise across the end-to-end Treasury workflow, from Treasury Front Office exposure identification and deal execution through to Treasury Operations and accounting, including reporting.

Work closely with Treasury colleagues and other internal stakeholders as well as external providers to ensure Treasury technology solutions continue to meet business requirements.

Support knowledge transfer and the embedding of sustainable treasury process and technology capability across the function.

Performance & Delivery – Treasury Project Delivery

Lead and support Treasury projects and transformation initiatives.

Manage project plans, governance materials, risks, dependencies, actions and stakeholder communications.

Coordinate activities across Treasury, Finance, Technology teams, vendors and implementation partners.

Support business requirements gathering, solution design, testing, training, implementation and post-implementation review activities.

Ensure project delivery is aligned to agreed objectives, governance requirements and operational control standards.

Support Treasury transformation initiatives leveraging technology to improve efficiency, governance and operational effectiveness.

Ensure project outcomes are embedded through clear documentation, user training, knowledge transfer and effective handover to Treasury teams.

Sustainability & Social

Support Group Treasury initiatives aligned with the Group Finance agenda and wider business priorities.

People & Teams

Identify and agree own training and development requirements.

Demonstrate behaviour in line with the Group's values, standards and a professional workplace.

Build strong collaborative relationships with Treasury, Finance, Technology and external stakeholders.

Share expertise with colleagues and contribute to a constructive and productive working environment.

Compliance

Ensure Treasury processes remain aligned with Group Treasury Policy and relevant governance requirements.

Support the design, operation and enhancement of Treasury controls, including ICFR and related control frameworks where applicable.

Support internal and external audit activities through provision of appropriate documentation and evidence.

Promote appropriate segregation of duties, access governance, audit trail quality and control evidence across Treasury processes and technology-enabled activities.

Significant Corporate Treasury experience within a large multinational organisation.

Demonstrable experience implementing, enhancing or managing Treasury Management Systems.

Strong hands-on experience with FIS Quantum and/or other Treasury Management Systems such as FIS Integrity, Kyriba, Reval, IT2 or equivalent.

Experience supporting Treasury Management Systems in a live corporate environment, including configuration, controls, reporting, workflows and process design.

Proven project management experience delivering Treasury transformation or technology-enabled initiatives.

Strong understanding of treasury operations, cash and liquidity management, financial risk management, treasury controls and reporting.

Strong treasury accounting knowledge and knowledge of TMS configuration.

Experience working with software vendors, implementation partners and cross-functional business teams.

Strong skills in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel.

At Anglo American, we’re redefining what it means to mine responsibly. We lead with integrity, care deeply about people and the planet, and constantly push the boundaries of innovation to work safer and smarter. From reducing water and energy use to pioneering precision extraction technologies, we’re committed to sustainable practices that deliver real impact—today and for generations to come.

jobs.title: Shift Engineer (Electrical)
jobs.description:
Engineering for a better future.

Anglo American Australia

Grosvenor Mine – an underground steelmaking coal mine produced its first longwall coal in May 2016 and is located in Moranbah, about 190 km south-west of Mackay.

We are building the team to deliver the next chapter of Grosvenor Mine. With a planned return to longwall production by Q4 2027, this is a unique opportunity to contribute to a major mine restart and help shape the future of underground mining.

Working alongside experienced professionals, you will play a role in implementing leading-edge technology, automation, monitoring systems and operational improvements that will define how the mine operates for years to come.

Grosvenor Mine is seeking an experienced Shift Engineer (electrical) to support the engineering and maintenance team on-site. Reporting into the Engineering Superintendent, you will primarily be involved in the coordination of planned and unplanned maintenance activities, to ensure shift safety and production targets are delivered.

You will be accountable to provide effective technical support, shift management, shift reporting, work quality management, escalation & response, and supervision of trades personnel to optimize our assets and deliver the mine plan.

Your key responsibilities include:

Monitor performance against the plan and lead the trade supervisors to identify maintenance and engineering risks to delivering the mine plan.

Commit to the quality of engineering services delivered and deliver fit-for-purpose equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical/design and practicality at the face.

Identify improvements and/or corrective activities that will reduce the operating costs.

Maintain & monitor performance of maintenance activities with short interval control (SIC).

Issue work orders to trades personnel and receive completed work orders and shift reports, following that, review and raise actions for any priority works.

Audit quality of trades workmanship and completion of maintenance work orders.

Respond to unplanned variance and breakdowns on shifts.

Conduct preliminary RCAs on breakdowns.

Support departments to achieve business plan through engagement and continual process improvement

To be successful in the role you will have to have the following:

Valid QLD Electrical License

Hold the supervisor qualifications (S1, S2, S3) & G2

Previous experience in a mining maintenance role (preferably Coal) or heavy industry

Demonstrated experience leading a team of professionals to deliver against set targets

Experience in driving best practice through your department and into the business

Track record in driving continuous improvement

Full-time permanent position based at Grosvenor Mine, Moranbah QLD

Attractive 7 on, 7 off roster

Competitive salary package and annual bonus incentive programs

Residential, FIFO (company funded) & DIDO options

Subsidised accommodation and company funded camp options provided

Several conveniently timed, daily bus transfers from the airport to camp and onto site

Novated lease available

Domestic Relocation assistance to Moranbah township

What we Offer

When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package and a range of flexible work arrangements that support the balance of work, family and individual circumstances. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programmes, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too. We’re a large, successful multinational company – and we’re still growing all the time.

Who we are

We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies. As the custodians of coal and other precious natural resources – diamonds (through De Beers), copper, platinum and other precious metals, iron ore and nickel – our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively, with the utmost consideration for local communities, our customers and the world at large.

Background checks

Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

Inclusion and Diversity

Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How we are committed to your safety

Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies – from drones to data analytics – that are helping to make mining safer.

How to apply

To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. You will have the opportunity to upload your CV and other relevant documentation as part of this process.

CLOSING DATE

11 September 2026

Please note, screening and interviews may take place prior to closing date – applications may also close before this date.

jobs.title: Specialist Closure Planning | Mt Arthur Coal | NSWEC
jobs.description:
About BHP

At BHP we support our people to grow, learn, develop their skills and reach their potential.

With a global portfolio of operations, we offer a diverse and inclusive environment with extraordinary career opportunities. Our strategy is to focus on creating a safe work environment where our employees feel strongly connected to our values and objectives, and where the capability of our people is key to our success.

Come and be a part of this success.

About Mt Arthur Coal

Mt Arthur Coal is an open-cut coal mine 100 per cent owned by BHP. Located in the Hunter Valley, New South Wales it's the largest producer of energy coal in the region, operating alongside olive growers, wine makers, horse breeders and the nearby residential community of Muswellbrook.
Our greatest asset is and has always been our people and communities, which is why we are committed to working together on our Pathway to 2030 - a program to responsibly close Mt Arthur Coal. We are about doing the right thing and working with everyone to co-create a shared vision for the future of the region.

About the Role

This role, reporting to the Superintendent Closure Planning and environment, you will specifically:

Support team delivery of technical and other closure related studies.

Undertake routine data analysis and technical report reviews.

Support reporting and internal governance processes.

Contribute to reviews / updates of site Closure Plans.

Contribute to the development and positive culture of the Closure Planning function.

About You

To be successful in this role you shall possess:

A Bachelor of Science or Engineering in a relevant discipline.

Relevant project management and mining / project experience.

Effective interpersonal skills.

Energy to inspire and engage those around you.

Pathway to 2030 – be part of the legacy

Mt Arthur Coal is progressing toward a planned cessation of mining in 2030, with a clear focus on responsible operations, safe delivery and thoughtful transition planning.

This role offers a rare opportunity to:

•    Be part of the legacy of one of NSW’s most significant mining operations
•    Build your career through involvement in a mine closure process
•    Contribute to rehabilitation planning and the transition of the site to its next productive land use
•    Help define what “good” looks like in late life operations and responsible closure

Working at an open-cut coal mine like Mt Arthur Coal involves certain risks, including operating in or around heavy machinery, exposure to environmental hazards such as tailings dams, and managing fatigue from long or night shifts. Before applying, please ensure you understand these risks and can commit to following all safety requirements and procedures designed to keep you and others safe.

About Our Process

At BHP, we are committed to employing individuals who align with the BHP Charter Values and meet the requirements of the role. As part of the recruitment process, there are a number of checks which may be conducted to demonstrate applicants suitability for a role including police / criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks, and/or reference checks.

The historic Chino mine was among the world's first low-grade, open-pit copper mines. Today, the operation consists of a 36,000-metric-ton-per-day concentrator that produces copper and a 150-million-pound-per-year solvent extraction/electrowinning plant that produces copper cathode from solution generated by run-of-mine leaching.

Climax Molybdenum is the world’s leading producer of molybdenum and has a long, successful history of doing business safely, efficiently and responsibly. We have operated in Colorado for more than 100 years, with mining and milling operations near Leadville, Kremmling and Empire. Our Climax Mine is located between Frisco and Leadville – the seat of Lake County and the highest incorporated city in the United States.

Employees who are required to work on-site are eligible for a $1,450 monthly housing allowance, provided they meet program guidelines.   

At an elevation of over 10,000 feet, the rich historic town of Leadville is surrounded by snow-capped mountains. Our employees and their families can enjoy hiking, camping, ultramarathon activities, skiing, and boating in the area. Some attractions in Leadville include the National Mining Hall of Fame and Museum, Ski Cooper, Tennessee Pass Cookhouse, Tabor Opera House and the Leadville National Fish Hatchery. Perform other duties as needed.

Description

Highly skilled worker who under general supervision safely performs duties related to the smelting of metals from ore in various areas of the plant.

Completes duties within assigned area or areas that could include the utility area, the Isa, the electric furnace, the converters, the anode plant and the acid plant

Responsibilities within the
Isa smelting vessel area
include:

Operating tapping machines and belting systems

Working on and around an industrial boiler 

Responsibilities within the
electric furnace area
include:

Operating tapping machines

Operating a slag hauler (cress)

Cleaning launders which are used for molten metal transfers

Working around ventilation equipment which includes fans and scrubbers

Working with electrode-hydraulic systems

Performing housekeeping and minor maintenance activities such as troubleshooting equipment for smelter maintenance mechanics

Responsibilities within the
converter area
include:

Running belt systems

Handling silica flux and reverts

Operating a rotary furnace converter

Responsibilities within the
anode plant
include:

Working on water systems, casting systems, hydraulic systems, and refining processes

Responsibilities within the
acid plant
include:

Assisting with, and performing the starting and stopping of valves and pumps

Opening and closing valves

Acid stream sample retrieval

Analyzing samples for acid strength

Processing and analyzing samples in onsite lab

Responsibilities within the
utility area
include:

Unloading railcars that contain copper concentrate

Unloading bulk bags with various recycled materials such as foundry sands, precious metal scraps, and sludges that contain copper or precious metals

Managing truck unloading of copper concentrate, revert material, and silica

Transferring materials via belt systems that are distributed to different areas within the smelter

May assist with maintenance activities such as changing valves and piping

May operate skid-steer loaders, front-end loaders, 35 ton haul trucks, 75 ton overhead cranes, track excavators, forklifts, graders, water trucks, and vacuum trucks

Mentor and train fellow employees

Modify and create smelter operations standard operating procedures (SOP's)

Acts as a Fill-in Supervisor as needed

At least 2 (two) years of experience in trade

Possess good communication skills

Ability to understand and apply verbal and written work and safety-related instructions and procedures given in English

Ability to communicate in English with respect to job assignments, job procedures, and applicable safety standards

Work is performed in a mine or manufacturing plant setting, which may include exposure to extremes in temperature and humidity, moving mechanical parts, risk of electrical shock, toxic chemicals, explosives, fumes or airborne particles

Reporting to the Global Communities and Local Content Manager, you will support the delivery of socio-economic studies, social performance management plans and community initiatives across Fortescue’s global portfolio of projects.

You will also contribute to the implementation of Fortescue’s communities policies and standards, ensuring our approach reflects international best practice.

Key Responsibilities

Support the implementation of Fortescue’s communities policies and standards.

Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

Support stakeholder engagement, grievance management and accurate record keeping.

Contribute to the development and delivery of local content and community investment initiatives.

Support the engagement and management of social performance consultants, including developing scopes of work, assessing proposals and monitoring delivery against budget, schedule and agreed outcomes.

Coordinate communities team deliverables for projects and maintain effective interfaces with internal stakeholders.

Undertake research to identify social risks and opportunities during early project development and project bids.

Develop innovative solutions and identify improved ways of working to strengthen social performance management.

Support the preparation and delivery of social performance studies and associated management plans.

Qualifications and Experience

5–7 years’ experience in social performance, community development or a related field.

Experience designing, developing and delivering social performance and management plans, such as stakeholder engagement plans, resettlement plans or community investment programs.

Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective relationships with community stakeholders.

Experience managing consultants and project deliverables.

Strong research, communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

International experience, while desirable, is not essential.

A degree in social science, community development or a related discipline.

About Us

jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location:
Fortescue’s Cloudbreak mine is located on the traditional lands of the Palyku and Nyiyaparli peoples.

Roster: 
8D/20R
-
 FIFO ex Perth - B Crew

We are seeking an enthusiastic and safety-focused Mining Operator to join the Resource Definition Earthworks Crew at Cloudbreak.

This is a job-share opportunity working an 8 days on / 20 days off roster, on day shift only. You will fly from Perth to Cloudbreak each Wednesday and work as part of B Crew.

The role will support drilling programs by completing earthworks activities, including the construction and rehabilitation of drill lines, drill pads and sumps. You will work as part of a diverse and collaborative team, contributing to the safe and efficient delivery of Resource Definition activities.

Participate in reviews of SWIs and other relevant documentation.

Promote a safe, positive and inclusive work environment.

Complete machine pre-starts accurately and maintain all required records.

Identify, report and record machine faults and maintenance requirements.

Operate mobile earthmoving equipment safely and efficiently.

Use GPS systems such as Trimble or Guidex, where required.

Qualifications and Experience

Experience operating a 966 front-end loader or similar earthmoving machinery.

Previous mining experience, preferably within an earthworks or drilling environment.

An understanding of mine site safety requirements and operational documentation.

Previous experience using Trimble, Guidex or similar GPS systems is desirable but not essential.

A positive, enthusiastic and self-motivated approach.

The ability to work effectively as part of a diverse team.

jobs.description:

Work Location:
 Fortescue’s Iron Bridge project is located on the traditional lands of the Nyamal people.

Roster:
 8D/6R ex Perth

Join Iron Bridge’s Operations Planning team as a Project Mine Geologist and help shape one of Australia’s newest, largest and deepest open-pit operations.

Reporting to the Senior Mine Geologist, you’ll support high-quality mine geology practices that enable safe, efficient and accurate production outcomes. Assist with developing and maintaining grade control systems and procedures.

Support the Senior Mine Geologist to drive continuous improvement across team processes.

Tertiary qualification in Geology or Geoscience.

Current WA C-Class manual driver’s licence.

At least four years’ mining experience, including two years in mine geology.

Working knowledge of Vulcan, SQL databases and Microsoft Office.

About the role

The

Project Coordinator provides essential support to Project and Programme Managers in the delivery and coordination of complex, high-value advanced power systems programmes. This role plays a vital part in ensuring that all tasks, milestones, and deliverables are executed efficiently, on time, and in alignment with programme objectives. Working within a multidisciplinary environment, the Project Coordinator contributes to the seamless operation of project delivery through proactive coordination, communication, and progress tracking. Embody Fortescue’s Values in all interactions.

What you will do

Project Coordination and Support

Assist Programme Managers in the day-to-day execution of project scope & objectives.

Coordinate activities across multiple workstreams to ensure alignment and timely progress.

Maintain accurate and up-to-date project documentation, schedules, and action registers.

Ownership of task tracking & follow-up actions with stakeholders to ensure timely delivery.

Support the preparation and distribution of reports, dashboards, and meeting materials.

Liaise across departments to ensure contributors remain informed, aligned, and accountable.

Support internal and external stakeholder engagement to ensure effective collaboration.

Escalate issues or risks promptly and assist in implementing mitigation actions.

Continuous Improvement and Delivery Support

Take initiative to identify and address delivery gaps, ensuring progress continues as planned.

Contribute directly to project execution activities where necessary to maintain momentum.

Support adherence to governance frameworks, processes, and standards across programmes.

Promote consistency in delivery practices, contributing to process and system improvements.

Essential

Experience in project coordination, administration, or support roles—ideally within a

environment.

Strong organisational and communication skills, with a proactive and collaborative approach.

Proficiency in
Microsoft Office
suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook) and
project tracking tools
(e.g., MS Project, Planner, or equivalent).

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities & meet deadlines in a dynamic environment.

Effective interpersonal skills to work collaboratively with diverse, cross-functional teams.

Willingness and ability to travel internationally as required.

Preferred

Familiarity with
Microsoft Dynamics 365
or other enterprise project management systems.

Exposure to engineering, product lifecycle, or manufacturing programmes.

Strong attention to detail and a structured approach to task management.

Positive, solutions-oriented mindset with a focus on progress and accountability.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Collaborative team player who thrives in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

jobs.title: Land Management Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Reporting to the Geoscience & Land Supervisor, or any other individual designated by the Company, the Land Management Specialist supports land tenure, land access, and property management activities across resource development properties. This role assists with land tenure administration, agreement negotiation, land stewardship, and risk mitigation activities related to company-owned and managed lands.

This position works closely with internal teams including environmental, permitting, operations, and legal groups to ensure land-related activities align with regulatory requirements and company standards. The Land Management Specialist maintains accurate land records, supports property acquisitions and divestments, and contributes to cost-effective land management strategies.

All roles at NewRange serve as a courageous safety leader, leading by example and fostering a proactive safety and sustainability culture based on the common values of health, safety, environment, and communities.

Responsibilities

Land Tenure & Agreement Coordination

Ensure land management activities align with regulatory requirements, company policies, and environmental standards.

Support land-related compliance activities and participate in site risk assessments where required.

Review, track, and maintain land agreements including License of Occupation, Statutory Right of Way, Access, Road Use, and Purchase and Sale Agreements.

Assist in drafting and coordinating new land agreements and amendments as required.

Monitor agreement obligations, key dates, and commitments to ensure compliance with contractual terms.

Maintain accurate records of agreements and related correspondence.

Coordinate with internal teams, landowners, and external stakeholders to support land access requirements and agreement administration.

Land Stewardship & Portfolio Support

Support stewardship of company land assets by ensuring land use activities align with regulatory requirements and company standards.

Assist with property acquisitions, divestments, and land transactions where required.

Work with internal departments to integrate land considerations into operational and project planning activities.

Communicate with regulatory agencies, landowners, and other external stakeholders regarding land access, agreements, and related requirements.

Records Management & Data Systems

Maintain accurate and up-to-date land records including permits, agreements, and documentation related to third-party engagements.

Utilize GIS and database systems to track land tenure, property boundaries, and land-related activities.

Ensure land information systems and documentation are properly organized and accessible.

Research & Risk Reduction

Conduct research related to land rights, regulatory requirements, and permitting processes.

Prepare reports, summaries, and internal communications to support informed decision-making.

Support identification and resolution of land-related issues, risks, or stakeholder concerns.

Assist with initiatives that improve land management efficiency and reduce operational risk.

Other Duties

Perform additional duties and responsibilities as assigned to meet operational needs.

This job description is intended to provide a summary of the typical functions of the job and is not a comprehensive list of all possible job responsibilities, tasks, and duties. NewRange reserves the right to modify or assign other duties as necessary to meet operational needs.

Requirements

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree or certification in Business Administration, Commerce, Land Management, Real Estate, Legal Studies, Natural Resources Management Geosciences, or a related discipline is preferred.[CP2.1]

Minimum of five (5) years of experience in land management, real estate administration, legal administration, permitting, or a related field.

Experience working within resource development, mining, infrastructure, or land management environments is considered an asset.

Experience supporting land access agreements, land tenure administration, or property transactions is highly beneficial.

Skills and Abilities

Strong organizational and documentation management skills.

High attention to detail with the ability to track multiple agreements, obligations, and records.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Ability to coordinate effectively with internal teams, landowners, and regulatory agencies.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications including Excel, Word, and Outlook.

Experience with contract tracking systems, land databases, or records management systems is beneficial.

Experience in utilizing GIS platforms, such as ArcGIS, to manage and maintain databases related to land tenure records.

Strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization skills.

Physical Job Requirements & Working Conditions

This role requires the ability to work in both office and active project site environments, including occasional travel to operating or construction sites. Physical requirements may include extended periods of sitting and computer use, walking on uneven terrain, climbing stairs or accessing elevated platforms, and wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE) such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toe boots, respiratory protection and high-visibility clothing. The position may involve exposure to varying weather conditions, noise, dust, and other typical construction or industrial site environments, while maintaining a strong commitment to safety and compliance with all health, safety, and environmental standards.

Refer to the position-specific Physical Inventory for details.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

NewRange is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Cortez - Environmental Manager
jobs.description:
Position Description:

Would you like to have a career with a collaborative, diverse, and dynamic mining company? We have an exciting opportunity for you!

We are looking for an Environmental Manager to join the Cortez team. The role is responsible for Environmental Sustainability programs, ensuring continued compliance with all legal obligations and improvement on environmental performance, including accountability for water management, habitat improvement and reclamation, ISO14001 certification, and waste management and recycling. The Environmental Manager ensures that permits are obtained, revised, or updated as needed to facilitate seamless mine plan implementation.

At Nevada Gold Mines, our vision is to be the world's most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and operating the best assets with the best people. We are committed to a safe work environment sending every person home safe and healthy every day and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities.

Responsibilities:

Actively manage all environmental programs and compliance for open pit and underground mining operations, including overseeing the collection of data necessary to ensure the accurate and timely environmental reporting to site management and regulatory agencies;

Communicate with all departments and government agencies, at local, state and federal level, on environmental compliance matters;

Manage all key environmental aspects related to water, waste (non-hazardous and hazardous), air quality, lands (public and private), and reclamation/closure;

Oversee the preparation of environmental reports and other technical documents that are submitted to local, state and federal regulatory agencies

Liaise and coordinate with the Corporate permitting team to ensure that Operational perspectives are taken into consideration during large scale permitting activities;

Track permit renewals, regulatory proposals and pending legislation;

Develop and manage the environmental department budget;

Coach and mentor environmental department personnel to aid in professional development of skill sets

Assure compliance with company and site-specific policies, standards, procedures and objectives associated with site processes, initiatives/projects and recommend new policies or procedures, if necessary;

Direct the site development of guidance material and programs to support implementation of NGM's Environmental Management System and associated ISO 14001:2015 standard;

Participate in the development of audit protocols and coordinate internal and third-party audits to confirm compliance with all legal and other requirements;

Engage with business partners, community stakeholders and NGO's on business matters as needed;

Prepare recommendations for upper management on the implementation of new environmental systems, procedures or organizational changes;

Conduct operational effectiveness reviews to ensure environmental compliance; and,

Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in technical discipline such as Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Biology or Geology
required

Minimum of ten (10) years demonstrated environmental experience
required

Minimum five (5) years mining experience (open pit and underground operations)
required

Minimum five (5) years supervisory experience
required

Experience working on public land
required

Experience in engaging with U.S. agencies
preferred

What We Can Offer You

A comprehensive compensation package including a competitive medical, dental, and vision plan with national provider networks, a 401k retirement plan with employer contribution, paid time off, company-sponsored medical clinics, company match share purchase program, and much more!

Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.

Opportunities to grow and learn with the industry colleagues are endless.

Access to a variety of career opportunities across the organization.

Nevada Gold Mines is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

About Nevada Gold Mines

Nevada Gold Mines is a joint venture between Barrick Gold Corporation (61.5%) and Newmont Goldcorp Corporation (38.5%), combining their significant assets across Nevada to create the single largest gold-producing complex in the world and realize the full potential of these mines through synergies and best-in-class operational improvements.

The massive mining operation comprises 8 mines along with their associated infrastructure and processing facilities that produced an estimated 4 million ounces of gold in 2018. Three of these assets are Tier One gold mines: Barrick's Cortez; the combination of Barrick's Goldstrike and Newmont Goldcorp's Carlin; and the combination of Barrick's Turquoise Ridge and Newmont Goldcorp's Twin Creeks. In addition, Barrick's Goldrush-Fourmile project has the potential to become the fourth Tier One asset in this portfolio. The new JV is expected to generate around $5 billion in cost savings over the next five years. Nevada Gold Mines is operated by Barrick.

Anglo American is a leading global mining company reimagining the future of mining to improve lives. With a focus on the responsible production of copper, premium iron ore, and crop nutrients—critical resources for decarbonising the global economy and enhancing food security—Anglo American is at the forefront of sustainable innovation. Through its FutureSmart Mining™ approach, the company integrates cutting-edge technology, digitisation, and sustainability across the entire mining value chain. Guided by its Sustainable Mining Plan, Anglo American is committed to creating thriving communities, protecting the environment, and delivering enduring value for all stakeholders. Headquartered in London, the company operates across five continents and is listed on both the London and Johannesburg stock exchanges.

The Sakatti deposit is located in Finnish Lapland near the town of Sodankylä, and within the existing exploration permit areas fully owned by Anglo American Sakatti Mining Oy, a wholly owned subsidiary of Anglo American Plc. The Sakatti deposit is a unique, poly-metallic deposit that contains seven payable metals, including copper, nickel, cobalt, platinum, palladium, gold, and silver. The mine is targeted to produce two concentrates, high-grade copper and nickel concentrates but has optionality available to produce a bulk Cu-Ni concentrate.

We are seeking a
Database Geologist
to manage and maintain geoscience drill hole, sampling, and geological databases, ensuring data is accurately captured, governed, quality controlled, preserved and accessible to support resource estimation, technical studies, mine development and operations. The successful candidate will play a key role in maintaining the integrity and reliability of geological data, implementing best-practice data management processes and providing trusted datasets for operational and strategic decision-making.

Core Responsibilities (amongst others):

Manage, maintain, and develop the acQuire drill hole database, sampling, assay, and related geoscience databases, ensuring data integrity, security, accessibility, and long-term preservation.

Implement best-practice data governance, standards, procedures, protocols, and audit-ready workflows aligned with company requirements.

Ensure validated, fit-for-purpose geoscience data is available to support modelling, resource estimation, technical studies, reporting, mine planning, and operational readiness.

Support QAQC, sample tracking, laboratory data workflows, and data quality reviews through reliable data capture, loading, validation, and availability.

Support spatial data management, data extraction, reporting, and delivery of geoscience data products.

Provide database access, user support, training, and mentoring to relevant stakeholders.

Collaborate with Geo IM, Geoscience, Exploration, IM, laboratories, and vendors to improve data integration, workflows, templates, digital tools, and database systems.

Support the evaluation and implementation of emerging technologies into drill core logging workflows, such as Assisted Core Logging where relevant.

MSc degree in Geology, Geoscience, Mining Geology or similar required

Proven experience in geoscience database management, including advanced SQL skills, data validation, governance, quality control, maintenance, and reporting. Experience with acQuire database administration is highly preferred, particularly beyond user-level experience, including back-end configuration, development, and troubleshooting

Good understanding of assaying, sampling workflows and QAQC principles to ensure data is accurate and fit for purpose.

Good understanding of exploration and mining data types and how data from different methods is captured, managed, validated and integrated within geoscience database workflows.

Knowledge of Resource and Reserve reporting codes, such as SAMREC, JORC or NI 43-101, is beneficial.

Mine Geology & Production Support

Lead, plan, coordinate, and oversee the underground Mine Geology function to safely achieve production and business objectives.

Provide geological expertise to mine planning, production, engineering, exploration, and project development activities.

Monitor mining activities and grade control to optimize ore extraction, minimize dilution and ore loss, and support production targets.

Oversee underground geological mapping, structural interpretation, face sampling, chip/channel sampling, and geological data collection.

Develop, implement, and continuously improve grade control, geological mapping, sampling, and QA/QC programs.

Analyze production geology data and complete monthly production reconciliations, identifying variances and opportunities for improvement.

Prepare technical reports, geological summaries, and recommendations for management and operational teams.

Support the Corporate Resource Geologist in preparing, maintaining, and updating geological and resource models.

Contribute to wireframing, grade control modelling, geological interpretation, resource estimation, and mine depletion tracking.

Manage drilling contractors to ensure safe and efficient execution, adherence to scope and schedule, data quality, and budget requirements.

Coordinate geological logging, sampling, QA/QC, database management, and interpretation associated with drilling programs.

Review drilling results and provide geological interpretation and recommendations to support resource development and mine planning.

Track drilling expenditures and provide input into annual geological drilling budgets and forecasts.

Manage, mentor, and develop the geology team, promoting technical excellence, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Establish clear priorities, work plans, and performance expectations for geological activities.

Foster a strong safety culture and ensure geological personnel and contractors work in accordance with company policies and procedures.
