Support the Special Projects team by providing geological expertise for project development, technical evaluations, resource growth initiatives, and due diligence activities.

Provide technical geological input to studies, business cases, project evaluations, and strategic initiatives.

Collaborate with corporate and site-based geology teams to ensure consistency in geological interpretation, data standards, modelling, and reporting.

Contribute to monthly, quarterly, and annual operational and technical reporting.

Provide geological expertise for other corporate or operational initiatives as required.

Budget, Data & Reporting

Assist with annual budgeting and forecasting for geological programs.

Monitor geological expenditures and support effective cost control.

Maintain oversight of geological drilling contractors, including scope, performance, safety, schedules, and costs.

Ensure geological databases, sampling records, geological logs, QA/QC information, and supporting documentation are accurate, current, and maintained in accordance with company standards.

Ensure geological information is appropriately documented and readily available to support operational and technical decision-making.

Promote and maintain a strong health and safety culture across all geological activities.

Ensure geological programs and activities comply with applicable health, safety, environmental, regulatory, and company requirements.

Identify and address geological and operational risks associated with mining activities.

Ensure contractors and geological personnel comply with required safety standards and procedures.

Identify and implement opportunities to improve geological processes, systems, workflows, and data quality.

Evaluate new geological technologies, tools, and methodologies that may improve operational performance and resource understanding.

Promote the sharing of geological knowledge, lessons learned, and best practices across the organization.

Manage all car and assembly build activities ensuring Technical Drawings and Bulletins are captured and adhered to, relevant spares are defined and available and that build schedules are followed. Provide trackside vehicle build for events.

What you will do

Assemble, disassemble, and maintain cars, car components and other agreed assemblies and equipment, day to day

As a full-time team mechanic, attend test, rig, PR or race events as required, whilst being based at the factory daily when not on event.

Ensure that cars, components and assemblies are built to approved engineering specifications, referencing drawings, technical bulletins and build specs as distributed and that build checklists and build sheets are completed as required.

Ensure all faults and issues are escalated to the Chief Mechanic or to Design.

Identify and suggest improvements to components, team equipment and working practices day to day

Operate necessary tools and pit equipment as required

To build up and pack down garage / track setup environments as and when required.

Record and work with personal and department performance measures to identify the cause of any downtime or delays.

Maintain positive relationships with all other factory departments and company personnel.

To be able to work under their own initiative when necessary.

To follow and actively enforce the company’s health and Safety policy

jobs.title: Business Management Associate
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location:
San Francisco, CA or can be remote (within the US)

Roster:
5 Days / 2  Off

Role overview

Elysia's grid-scale BESS software division delivers on-premise and cloud software solutions to grid-scale storage owner-operators. As the division scales within Fortescue, it requires dedicated operational support across financial administration, customer delivery, internal alignment, and lab and product operations.

The BESS team’s Business Management Associate is responsible for the operational management processes that support the commercial and product functions of Elysia BESS business line. 

This is an execution-focused role: success is measured by processes running on schedule, bottlenecks being identified and escalated early, and reporting that leadership and Fortescue functional teams can rely on. 

Across all areas, the role measures and enables the business; execution ownership remains with the accountable functional teams.

This role reports to the Executive Vice President overseeing the division.

About Elysia

Elysia Battery Intelligence provides industry-best algorithms managing more than 10 GWh of batteries across verticals, with customers including consumer EV, heavy industry, and grid-scale BESS owner-operators.

Our algorithms make those batteries safer, more profitable, and more performant for more years, with proof points and deep learnings across many vendors and verticals.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial and Operational Administration

•    Administer and organize the division's financial and day-to-day operational processes, including budgeting, budget-to-actual tracking, customer invoicing, and compliance activities.

•    Provide appropriate reporting to Fortescue functional teams and coordinate the division's use of Fortescue resources (finance, legal, HR, recruiting, procurement) to best effect.

•    Coordinate hiring operations, including requisitions, interview scheduling, candidate pipeline management, and onboarding logistics.

2. Commercial and Customer Operations

•    Facilitate customer deliveries of our on-prem and cloud software solutions with grid-scale storage owners, tracking deployments through go-live and identifying and escalating bottlenecks with supporting data.

•    Measure and report on support bandwidth and quality, including ticket volume, response times, backlog, and recurring issues, and direct attention and process improvements to the areas that matter most to the business.

•    Facilitate legal, compliance, and deal desk resources in support of sales, lab, and customer operations.

3. Internal Alignment Heartbeat

•    Organize weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting and planning sessions with the relevant BESS division leadership stakeholders, including agendas, inputs, materials, and action tracking.

•    Facilitate alignment with broader Elysia and Fortescue strategic planning, functional processes, senior leadership team

4. Lab and Product Operations

•    Support battery lab and modeling R&D operations, including coordination with external test labs and the Elysia UK lab.

•    Support hardware procurement and operational logistics for Elysia's on-premise and cloud product deployments at BESS sites.

Qualifications and Experience

Required

•    3 to 4 years of experience in business operations, finance, consulting, engineering, or a comparable role

•    Comfort working with contracts and with legal and finance counterparts

•    Strong analytical and spreadsheet skills, including the ability to build and maintain reporting adopted by stakeholders

•    Clear, concise written communication, including the ability to distill complex operational situations for senior leadership in briefs, presentations, and dashboards.

•    Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities and limited existing process

Preferred

•    MBA or comparable formal business training, completed or planned

•    Exposure to batteries, energy, hardware, or laboratory environments

•    Experience with budgeting, invoicing, or compliance processes

•    Experience supporting recruiting or planning cycles within a larger corporate environment

How We Will Evaluate You

•    Financial and operational processes run on schedule with accurate, complete inputs, making effective use of Fortescue resources.

•    Customer delivery and support reporting is current and accurate, and directs action to the right owners.

•    The division's weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting and planning heartbeat runs reliably.

•    Lab and hardware logistics are coordinated proactively and without schedule surprises.

jobs.title: Managing Director - Power Systems
jobs.description:
The Power of Now

Fortescue Zero is at the forefront of advanced engineering and technology, developing high-voltage power systems, advanced battery software and electrification solutions for some of the world’s most demanding applications.

Our technology and engineering expertise extends across heavy industry, defence and elite motorsport, with involvement in global championships including Formula E, the IMSA and the World Endurance Championship.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Managing Director – Power Systems to join Fortescue Zero in Oxford.

About the Role

As Managing Director – Power Systems, you will lead the engineering, product development and programme delivery of our global power systems portfolio. Our technologies will support the electrification of some of the world’s largest mobile industrial equipment, with opportunities to expand into adjacent applications, including data centres.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, you will have genuine end-to-end accountability across the product lifecycle, from concept and design through industrialisation, commissioning and customer acceptance. Supported by executive leadership, significant investment and dedicated resources, you will have a clear mandate to build capability, scale delivery and turn ambitious technology into safe, reliable and commercially successful products.

This is a rare opportunity to lead a multidisciplinary organisation at the forefront of industrial decarbonisation and shape products with the potential to change how industries operate.

What You Will Do

Lead and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary organisation across electrical, mechanical, systems, software, controls, product and programme management

Own the engineering, design and delivery of the power systems portfolio from concept through commissioning and customer acceptance

Set engineering standards, governance and technical assurance processes that deliver safe, reliable and scalable products

Ensure portfolio commitments are delivered safely, on time, within budget and to agreed quality and contractual requirements

Hold accountability for commercial and financial performance, including profitability, forecasting, cost control and resource planning

Establish disciplined programme governance, portfolio prioritisation, performance metrics and operating rhythms

Identify and manage technical, commercial, programme and customer risks across the full product lifecycle

Partner with Sales, Commercial and Finance teams on bids, pricing, contracts, change control and delivery risk

Build trusted executive relationships with customers, partners and stakeholders, acting as executive sponsor for major programmes

Translate Fortescue Zero’s technology and product strategy into executable plans that improve capability, scalability and business performance

About You

Significant executive leadership experience within a large engineering, product development or programme delivery organisation

Proven success leading multidisciplinary engineering teams through the full product lifecycle

Experience taking complex electrical, engineered or technology products from concept through industrialisation and into production

Strong commercial and financial capability, including profit and loss accountability, project profitability and contract management

Extensive programme management, portfolio governance and large-scale project delivery experience

Strong understanding of systems engineering, product development, technical governance and operational excellence

Experience delivering products or systems within mining, energy, industrial, heavy engineering or other demanding sectors

Demonstrated ability to combine engineering excellence, innovation and commercial delivery

Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, systems engineering or a related discipline

Experience working with original equipment manufacturers, engineering, procurement and construction contractors, mining companies or industrial customers will be highly regarded

An opportunity has arisen for a Senior Engineer - Motorsport Analysis to join the Motorsport & Advanced Engineering department.

About the role

The 

motorsport and advanced engineering 

business unit have a team comprising of design engineers and engineering analysts. 

An engineering analyst is required to develop robust models and workflows to be used in simulation-led design optimisation activities.

 T

he ideal candidate has experience across thermal

,

s

Fortescue Zero exists to accelerate the advantage and impact of our clients. We do it through innovative engineering and technology that solves complex problems and brings a step-change in weight, speed and efficiency. Join us to help fulfil our mission to accelerate an efficient, electric and sustainable future.

We operate a 12-month (Summer 2027 – Summer 2028) student placement programme within the Vehicle Performance group. This is an exciting opportunity where you will work with highly skilled and experienced engineering professionals and graduates who you can learn and develop with - the more questions you ask the more you will gain from your experience.  It is important to know that many of our industrial placements have been successful in obtaining graduate roles on completion of their degree.

To be eligible for an industrial placement within our Formula E Vehicle Performance team you should be working towards a STEM degree including but not limited to, Mathematics, Mechanical, Aerospace, Automotive, Computer Science, Data Science, Physics or Motorsport Engineering.  An understanding of vehicle dynamics, control systems (including optimal control), mathematical modelling and programming (MATLAB, Python, JavaScript, C#, C, C++ and OOP) would be advantageous.

What you will do

During the placement, you will take on responsibilites such as:

Analysis of car, rig, simulator & model data to unlock performance potential in current & future cars

The analysis of race data whilst working with the strategists in order to maximise our decision making and find the optimal strategies for the races.

Being part of the Ops Room (mission control) where you will be supporting the race team at the track.

Developing software tools and models in order to make processes and analysis more automatic.

Contributing towards our pre-event and post-event analyses of car, tyre, systems, & strategy performance.

Overall, you will contribute to make our car faster, more reliable and more efficient. 

When applying for industrial placements opportunities, all students are expected to submit a covering letter along with a Curriculum Vitae containing the following information: 

Your current career aims and how you plan to achieve them. 

Subjects that you are currently taking and plan to take. 

Relevant leisure pursuits and activities. 

Why work experience would be beneficial to you. 

Next Steps

Those students that are shortlisted will be invited to attend an assessment.  It is expected that the student takes sole responsibility for making suitable travel and accommodation arrangements.

Our Commitment

You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. At Fortescue Zero we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences and skills.   Fortescue Zero is an equal opportunity employer who values diversity and inclusion. If you have a disability,  We are happy to discuss reasonable job adjustments.

About Woodside

We know great results come from our people feeling valued, getting the support they need to reach their full potential and working in a positive work environment. We recognise that enduring, meaningful relationships with communities are fundamental to maintaining our licence to operate.

Technology and innovation are essential to our long-term sustainability. We are working to improving energy efficiency, offset emissions, reduce emissions intensity and explore options for lower-carbon energy. Woodside led the development of the LNG industry in Australia and is applying this same pioneering spirit to solving future energy challenges globally.

Refer to our corporate website for more information about our different locations and projects: 
https://www.woodside.com/what-we-do

About the Role

The Principle Process Engineer I is responsible for providing engineering support to Trion operating facilities in the Gulf of Mexico. This position requires interface with Operations, Production Engineering, HSE and other functions, and is responsible for providing technical support to the production facilities, advising on startup, shutdowns, process and production optimization (inclusive of emissions reduction efforts) and supporting the integration of future development projects. The role will contribute to operations readiness, commissioning and startup activities and transition into ongoing operational stewardship as the project moves into steady-state Operate Phase.

Duties and Responsibilities

Execute Phase

•    Support review and development of standard operating procedures, temporary startup (operational test procedures, OTPs) and flowback operations.
•    Support review and development of production allocation plan, oil and gas balance models and reports (internal and external regulatory).
•    Support commissioning and startup activities for process systems on the FPU (floating production unit).
•    Provide technical information to other support business functions (HSE, Regulatory, Marketing, Commercial, etc) for permitting workflows.

Operate Phase, responsibilities include: 
•    Provide technical leadership and support in process engineering across subsea flowline and topsides equipment to the operations and maintenance teams.  Foster effective relationships with both office and site-based teams.
•    Propose and develop process solutions to ensure safe and reliable operations which may include additional new or temporary equipment as projects and opportunities are assigned.
•    Execute surveillance of the offshore asset(s) and provide assurance of on-going performance against key KPIs.  Continually improve the process surveillance tools and KPIs across the operated facilities.
•    Lead or participate as a member of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) teams as required

•    Lead or participate in HAZOPs, HAZIDs, LOPAs, other risk assessments and Design Reviews as required.
•    Provides governance and oversight to ensure engineering practices are carried out in accordance with the required technical standards, processes, and procedures while operating in compliance with local regulations and corporate standards
•    Provision of technical expertise and direction into “Operational Risk Assessment” scenarios related to process engineering as assigned.
•    Identify, design, and implement engineering & maintenance change projects as they relate to the process engineering discipline in accordance with Management of Change procedures.  Provide review and endorsement where applicable for management of change projects led by others for the facilities.
•    Provide guidance to engineering contractors on the application of Woodside’s procedures and guidelines

·    Work within company management systems and processes, applying sound risk management and management of change.

•    Periodic travel to offshore facility or operations base during startup and operations phase.

The role focuses on maintaining material readiness, optimizing inventory holdings, and ensuring alignment with forecast demand while meeting business, compliance, and operational performance objectives.

Duties and Responsibilities

Develop and maintain inventory strategies tailored to reduce excess, obsolete, and slow-moving inventory. 

Coordinate material readiness reviews and facilitate planning routines with operational stakeholders.

Develop strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders to drive inventory optimization and operational performance.

Promote standardization, process discipline, and continuous improvement opportunities across inventory management processes.

Support physical stocktake programs and ensure inventory accuracy across Woodside-managed, vendor-held, and third-party storage locations.

Ensure compliance with SOX and WMS standards, assurance requirements, joint venture obligations, and inventory governance standards.

Provide inventory expertise and support for business inquiries, audits, assurance reviews, and operational planning activities.

Contribute to initiatives that improve inventory visibility, forecasting accuracy, and cost efficiency.

Interface closely with Supply sub-functions to ensure effective communication and collaboration across teams.

Manage material disposals and subsequent sales to 3rd party buyers in support of inventory optimization strategies

Skills and Experience

3-5+ years experience in oil and gas industry, Drilling & Completions support a plus

Experience in Warehouse, Inventory and Logistics

Strong analytical abilities and problem-solving skills, with a meticulous attention to detail.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with diverse teams and stakeholders.

Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Excel

SAP S/4HANA  

Materials Management  

Inventory Controls  

Supply Chain Optimization 

Surplus Disposition 

Audit & SOX Compliance 

Stakeholder Engagement 

Risk Management 

Data Analytics  

Continuous Improvement  

Commercial Awareness 

Process Governance  

Inventory Assurance

•    Values led culture with a focus on creating a psychologically and physically safe work environment
•    Active employee-led working groups driving initiatives to build an inclusive culture.
•    Community volunteering opportunities
•    Relocation assistance (if required)
•    A competitive remuneration package featuring performance-based incentives
 
Woodside is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workforce culture, which is supported by our Values. Our aim is to attract, develop and retain a truly diverse and high-performing workforce. 
 
Diversity encompasses various differences, including but not limited to differences in age, nationality, race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, sex, sexual orientation, intersex status, gender identity or expression, relationship status, disability, neurodiversity, veteran status, cultural background, thinking styles, experience, family background, including caregiving commitments, and education. Inclusion centres on all employees creating a climate of respect, trust and belonging, where people feel enabled to be their best and authentic version of themself.
 
We offer supportive pathways for all employees to grow and develop leadership skills.

At Agnico Eagle, our values never waver. We believe in trust, respect, equity, family and responsibility. Why? Because they express who we are, and they have helped us succeed in business for over 60 years. We value
you
- your unique set of skills and experience. We value your willingness to build those skills and make a meaningful contribution to our company. And, we value your commitment to treat every person on our team with respect, helping us to operate safely, protect the environment and make a positive contribution to our local communities.

ABOUT OUR OPERATION

Canadian-based and led, Agnico Eagle is Canada's largest mining company and the second largest gold producer in the world. It produces precious metals from operations in Canada, Australia, Finland and Mexico and has a pipeline of high-quality exploration and development projects. Agnico Eagle is a partner of choice within the mining industry, recognized globally for its leading sustainability practices. Agnico Eagle was founded in 1957 and has consistently created value for its shareholders, declaring a cash dividend every year since 1983.

Agnico Eagle Mines' Macassa Mine is situated on the traditional homelands of the Apitipi Anicinapek Nation, Beaverhouse First Nation, and Matachewan First Nation. In honoring our relationships with and commitments to our Partner Nations, Agnico Eagle prioritizes the hiring of Members from these Nations. To support this commitment, members from these Nations seeking employment opportunities at the Macassa Mine are encouraged to self-identify during the job application process. This ensures that we can consider your application appropriately in line with our dedication to supporting our Partner Nations.

Want to learn more about Macassa Mine?

!

You will also ensure that the goals and objectives are achieved while promoting and respecting Agnico Eagle’s values, Health & Safety Code of Conduct and the environment.

Facilitate job site preparation and material set up;

Participate in job site final walk though;

Assist Trades personnel in the coordination of on-site activities and installations;

Provide input relating to the resolution of any design or installation issues;

Keep accurate records of underground material stock levels;

Assist with cable pulls and equipment installations;

Ensure tools are organized and in good repair;

Participate in safe lockout;

Apply 5 S principles - Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain;

All other duties as directed by supervisor.

Must be able to read or learn to read and understand electrical prints;

Must have good communication and leadership skills;

Able to set priorities;

Ability to think logically and keep up with changes in technology;

Good people skills, and good planning;

Basic computer skills, written and verbal communication skills;

Team player and self-motivator;

Training in First Aid, Fall Protection;

Experience in operating heavy equipment;

Valid Drivers licence an advantage.

jobs.description:
At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing an employment package that recognizes excellence, encourages safe production and a culture supported by our core values. Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority, all opinions are valued, and people are empowered to grow in their career. 
Apply Today!     

Where You Will Work

Located approximately 50 miles northeast of Safford, Arizona on U.S. Highway 191, Morenci operations (an open-pit copper mining complex) has been in continuous operation since 1939. The operation consists of two concentrators, crushed-ore leach pad and stacking system, a low-grade run-of-mine (ROM) leaching system; four SX plants; and three EW tank houses that produce copper cathode.  

Morenci is a unique company town where our employees and their families can reconnect with nature through hiking, fishing, camping, hunting and numerous parks. The company offers several amenities, including company housing OR employees who are required to work on-site are eligible for a $750 monthly housing allowance, provided they meet program guidelines, a newly constructed daycare and community center, library, health-care facilities, state-of-the-art fitness centers, a movie theater and a skate park. Our dedicated Parks and Recreation Division plans activities for people of all ages, making sure there’s something for everyone to enjoy. Visit the Morenci town 
website
 to learn more. 

Description

Process Operator I's are skilled employees who operate at least one material handling system in the production process, such as conveyors, transfer chutes, flow systems and flotation/grind mills. Employees work under minimal supervision in environments where the primary objective is safe production. 

A Hydromet CLP Operator I performs duties related to Concentrate Leach Plant operations. Requires familiarity with pumps, pipes, valves, process flow and controlling processes to predetermined set points. Operates assigned circuit to achieve production targets and troubleshoots operational issues including minor maintenance on equipment and components in assigned area of responsibility. 

Operate/control processing equipment per operating guidelines 

Perform area housekeeping to include tasks such as shoveling, using fire hose and digging 

Operate processing and mobile equipment 

Monitor equipment and enter data via computer 

Identify and report machinery maintenance needs 

Perform other tasks as assigned

Six (6) months of experience in the trade

Experience with material handling equipment

This exam is based on skills/abilities and/or academic knowledge; as well as safety.

Experience with steam generator (boiler) operation, scrubbers, heat exchangers, filters, thickeners, and pressure vessels

Experience with sample collection and analysis

Experience operating material handling equipment including forklift, skid steer loader, and overhead crane

Occasionally may be required to lift up to fifty (50) pounds during the course of the work day

Personal protective equipment is required when performing work in a mine, outdoor, manufacturing or plant environment, including hard hat, hearing protection, safety glasses, safety footwear, and as needed, respirator, rubber steel-toe boots, protective clothing, gloves and any other protective equipment as required

jobs.title: Product Manager - Commercial
jobs.description:
The Power of Now

Be part of something big. Fortescue is leading the world with our plan to decarbonise our iron ore operations, projects that harness renewable energy and the development of technology that will change our planet forever.

An opportunity has arisen for a Product Manager - Commercial to join the Product & Delivery department.

About the role

The
Commercial Product Manager
is a technically strong and commercially driven professional responsible for leading the
development, launch, and commercialisation
of products that accelerate the
electrification and decarbonisation of heavy industry
. This role combines strategic product leadership with deep technical understanding of
power electronics and energy systems
, ensuring Fortescue remains at the forefront of industrial sustainability and innovation.

Working collaboratively across
engineering, operations, and commercial functions
, the Commercial Product Manager will drive products from
concept through deployment
, delivering solutions that reduce emissions, enhance efficiency, and create long-term value for industrial customers. Embody Fortescue’s Values in all interactions.

What you will do

Product Strategy and Leadership
•    Define and execute the product strategy and roadmap for industrial electrification and power system solutions.
•    Translate customer, regulatory, and operational requirements into detailed Product Requirements Documents (PRDs) and actionable development priorities.
•    Ensure alignment of product initiatives with Fortescue’s sustainability, energy transition, and zero-emission strategy.
•    Manage the end-to-end product lifecycle — from concept and prototyping through validation, pilot deployment, commercial launch, and continuous improvement.

Technical and Cross-Functional Collaboration
•    Collaborate with Engineering, Innovation, and Manufacturing teams to guide product design, testing, and industrialisation.
•    Support technical feasibility assessments, manufacturing readiness reviews, and cost optimisation initiatives.
•    Ensure all products meet relevant industry standards, safety regulations, and certification requirements (IEC, IEEE, ISO, etc.).
•    Partner with Supply Chain and Procurement to evaluate suppliers, components, and technology partners for commercial viability.

Market, Customer, and Commercial Focus
•    Conduct market research and competitive analysis to identify trends, technology shifts, and partnership opportunities within industrial electrification.
•    Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, and Business Development to define go-to-market strategies, pricing, and customer value propositions.
•    Engage directly with customers to capture use cases, performance targets, and total cost of ownership (TCO) drivers for electrified systems.
•    Develop and maintain business cases, financial models, and ROI analyses to support product investment and portfolio decisions.

Performance and Continuous Improvement
•    Monitor product performance metrics, including adoption, reliability, and sustainability impact, providing insights to guide iteration.
•    Support operational readiness by coordinating cross-functional launch and lifecycle management activities.
•    Identify opportunities for product enhancement and portfolio growth based on customer feedback and market intelligence.

About you

Essential

Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in
Engineering (Electrical, Mechanical, Energy Systems, or related discipline)
.

Significant
experience in
product management, technical leadership, or business development
within industrial equipment, power systems, or clean energy technologies.

Strong technical understanding of:

Electric motors and drives

Power electronics and conversion systems

High-voltage infrastructure or microgrids

Battery energy storage systems (BESS)

Proven track record in
cross-functional project delivery
across engineering, commercial, and operational domains.

Strong
commercial and analytical skills
, including business case development and financial modelling.

Familiarity with
industrial regulations, safety standards, and sustainability metrics
.

Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence technical and executive audiences.

Willingness and ability to
travel internationally
as required.

Preferred

Experience in
mining, manufacturing, transportation, or energy infrastructure
sectors.

Background in
electrical engineering, power systems, or industrial automation
.

Experience with
Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
systems and digital product data tools.

Master’s degree or MBA
preferred.

Passion for
sustainability, decarbonisation, and the global energy transition
.

Attributes

Strategic thinker with strong commercial acumen and technical credibility.

Collaborative and adaptable, able to navigate complex multi-stakeholder environments.

Data-driven decision-maker with excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.

Clear and confident communicator capable of bridging engineering and business priorities.

Results-oriented with a passion for innovation, impact, and sustainability.

What is in it for you?

Our UK benefits include:

Bonus scheme

Aviva Pension

Group Life Assurance

Group Income Protection

Electric Car Scheme

Health Cash Plan

Employee Assistance Programme

Private Medical Insurance

26 days holiday
plus
public holidays and the opportunity to purchase an additional 5 days per year

jobs.title: Topógrafo(a) – Proyecto  Antamina
jobs.description:
En Grupo Empresas Geoblast, buscamos un(a) Topógrafo(a) con experiencia en minería a tajo abierto y fotogrametría digital para integrarse al equipo del proyecto Antamina, contribuyendo desde el levantamiento topográfico de precisión al control geométrico de bancos, la validación de diseños de voladura y la generación de modelos 3D para la conciliación de banquetas.
Objetivo del cargo
Ejecutar levantamientos topográficos superficiales y capturas fotogramétricas de alta precisión mediante RPAS/Dron en el tajo y botaderos, validando la constructibilidad geométrica de las mallas de voladura y generando los ortomosaicos y modelos 3D necesarios para la conciliación de banquetas.
Principales responsabilidades
Validar el diseño geométrico de la voladura en terreno y medir con precisión milimétrica los resultados obtenidos post-disparo.
Obtener imágenes aéreas sistemáticas para la generación de ortomosaicos de alta resolución y modelos 3D en formatos OBJ y DXF.
Ejecutar el procesamiento de datos topográficos para los trabajos de conciliación de banquetas tanto para banco simple como para banco doble.
Ejecutar levantamientos topográficos de alta precisión antes y después de las actividades de perforación y voladura.
Validar y controlar el cumplimiento de los diseños de P&V, verificando la conformidad entre el diseño planificado y la ejecución en campo.
Realizar el control topográfico de paredes finales (Wall Control) mediante la medición y evaluación de crestas, pies de banco, bermas, taludes y demás elementos geométricos.
Operar equipos topográficos y sistemas de captura geoespacial: estaciones totales, receptores GNSS RTK y drones (UAV).
Ejecutar y procesar levantamientos fotogramétricos con UAV, generando ortomosaicos, modelos digitales del terreno y de superficie, nubes de puntos y modelos tridimensionales.
Preparar planos, perfiles, secciones e informes técnicos que respalden la evaluación del desempeño de las voladuras y el cumplimiento de los criterios de calidad del servicio QA/QC Wall Control.
Gestionar y resguardar la información topográfica y geoespacial generada durante el servicio.
Asegurar el cumplimiento de los estándares del Sistema de Gestión Integrado (ISO 9001, 14001, 45001).
Requisitos
Técnico Nivel Superior titulado en Topografía, Geomensura o Geominería.
Mínimo 3 años de experiencia en topografía superficial de minería a tajo abierto y fotogrametría digital.
Licencia y acreditación vigente de operador RPAS (Dron) emitida por la autoridad competente de Perú.
Manejo de equipos de precisión (GPS Diferencial, Estaciones Totales, Drones).
Dominio a nivel usuario de software de procesamiento fotogramétrico (Pix4D, AutoCAD, Civil 3D).

Sistema de turno 10x10
Proyecto de duración definida con posibilidad de extensión
Beneficios; cubrimos 100% la EPS al colaborador y 50% a sus derechohabientes.

Planilla a regimen general.

jobs.title: Asistente de recursos humanos
jobs.description:
Buscamos Reclutador(a) de Personal Técnico

En RAM Equipos nos especializamos en reparación y mantenimiento de maquinaria pesada. Trabajamos con importantes contratistas mineros, empresas mineras, constructoras y compañías de los sectores automotriz e industrial.

Buscamos una persona dinámica, organizada y orientada a resultados, interesada en asumir un rol clave en nuestras operaciones y crecer profesionalmente dentro del área de Recursos Humanos.

El principal reto será asegurar la incorporación oportuna de técnicos mecánicos, electricistas, soldadores, supervisores y otros perfiles especializados.

Principales funciones:

• Gestionar integralmente los procesos de reclutamiento, selección y contratación, desde el levantamiento del perfil hasta la incorporación del candidato.

• Manejar simultáneamente entre 5 y 8 procesos, incluyendo coberturas rápidas y contrataciones temporales por días o semanas.

• Reclutar perfiles para los sectores de maquinaria pesada, minería, construcción, automotriz, industrial y metalmecánico.

• Publicar vacantes y buscar activamente candidatos mediante LinkedIn, Computrabajo, Bumeran, redes sociales, referidos y otras fuentes.

• Realizar filtros curriculares, entrevistas por competencias, validación de experiencia, referencias laborales y seguimiento de candidatos.

• Construir y mantener una base de datos actualizada de personal técnico disponible.

• Utilizar herramientas de inteligencia artificial para sourcing, identificación de candidatos y optimización de los procesos de selección.

• Coordinar con supervisores y responsables de cada área el avance y cierre de las posiciones.

• Gestionar el onboarding y offboarding del personal, incluyendo documentación, inducción, seguimiento inicial, encuestas de salida e identificación de oportunidades de mejora.

• Elaborar reportes e indicadores de reclutamiento, contratación, incorporación, rotación y salida de personal.

¿Qué perfil buscamos?

• Egresado(a), bachiller o profesional de Psicología, Administración, Recursos Humanos, Ingeniería Industrial o carreras afines.

• Experiencia mínima de 3 años en reclutamiento, selección y contratación de personal.

• Experiencia comprobable reclutando técnicos mecánicos, electricistas, soldadores, supervisores y otros perfiles técnicos u operativos.

• Experiencia en maquinaria pesada, minería, construcción, automotriz, industria, metalmecánica, mantenimiento o servicios técnicos.

• Capacidad para gestionar varios procesos simultáneamente y atender coberturas rápidas o temporales.

• Manejo de LinkedIn, Computrabajo, Bumeran y otras fuentes de reclutamiento.

• Manejo avanzado de Excel: bases de datos, fórmulas, filtros, tablas dinámicas, cruces de información e indicadores.

• Conocimiento de inteligencia artificial aplicada al reclutamiento y conocimientos generales de Recursos Humanos.

Competencias:

• Orientación a resultados y sentido de urgencia.

• Organización y capacidad de seguimiento.

• Comunicación efectiva.

• Iniciativa, dinamismo y adaptabilidad.

• Confidencialidad y responsabilidad.

¿Qué ofrecemos?

• Remuneración de S/2,000 a S/2,300 brutos mensuales, según experiencia y ajuste al perfil.

• Oportunidades de aprendizaje y crecimiento profesional.

• Participación directa en procesos clave para nuestras operaciones.

• Desarrollo profesional en reclutamiento técnico y gestión de personal.

Lugar y horario:

• Trabajo 100 % presencial: 4 días en Santiago de Surco y 2 días en Lurin.

• Horario: lunes a viernes de 8:00 a. m. a 5:30 p. m. y sábados de 8:00 a. m. a 1:00 p. m.

• Es indispensable residir en Surco, Lurin o zonas aledañas que permitan trasladarse fácilmente a ambas sedes.

Si tienes experiencia reclutando personal técnico, disfrutas trabajar con objetivos y quieres desarrollarte en una empresa vinculada a sectores importantes de la economía, queremos conocerte.-Requerimientos- Educación mínima: Técnico

Manage environmental data and associated databases

Execute environmental disturbance permitting

Undertake environmental sampling activities

Perform data validation of all environmental monitoring data for inclusion in internal and external reports

Monitor and report on various environmental aspects 

Manage third-party contracts

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, sex, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, citizenship, genetic information or other protected status under federal, state or local laws.

jobs.title: Mining Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Reporting to the Study Manager, or any other individual designated by the Company, the Mining Engineer is responsible for supporting mine planning, design, and scheduling activities for surface mining operations. This role contributes to the development of safe, practical, and economically viable mine plans aligned with operational and strategic objectives.

Working closely with operations, geology, environmental, and project teams, the Mining Engineer applies sound engineering practices to support short- and long-term planning, technical analysis, and continuous improvement initiatives.

All roles at NewRange serve as a courageous safety leader, leading by example and fostering a proactive safety and sustainability culture based on the common values of health, safety, environment, and communities.

Responsibilities

Operational Support

Collaborate with operations teams to ensure mine plans are safe, practical, and aligned with site requirements.

Participate in daily operational interactions and planning discussions to support safe and efficient production.

Mine Planning & Design

Develop mine designs, plans, and scheduling models using mining software such as Deswik and Whittle.

Develop and maintain regular schedules to support operational execution and planning alignment.

Perform pit optimization analysis on a regular basis to support economic extraction strategies.

Support short-term, medium-term, and long-term planning activities.

Contribute to Life-of-Asset mine planning on an annual basis.

Prepare mine design documentation and engineering calculations supporting mine development and planning activities.

Engineering Analysis & Technical Support

Perform engineering calculations and technical analysis to support mine design and operational decision-making.

Apply engineering judgment and problem-solving skills in complex or non-standardized situations where established procedures may not exist.

Conduct trade-off studies and evaluations to optimize mine design, scheduling, and project outcomes.

Support budgeting and forecasting activities through development of production assumptions and planning inputs.

Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and reduce mining impacts through engineering solutions.

Develop solutions informed by knowledge of mining market conditions, emerging technologies, and industry trends.

Reporting & Documentation

Prepare technical reports, schedules, and presentations for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Support annual mineral resource and ore reserve reporting.

Develop and maintain documentation related to mine planning processes, engineering studies, and project evaluations.

Utilize Microsoft Office applications to prepare analysis, reports, and presentations.

Support process mapping and documentation of mine planning workflows.

Consultant & Contractor Coordination

Develop scopes of work for technical studies, trade-off analyses, and engineering support activities.

Coordinate with consultants, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), and technical specialists to support project requirements.

Review and evaluate external technical work and incorporate findings into mine planning activities.

Other Duties

Perform additional duties and responsibilities as assigned to meet operational needs.

This job description is intended to provide a summary of the typical functions of the job and is not a comprehensive list of all possible job responsibilities, tasks, and duties. NewRange reserves the right to modify or assign other duties as necessary to meet operational needs.

Requirements

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Mining Engineering is required.

Minimum of three (3) years of experience in mine planning, mine design, or mining engineering within surface mining or resource development operations.

Professional engineering designation or eligibility for registration is considered a strong asset.

Experience with mine planning and optimization software is required.

Skills and Abilities

Experience with mining software including Deswik and Whittle.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Strong analytical, technical, and problem-solving skills.

Ability to apply sound engineering judgment in complex and non-routine situations.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to convey technical information clearly.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.

Strong collaboration skills with multidisciplinary teams including operations, geology, and environmental groups.

Knowledge of mining methods, market conditions, and emerging technologies to support innovative solutions.

Physical Job Requirements & Working Conditions

This role requires the ability to work in both office and active project site environments, including occasional travel to operating or construction sites. Physical requirements may include extended periods of sitting and computer use, walking on uneven terrain, climbing stairs or accessing elevated platforms, and wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE) such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toe boots, respiratory protection and high-visibility clothing. The position may involve exposure to varying weather conditions, noise, dust, and other typical construction or industrial site environments, while maintaining a strong commitment to safety and compliance with all health, safety, and environmental standards.

Refer to the position-specific Physical Inventory for details.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

NewRange is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Salary Description

$88,000-$110,000

Ejecutar de manera segura y eficiente las actividades de mantenimiento preventivo y correctivo de los sistemas e instrumentos de control, conforme a los estándares, procedimientos e instructivos de la unidad minera y al programa de mantenimiento establecido, con el fin de asegurar la confiabilidad, disponibilidad y óptimo desempeño de los equipos y procesos operativos. 

III. RESPONSABILIDADES Y FUNCIONES

Ejecutar y controlar las actividades de inspección, mantenimiento preventivo y correctivo de los instrumentos de campo, sistemas de pesaje, lazos de control y sistemas de automatización, garantizando su confiabilidad y disponibilidad operacional.

Coordinar con las áreas operativas y de mantenimiento la programación y ejecución de las actividades de instrumentación, asegurando la disponibilidad de recursos, herramientas, repuestos y permisos requeridos.    

Diagnosticar fallas y desviaciones en instrumentos y sistemas de control, implementando acciones correctivas para minimizar su recurrencia.   

Ejecutar, verificar y optimizar las actividades de mantenimiento y calibración de balanzas dinámicas y estáticas, asegurando la exactitud de las mediciones utilizadas en el control de procesos y balances metalúrgicos.

Mantener actualizada la documentación técnica de instrumentación y control, incluyendo hojas de datos, diagramas de lazo, planos P&ID, manuales, listas de instrumentos y respaldos de sistemas de control.

Gestionar y realizar seguimiento a las notificaciones, avisos y órdenes de trabajo en SAP PM, garantizando la calidad del registro histórico y el cierre oportuno de las actividades ejecutadas.

Identificar, evaluar e implementar mejoras en los sistemas de instrumentación, automatización y control orientadas a incrementar la seguridad, confiabilidad, disponibilidad y eficiencia operacional.

Contribuir al sostenimiento de las buenas prácticas corporativas relacionadas con LinGo, DdD, RdP, estandarización de procesos y metodología 5S.

Cumplir y promover las políticas, normas y estándares de Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Medio Ambiente, velando por la integridad de las personas, procesos y activos de la organización.

Ejecutar otras funciones afines al cargo que le sean asignadas por su supervisión y para las cuales cuente con la capacitación y autorización correspondiente.

jobs.description:
Acerca de BHP

BHP trabaja en conjunto con empresas colaboradoras que promueven un proceso de selección justo, equitativo y accesible para todas las personas. En este contexto, autorizo que, como parte del proceso, pueda ser contactado(a) por un tercero que actúe en representación de BHP.

¿Por que BHP Chile?

Porque aquí tendrás la oportunidad de crecer en una organización que valora la diversidad, fomenta el desarrollo profesional y apuesta por tecnologías que transforman la industria minera. En BHP Chile podrás generar impacto real en la comunidad y el medioambiente, mientras construyes tu carrera en una empresa reconocida por su cultura inclusiva y su compromiso con el futuro.

El desafío que te espera

Buscamos Especialistas de Control para integrarse al Centro Remoto, contribuyendo a la gestión operacional de procesos asociados a operaciones mina, gestión de flota y tecnologías avanzadas de control operacional.

El rol será responsable de monitorear y coordinar la ejecución del plan operacional en tiempo real, optimizando el desempeño de los equipos y recursos productivos, gestionando desviaciones operacionales y contribuyendo a una operación segura, estable y eficiente.

Buscamos profesionales capaces de analizar múltiples fuentes de información, tomar decisiones oportunas bajo condiciones dinámicas y contribuir al desarrollo de una operación cada vez más digital, conectada y automatizada. Basado en competencias identificadas en los roles de autonomía relacionados con control operacional, gestión de flota, análisis de desempeño y toma de decisiones en tiempo real.

Responsabilidades:

•    Monitorear y controlar variables operacionales críticas asociadas a la ejecución del plan mina.

•    Gestionar la utilización y desempeño de equipos de carguío y transporte.

•    Analizar desviaciones operacionales y ejecutar acciones correctivas para minimizar impactos productivos.

•    Coordinar acciones con operaciones, mantenimiento y otras áreas para asegurar la continuidad operacional.

•    Gestionar contingencias operacionales y escalamientos de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos.

•    Analizar información operacional en tiempo real para optimizar el rendimiento de los activos.

•    Participar en iniciativas de mejora continua, digitalización y optimización operacional.

•    Promover el cumplimiento de estándares de seguridad, sustentabilidad y excelencia operacional.

•    Participar activamente en procesos de entrenamiento y transferencia de conocimiento dentro del equipo.

Lo que esperamos de ti

Buscamos profesionales con experiencia en operaciones mina y gestión de flota, que se sientan cómodos trabajando en entornos tecnológicos, tomando decisiones en tiempo real y coordinando operaciones de alta complejidad.

•    Título profesional de Ingeniería Civil o Ejecución en Minas, Industrial o carrera afín.

•    Mínimo 3 años de experiencia en operaciones mina.

•    Experiencia en despacho mina, gestión de flota, centros integrados de operación o salas de control.

•    Experiencia gestionando flotas de carguío y transporte.

•    Deseable experiencia en operaciones autónomas, semiautónomas o tecnologías avanzadas de control operacional.

•    Inglés intermedio deseable para interpretación de documentación técnica.

•    Certificaciones OEM, cuando corresponda.

•    Certificaciones de control de procesos, gestión de flota, despacho, autonomía o tecnologías operacionales, según especialidad

•    Experiencia en sistemas de gestión de flota (FMS).

•    Experiencia en plataformas de despacho o monitoreo operacional.

•    Experiencia en tecnologías de automatización y autonomía minera.

•    Conocimiento de indicadores de producción, utilización, disponibilidad y rendimiento de flota.

•    Experiencia en ambientes de operación remota y centros de control integrados

Experiencia en configuración, administración, optimización o soporte de sistemas de gestión de flota, plataformas de automatización, tecnologías de autonomía o herramientas de modelamiento operacional.

Ubicación: Santiago.

Por qué te encantará trabajar aquí

En BHP Chile entendemos que para dar lo mejor, necesitas sentirte bien. Por eso, nuestros beneficios están diseñados para acompañarte en cada etapa, cuidando tu salud, impulsando tu desarrollo y promoviendo un equilibrio real entre tu vida personal y laboral.

Desarrollo profesional: Formación continua y oportunidades reales de crecimiento.

Remuneración: justa y competitiva que refleje tu rol, habilidades y logros.

Cultura inclusiva: Promovemos un entorno laboral donde cada persona se siente valorada, respetada y libre de expresar su identidad auténtica.

Reconocimiento: Te recompensamos por tus pequeños y grandes logros a través de nuestro programa global de reconocimiento Big Thanks | Muchas Gracias.

¡Y mucho más!

Apoyamos una fuerza laboral diversa

En BHP nos adherimos a la Ley de Inclusión 21.015.

Sabemos que la diversidad nos fortalece. Es por eso por lo que estamos enfocados en crear una fuerza laboral más diversa que represente las comunidades en las que operamos y vivimos, asegurando un ambiente laboral donde cada persona sea incluida y tratada con respeto.

En ese sentido, estamos comprometidos a realizar un proceso de selección justo, equitativo y accesible para todos. Si tienes algún tipo de discapacidad, por favor escríbenos a inclusion@bhp.com para poder ajustar nuestro proceso de selección y brindarte el apoyo necesario.

Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority, all opinions are valued, and people are empowered to grow in their career. 
Apply Today!     

Where You Will Work   

Located approximately 50 miles northeast of Safford, Arizona on U.S. Highway 191, Morenci operations (an open-pit copper mining complex) has been in continuous operation since 1939. The operation consists of two concentrators, crushed-ore leach pad and stacking system, a low-grade run-of-mine (ROM) leaching system; four SX plants; and three EW tank houses that produce copper cathode.  

Morenci is a unique company town where our employees and their families can reconnect with nature through hiking, fishing, camping, hunting and numerous parks. The company offers several amenities, including company housing OR employees who are required to work on-site are eligible for a $750 monthly housing allowance, provided they meet program guidelines, a newly constructed daycare and community center, library, health-care facilities, state-of-the-art fitness centers, a movie theater and a skate park. Our dedicated Parks and Recreation Division plans activities for people of all ages, making sure there’s something for everyone to enjoy. Visit the Morenci town 
website
 to learn more. 

What You Will Do

You provide leadership, management, direction, and advanced problem solving for Process Automation while reviewing and improving the performance of site Industrial Control Systems. You lead and promote safety and environmental programs, communicate safety implications related to Process Automation, and direct Industrial Control System cybersecurity practices.

In this role, you lead and manage others by providing technical direction and guidance to direct reports on Process Automation Engineering topics, review engineering project proposals and designs to ensure work meets site Process Automation standards, and guide performance of ICS hardware and software to identify automation‑driven improvements that enhance operator and operations effectiveness. As the Senior Process Automation Engineer, you direct implementation and maintenance of the Process Control Network while maintaining plant performance, cybersecurity, and historian systems.

You approve specialized analytical and advanced instrumentation solutions, manage automation equipment life‑cycle planning, proposals, and budget estimates, and perform other duties as required.

What You Bring To Freeport

Bachelor’s degree in an Engineering discipline
and
five (5) years of related experience in engineering relevant to Process Automation or a related field
including
three (3) years of experience with regulatory and advanced control systems

OR

Master’s degree in an appropriate Engineering discipline
and
three (3) years of related experience in engineering relevant to Process Automation or a related field
including
three (3) years of experience with regulatory and advanced control systems

Preferred Qualifications

Previous supervision and leadership experience

PLC, HMI, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) and/or Distributed Control Systems (DCS) manufacture training or certification

Experience with plant process historians or similar database storage and retrieval systems

Experience with ICS/PCN network architecture, communication, and security

Experience in or understanding of mining and mineral processing systems

Familiarity with or training in NFPA 70, NEC, or Electrical Journeyman Training

What We Offer You

$97,500-$138,000
. This range reflects base salary only and does not include bonus payments, benefits or retirement contributions. Actual base pay is determined by experience, qualifications, skills and other job-related factors. This role is eligible for additional discretionary and incentive payment considerations based on company and individual performance. More details will be shared during the hiring process.

jobs.description:
Why You Should Apply for This Job  

At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing an employment package that recognizes excellence, encourages safe production and a culture supported by our core values. Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority, all opinions are valued, and people are empowered to grow in their career.
Apply Today!

Where You Will Work    

Our global headquarters is in Phoenix, Arizona. Several hundred employees support global operations in finance, human resources, information technology, planning and more from the main office, satellite offices or online. As a Hybrid employee, you’ll engage in virtual collaboration as well as attend in-person meetings at our Collaboration Hub in Phoenix or at one of our site locations. The Collaboration Hub provides an open, flexible workspace for individuals and teams to come together for various business needs. Amenities at the Hub include a working café, phone booths and meeting rooms with technology tools for virtual and in-person collaboration. In-person attendance may vary based on the position and department requirements. 

Phoenix is the capital of the Grand Canyon State and enjoys mostly bright skies throughout the year. It is the perfect place if you enjoy the outdoors, love sports, concerts and other big city amenities or technology. There are great neighborhoods around Phoenix, with easy access to a major city, nature, the arts and many more amenities.  

What You Will Do

Lead project engineering outcomes across a portfolio of capital projects, providing technical leadership in Process Engineering, Process Automation, and Instrumentation disciplines. Oversee the delivery lifecycle from concept and design through commissioning and operational ramp-up, ensuring projects achieve performance targets and reach nameplate capacity. Coordinate and align cross-functional teams, strategically deploy technical talent to maximize project execution success, and foster collaboration across operations, project delivery teams, and external engineering partners. Drive engineering consistency, innovation, and continuous improvement while ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient project delivery.

Develop and execute enterprise-wide Process Engineering, Automation, and Instrumentation strategies that support business objectives and operational excellence.

Prioritize project portfolio investments and strategically allocate engineering resources based on project risk, complexity, and stage of development.

Lead, coach, and develop multidisciplinary engineering teams, fostering a culture of safety, accountability, collaboration, and timely decision-making.

Provide oversight of process design activities, including flowsheets, mass and energy balances, while driving improvements in plant performance, recovery, throughput, and efficiency.

Lead Process Safety Management (PSM) programs and hazard assessment activities throughout engineering, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operational phases.

Establish continuous improvement processes that leverage operational feedback to optimize designs, enhance reliability, and prevent recurring issues.

Develop and standardize instrumentation strategies, ensuring effective specification, implementation, commissioning, start-up, and operational readiness across projects.

Define process control philosophies, oversee integration of DCS, PLC, and SCADA systems, and champion advanced digital technologies, including APC and predictive analytics, through strong IT/OT partnerships.

Provide technical leadership across the full project lifecycle, ensuring compliance with engineering standards and regulatory requirements while achieving safety, cost, schedule, and performance objectives.

Perform other duties as required.

Five (5) years of leadership experience managing engineering teams

Demonstrated experience supporting capital project delivery in the technical functions

Strong leadership and organizational skills with the ability to influence across functions

Excellent communication and stakeholder management capabilities

Strategic thinker with strong problem-solving abilities

Ability to build and lead cross-functional teams where engineers report by process area, not discipline

Ability to operate effectively in a complex, matrixed organization

jobs.title: Defence Security & Compliance Officer
jobs.description:
The Power of Now

Be part of something big. Fortescue is leading the world with our plan to decarbonise our iron ore operations, projects that harness renewable energy and the development of technology that will change our planet forever.

An opportunity has arisen for a Defence Security & Compliance Officer to join the Motorsport & Advanced Engineering. 

About the role

The Defence Security & Compliance Officer ensures the company adheres to strict regulations, such as export controls (e.g., ITAR/EAR), and manages security protocols for sensitive defence information and systems. Managing security vetting (BPSS), protect personnel and technical assets, and ensure compliance with UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) and customer standards

What you will do

Implementing Security Standards:
 Developing, implementing, and maintaining security policies, standards, and procedures across the organisation, aligned with Def-Stan 05-0138 and GovS 007

Security Assurance and Audit:
 Establishing and supporting security auditing, monitoring, and assessment capabilities to ensure data systems and business areas comply with legal and regulatory requirements (e.g., DPIAs, SyOPs)

Risk Management:
 Identifying, managing, and mitigating security risks, including those arising from third-party suppliers, delivery partners, and supply chains

Incident Response:
 Ensuring correct procedures and delegations are in place to respond to security incidents and breaches and assisting with investigations

Training and Awareness:
 Promoting best practices by developing training and engagement activities related to data protection and security

Leadership and Governance:
 Providing leadership on operational security matters, often involving cross-divisional collaboration

Key Skills and Experience

Regulatory Knowledge:
 Deep understanding of HMG security policies and standards (GovS 007 & Def-Stan 05-0138)

Technical Expertise:
 Knowledge of security auditing, risk assessment, and data protection mechanisms

Stakeholder Management:
 Ability to engage with various business areas and external suppliers

About you

Strong working knowledge of 
UK GovS 007
 and how it applies to a defence contractor environment 

Experience leading a security function covering 
personnel, physical, information and contract security

Confidence operating as a senior security point of contact with 
government and external agencies
and
reporting to the Senior Leadership Team

Ability to interpret and advise on 
emerging threats, geopolitical developments and defence sector risks

Experience delivering 
security training and awareness
, including inductions and briefings 

Experience planning and managing 
international visits

Strong leadership skills, with the ability to manage, develop and motivate

Demonstrated leadership potential alongside effective communication skills

Support Programme Management requirements and Business Development/Strategy requirements within the Defence sector

Must be able to achieve and maintain Base Line Security Clearance (BPSS) for this role.

Ability to travel outside the UK

What is in it for you?

Our UK benefits include:

Bonus scheme

Aviva Pension

Group Life Assurance

Group Income Protection

Electric Car Scheme

Health Cash Plan

Employee Assistance Programme

Private Medical Insurance

26 days holiday
plus
public holidays and the opportunity to purchase an additional 5 days per year

jobs.title: Process Plant Operator – Fixed Term Contract Fly In/Fly Out - Gahcho Kué Mine, NWT
jobs.locationRaw: Gahcho Kué Mine, NORTHWEST TERRITORIES, Canada
jobs.description:
Be part of the team. The team that makes it happen.

We are the world’s leading diamond company, powered by thousands of people around the world who are driven to support thriving local communities, protect the natural environment, and stand with women and girls, focused on Building Forever.

If you like chasing demanding targets, thrive on making decisions in the pursuit of brilliance, and enjoy the support of the world’s finest experts, we have a place for you.

De Beers Group has an exciting full-time opportunity for a motivated and energetic individual to join the Process Plant Team at the Gahcho Kué Mine Site based in the Northwest Territories. Reporting to the Process Plant Supervisor and working a 14 day on/14 day off rotation, this position is responsible for ensuring optimum plant operations to maximize throughput and diamond recovery. The successful candidate will demonstrate a commitment to all security policies and report any issues that may harm the people, environment, information or product. The ideal candidate is one who is committed to safe working practices and strives for zero harm.

This is a contract position with an end date June 2027.

Rewards & Benefits:

Eligible for the Quarterly Bonus program;

Remote Mine Site Allowance;

Salary Enhancement for working in the NWT;

Immediate participation in our 100% employer-paid extended health and dental benefits program (no waiting period);

Relocation support is available to anyone who wishes to move to the Northwest Territories;

The Gahcho Kué Mine camp features a full-service dining room, and individual private bedrooms equipped with satellite cable television, telephones, and WiFi internet. There’s also a full-sized gymnasium, squash courts, and state-of-the-art fitness equipment.

Key responsibilities:

Operating the crushers, rock breakers, scrubbers, conveyors, vibrating screens, pumps, thickeners, dense media separation and recovery specific equipment; and/or

Monitoring and inspecting plant equipment and systems to detect equipment malfunctions and ensure plant systems are operating normally;

Recording process data and reporting any deviations to plant conditions or parameters to minimize plant delays and breakdowns;

Completing and maintaining plant logs and reports;

Maintaining areas and responsibilities according to standard operating procedures and preventative maintenance;

Reporting to the Process Plant Supervisor this is a site-based position with two (2) weeks in/ two (2) weeks out rotation.

Experience on small mobile equipment;

Strong communication skills;

Proven commitment to Safety, Health and Environmental standards.

Please note, preference will be given to Members of the Deninu Kué, Lutsel K’e Dene First Nation, North Slave Métis Alliance, Northwest Territory Métis Nation, Tlicho Government, or Yellowknives Dene First Nation, followed by non-indigenous residents of the Northwest Territories.

Who We Are:

Active in Canada for over 60 years, we are part of De Beers Group, the world's leading diamond company. Globally, we are a team of more than 20,000 people, with operations in Canada, Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa, and activities across the diamond value chain from exploration to diamond jewelry retail. Our unwavering focus on sustainability and Building Forever fuels our commitment to advance standards across the diamond industry, protect the natural world, partner with local communities, and accelerate economic inclusion to support diversity in our business and beyond.

In Canada, we have more than 600 employees working at offices in Calgary, Toronto and Yellowknife, actively exploring for new diamond opportunities, recovering diamonds at the joint venture Gahcho Kué mine in the Northwest Territories, and closing and rehabilitating two mines. We are also advancing the Chidliak Project to establish a technologically advanced diamond mine on Baffin Island using FutureSmart Mining™ principles.

At De Beers, we believe in the power of working in partnership with communities to create lasting, positive impacts that endure long after we recover the last diamond. Our inclusive and diverse workplace values mining with respect for the environment and nearby communities, and we seek team players who share our passion for Making Life Brilliant.

Safety

Safety first is a way of life for us. We are unconditional about the safety, health, and the well-being of our colleagues, at work and at home, and about that of the communities where we work. We aim to lead the industry by investing in innovation to protect people, who are at the heart of our business. Our high performing teams take accountability for their own and others' actions, work collaboratively, and always show care and respect
.

Equity, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI)

As a global #HeForShe Thematic Champion, De Beers is committed to promoting an equitable, inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are. What You Will Do

Safely performs duties related to the operation and minor maintenance of locomotive equipment and railroad tracks at a highly skilled level.

In this role, you are responsible for the knowledge and safe performance of procedures for working on or near railroad tracks, including the use of chains and slings and inspection for defects, crossing from one side of a train to the other, Blue Stake procedures, reading blueprints for proper building of switches, and illustrating standard crane signals.

As the Locomotive Operator II, you perform track inspections, general track work, flagging trains, opening and closing boxcars, and re‑railing cars after train derailments, and may perform minor track maintenance duties such as lubricating switches and using track wrenches and pneumatic tools to tighten nuts and bolts on railroad tracks.

You may load, unload, and cut bands from railroad tie bundles, transport materials, recognize and report defects on equipment and tools, identify and repair defective track switches, and identify and repair defective rail.

Duties also include building track panels, handling and laying track sections, operating ballast regulators, performing ballast train dumping operations, operating spot tampers, track maintainers, and crane cars, and operating track drills, track saws, truck‑mounted hoists, backhoes, hi‑rail trucks, boom trucks, forklifts, and hydraulic front‑end loaders.

You train and mentor co‑workers and may perform brakeman and switchman duties, including handling, coupling, and uncoupling acid, freight, and concentrate railcars, performing railcar brake inspections, weighing and inspecting railcars, and ensuring proper and safe securing of railcars.

You are responsible for the safe movement of freight trains and railcar switching in rail yards, providing clear hand and radio signals to locomotive operators, demonstrating knowledge and safe performance of locomotive horn signals, riding positions, mounting and dismounting moving trains and locomotives, use of hand brakes, proper alignment of railroad track switches, hand and lantern signals, establishing car clearances, crossing over railcars, spotting railcars, connecting multi‑unit locomotive air hoses, performing locomotive engineer duties including the operation of single and multiple unit locomotives, completing pre‑shift equipment inspections, performing minor maintenance and operations support activities, and performing other duties as required.

Two (2) years of locomotive operating experience.

Knowledge of the proper use and performance of railroad track jacks.

Knowledge of the proper use and performance of claw bars to move rails and spiking or spacing hammers to insert spikes.

Knowledge of locomotive mechanical and electrical functions and locomotive air systems.

High Scool Diploma or GED

Railroad Transportation experience
