jobs.description:
FUGRO CHILE S.A, compañía especializada en geotecnia, geofísica y levantamiento de datos con sede en Santiago, Chile. Los servicios de Fugro Chile S.A. se enfocan hacia un rango amplio de sectores: minería, energía, gestión recursos naturales, planificación urbana, proyectos ambientales y de ingeniería.
Dado que estamos en constante adjudicación de nuevos proyectos es que te invitamos a sumarte en nuestro equipo como “Experto en Prevención de Riesgos”, quien tendrá como objetivo principal brindar soporte especializado en la gestión preventiva de Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional, Medio Ambiente y Calidad en proyectos de clientes mineros, asegurando la correcta implementación de políticas, procedimientos y estándares definidos por la compañía y el mandante. El cargo tiene como propósito fortalecer la continuidad operacional mediante la identificación temprana de riesgos, la promoción de prácticas seguras y el apoyo directo al equipo en terreno, contribuyendo al cumplimiento normativo y a la mejora continua en materia QHSSE.

Principales funciones:
1. Realizar difusiones de Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Medio Ambiente.
2. Realizar inducción de hombre nuevo (IRL) y de RIOHS al personal. Participación y/o Elaboración de informes de gestión, informes de cierre de eventos/hallazgos, cierre de inspecciones que surjan de las actividades realizadas en proyectos, taller, oficina o laboratorio.
3. Mantener la información documental de manera ordenada y al día, en materia de SST y MA.
4. Revisión de ART, check list y/o herramientas preventivas de áreas asignadas.
5. Realizar inspecciones de áreas en materias de Seguridad y Medio Ambiente.
6. Realizar actividades de SST y MA que se indiquen, para atender solicitudes de la corporación y/o cliente.
7. Preparación de documentos, imprimir documentación asociada a la acreditación, credenciales, material para señalética, formatos, cartas, planillas, entre otros, que se requieran para dar continuidad al avance de temas de SST y MA de la empresa.
8. Participar activamente en la elaboración de carpetas de arranque de los proyectos, si se le asigna. Inscripción y monitoreo de cursos en portal de mutualidad.
9. Realizar, revisar y/o actualizar matriz de riegos o cualquier otro documento de SSTMA que se requiera. Si es necesario, prestar apoyo en difusiones, capacitaciones, elaboración de documentos en general u otros, con el fin de colaborar con las acreditaciones de personal de los proyectos.
10. Coordinar, ejecutar y cumplir el programa de prevención de riesgos de la empresa y sus derivados. Informa a su jefatura directa o indirecta de defectos o fallas, condición insegura o sub- estándar en herramientas o instalaciones, que puede ser causa de lesiones a las personas o daño al equipo e instalaciones.
11. Cumplir con el Reglamento Interno de Orden, Higiene y Seguridad. 12. Cuidar y hacer uso obligatorio de sus elementos de protección personal, además de hacer cumplir el uso de ellos a su personal a cargo.
13. Garantizar el orden y limpieza de las instalaciones, mediante el uso de recursos a su alcance.
14. Participar activamente en temáticas de Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Medio Ambiente vigentes en la compañía, como en la del mandante, a fin de evitar accidentes, lesiones e impactos negativos al medio ambiente y cumplir la normativa local.
15. Actuando ante un evento no deseado en cumplimiento de la ley y de los lineamientos de la organización asociados a la ética y políticas.
16. Eventualmente conducir vehículos livianos previa autorización.
17. Compromiso con la Seguridad y el Cumplimiento: Verificar cumplimiento de normas y procedimientos.
18. Cumplir con las actividades del Programa de Liderazgo QHSSE. Comunicación Efectiva: Retroalimentar al personal y coordinar acciones.
19. Attractive package on the Dawson EBA: $210,481.98 Package + Performance Bonus!

Closest large Mine to South-East QLD – it’s a lifestyle!

Dawson Mine

Steelmaking Coal is an essential ingredient in blast-furnace steel manufacture, producing steel used for critical building and infrastructure around the world.

Dawson Mine is a large and dynamic open cut steelmaking coal mine operation made up of two operating pits – Central and South. It commenced operations in 1961 and is one of the oldest coal mining operations in Central Queensland. Dawson Mine was the first mine in Australia to export coal to Japan in 1961 and was the first mine to introduce draglines into its operation in 1963.

We would like to invite applications from experienced Dragline Operators to join our Dawson Operation in Moura, QLD on a full-time permanent basis. The Dawson operation is a large open-cut coal mining operation showing no signs of slowing down! You will work as part of a team operating our BE1370 & Marion 8200 Draglines to produce Steelmaking Coal whilst demonstrating safe working behaviours and practices to achieve set targets.

To be successful for this position, you will ideally hold:

Be an experienced dragline operator with Dozer skills.

Demonstrated knowledge in dragline set up, operations and dig methods.

Provide proof of your operating experience.

Display excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

Be a team player with a safety first mindset.

Drive optimization and continuous performance improvement.

Full-time permanent position available at our Dawson Mine site

Attractive package on the Dawson EBA: $210,481.98 Package + Performance Bonus!

Employed under the Dawson Mines Collective Enterprise Agreement 2024

Lifestyle 5/4/4/5 Roster

Residential and Drive-in-Drive-Out options

Company funded camp accommodation available

Competitive Remuneration & Incentives on the Enterprise Agreement

What we Offer

When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programmes, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too. We’re a large, successful multinational company – and we’re still growing all the time.

Who we are

We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies. As the custodians of coal and other precious natural resources – diamonds (through De Beers), copper, platinum and other precious metals, iron ore and nickel – our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively, with the utmost consideration for local communities, our customers and the world at large.

Background checks

Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

jobs.description:
About the Company

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear – even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models—alongside our novel sensors—to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. Since our founding in 2018, KoBold has become by far both the largest independent mineral exploration company and the largest exploration technology developer. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 60 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the Role

In this role, you will own the computation hydrogeology program for KoBold’s exploration projects, including pre-feasibility and feasibility engineering studies. You will help to create water management strategies that maximize the safety, feasibility, and value of future mines. Working closely with field hydrogeologists, mining engineers, and computational scientists, you will lead the development and execution of numerical simulations necessary for quantitative evaluation of the strategies you develop. Your analyses and groundwater flow models will be an integral component of KoBold’s dynamic mine-planning and mine-operations technology.

You will join an outstanding team of geoscientists, data scientists, and software engineers. You will be a core part of the project teams, advancing the science and practice of exploration. In addition to contributing to the development of novel data collection programs, you will work closely with geologists and data scientists to build physics-based and data-driven models of the hydrogeology of our exploration sites. A key challenge will be to quantify uncertainties relevant to mining, and to identify efficient means for reducing these uncertainties as the project advances.

Responsibilities

The Computational Hydrogeologist will:

Develop multiple alternative groundwater management strategies and quality metrics

Identify data and information needed to evaluate the efficacy of a proposed strategy, differentiate the system response from other possible strategies, and compare the strengths and weaknesses of various water management actions

Design data collection programs required to inform evaluation analyses and work with field teams to develop methodologies for execution

Build and run computational analyses, including numerical simulations of groundwater flow, post-processing algorithms for hydrogeologic insights, and uncertainty quantification

Work with data scientists to develop novel approaches and tools to extract value from results

Qualifications

A great Hydrogeologist candidate will have:

Bachelor's or post-graduate degree in hydrogeology, geology, computational geoscience, geological or environmental engineering, or closely related discipline

6-10 years of work experience, including at least 2 years in mining hydrogeology

Experience with the design and implementation of water management strategies for mining applications

Experience with the design and implementation of hydrogeologic field studies

Deep expertise in computational modeling of porous media flows and coupled groundwater/surface-water systems

Experience analyzing hydrogeologic data to support the development of conceptual and numerical models of groundwater flow, including familiarity with modeling software such as MODFLOW or FEFLOW

Enthusiasm for developing novel mathematical models, both physics-based and data-driven

Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain. Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights through using our tools in exploration and willing to work directly with geologists in the field.

Ability to explain technical problems to and collaborate on solutions with domain experts who are not technical. A strong communicator who enjoys working with colleagues across the company.

Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on an evolving range of responsibilities.

Keen not just to build cool technology, but to figure out what technical product to build to best achieve the business objectives of the company.

What to Expect

Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.

About the Role

In this role, you will lead evaluations of potential properties for staking, partnering or acquisition, generate targets, and design and oversee field programs from target definition through to resource expansion. You will be part of a multidisciplinary team and will work closely with data scientists, using KoBold’s technology to help guide our field programs and decision-making. You will also work directly with our senior technical advisors and with the executive team on making the investment case for acquisitions and field programs.

Ultimately, your role is to help KoBold make valuable discoveries by identifying opportunities with rigorous evaluation and by ensuring that we safely and effectively conduct our field programs.

Responsibilities

Demonstrate in all activities a commitment to the highest standards in health and safety, environment, and community relations

Rigorously analyze geoscientific datasets across a range of scales from provinces to prospects to determine exploration potential and to identify, rank, and prioritize exploration targets

Design, budget, permit, and execute field programs ranging from geological mapping and sampling of grass roots prospects through to large drilling programs on advanced projects, with leading industry practice in data acquisition and validation

Provide technical guidance and support to local in-country project teams during the design and execution of exploration programs, including site visits and engagement with other project stakeholders (e.g., community representatives, regulatory authorities, and joint venture partners)

Work collaboratively with data scientist colleagues to conceive and implement insightful analytical methods

Assist in local community engagement and stakeholder communications.

Qualifications

A great Exploration Geologist candidate will have:

Strong technical knowledge of one or more ore deposit types. Experience working on sediment-hosted stratiform copper, magmatic sulfide or lithium deposits will be considered an advantage

Excellence in generative analysis ranging from new concepts to integration, interpretation, and modeling of large datasets

Good field skills and experience conducting field programs across a range of project stages from grassroots prospects through to advanced projects with significant drilling campaigns

Baseline level of proficiency in standard desktop software packages (e.g., ArcGIS or QGIS)

Strong leadership skills including the ability to motivate and inspire others, to share ownership and responsibility for project outcomes, and to work effectively in collaborative, interdisciplinary teams

Previous experience in coaching and training geoscientists of varying experience, educational backgrounds and cultures in leading-practice mineral exploration

Demonstrated commitment to high standards of health and safety in the workplace

A minimum of 3-7 years experience in the mineral exploration industry

Fluent in French and resident within the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)

Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain. Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights through using our tools in exploration and willing to work directly with geologists in the field.

It is helpful but not required to have:

Working knowledge of one programming or scripting language (e.g., Python, R, C/C++)

Knowledge of geostatistics and/or other statistical methods relevant for analysis of geoscientific data

Experience across more than one mineral system, particularly if that includes mineralization within felsic igneous systems, or in the Central African Copperbelt.

What to Expect

Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.

KoBold Metals is an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunities for people of any race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, age, citizenship, disability, or veteran status.

This position is a full-time contract. At this time, we are only accepting applications from Congolese nationals.

Location: Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of Congo. All candidates must be legally authorized to live and work within Democratic

jobs.description:
Personal Assistant to the CEO, Zambia

About the company

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear – even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models—alongside our novel sensors—to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. Since our founding in 2018, KoBold has become by far both the largest independent mineral exploration company and the largest exploration technology developer. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 60 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is seeking to engage a Coordinator, Communities and Social Performance who will coordinate and support stakeholder engagement, land access processes, and agricultural compensation activities across the company’s exploration licenses. This role is central to building and maintaining trusted community relationships that enable the safe and effective advancement of KoBold’s exploration program.

About the Role

We're looking for a seasoned, high-judgment Personal Assistant to support KoBold's CEO in Zambia. This is not a junior administrative role. It is a strategic, anticipatory partnership with a CEO who moves fast, operates at the highest level, and expects her executive office to run with intentionality, precision, and pace.

You will be embedded in a Slack-first, remote-friendly culture where priorities shift quickly and the difference between smooth and chaotic is the person holding the calendar. You'll be trusted with sensitive information, high-visibility communications, and executive decisions that touch the full breadth of KoBold's Zambia operations.

We take hiring seriously because we're building a team, not filling a seat. If you move forward, you'll complete a timed written assessment designed to test your judgment, resourcefulness, and communication under pressure. From there, you'll interview with our EA team and, if you advance, with the CEO directly. Our EA team is tight-knit and genuinely invested in each other's success, and we're looking for someone who will add to that.

Responsibilities

Executive Support

Own the CEO's calendar as a strategic asset, not a scheduling tool. Design weeks so top priorities actually happen, build in intentional thinking time, and protect it fiercely

Sequence days for energy management, not just logistics, and eliminate low-value noise

Coordinate meetings across time zones spanning Zambia, the UK, South Africa, and the US; manage last-minute changes without losing composure

Arrange domestic and international travel including flights, hotels, and ground transport, with contingency plans built in and the ability to adjust on the fly

Triage inbound requests and route communications so only what truly requires the CEO's attention reaches her

Ensure decisions are teed up and prepared, not discovered at the last minute

Prepare agendas and briefing materials so the CEO walks into every meeting ready

Take notes and track follow-ups when requested

Handle expense reports, approvals, and administrative tasks with speed and accuracy

Identify emerging issues early and surface risks and options before they become urgent

Qualifications

You are a high-judgment operator who runs an executive's world end to end. You don't need to be told what to do twice, and you don't need hand-holding to get things done. You are proactive and anticipatory: turning ambiguity into structure and staying two steps ahead rather than one step behind.

You are a strong gatekeeper with warmth and professionalism. You manage the flow, trade-offs, and constraints of a busy executive office with clarity and confidence. You communicate with precision: short, clear, no fluff, because you know everyone around you is busy. You treat sensitive information as if it were your own.

You bring positive energy to every collaboration and stay calm and decisive under pressure. You understand that you are often the messenger in the middle, and you don't take a curt Slack reply personally.

Minimum Qualifications

Based in Zambia (Lusaka strongly preferred)

7+ years supporting senior executives, ideally at the CEO level, in a fast-moving environment

Exceptional calendar management and organizational skills; you have owned multi-step workflows with multiple stakeholders before and understand that the calendar is the strategy

Strong gatekeeping instincts: you know what should reach the CEO and what shouldn't, and you enforce that with professionalism

Able and willing to travel domestically and internationally at a moment's notice; this role requires genuine mobility, not just theoretical flexibility

Available outside of regular business hours and across time zones; KoBold operates globally and the pace of the executive office reflects that

Flawless attention to detail; you're the person who catches the issue before it becomes a problem

Comfortable in real-time communication tools (Slack preferred) and quick to learn new systems

Already experimenting with AI, or excited to learn

Professional, discreet, and unflappable under pressure

jobs.description:
About BHP

At BHP, we believe our purpose goes beyond mining: we work to improve lives and create a more sustainable future. We are a global resources company with operations in more than 90 locations worldwide.

In Canada, our presence is growing with the development of 
one of the most significant potash projects in the world; Jansen.
This project reflects our long-term commitment to sustainability, community engagement, and economic growth
.

About Potash and the Jansen Project

Imagine being part of something truly world-class, something that’s shaping the future of sustainable agriculture and responsible resource development. That’s what the Jansen Potash Project offers.

Located about 140 kilometers east of Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, 

Jansen is set to become one of the world’s largest potash mines.

With a US$15.3 billion investment, it marks the biggest private investment in Saskatchewan’s history, and a bold step forward for BHP in Canada.

But Jansen is more than a mine; it’s a

long-term opportunity to build something meaningful.

During construction, it will create around 5,500 jobs and once operations are fully ramped up, 900 permanent roles. Whether you're looking to grow your career, contribute to a sustainable future, or be part of a legacy project, Jansen could be the place where it all begins.

Why BHP?

At BHP, we are transforming the way mining is done. We embrace innovation, sustainability, and inclusion to build a smarter, safer, and more human future.

We are proud to be recognized as
one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers for 2026,
a testament to our dedication to fostering a positive, diverse, and rewarding work environment. At BHP, you’ll be part of a team that values safety, integrity, performance, and collaboration.

The Challenge Ahead

Reporting to the Manager Tax, Canada, the Specialist Tax (Canada) plays a key role in managing Canadian corporate, regional, and international tax matters. This role provides expert tax advice to internal stakeholders and supports BHP in meeting its tax compliance, reporting, and governance obligations in a complex and evolving regulatory environment
.

Key Responsibilities

Assist in coordinating, preparing, and filing Canadian federal and provincial corporate income tax returns

Support the preparation and filing of royalty tax and indirect tax returns

Assist in responding to and engaging with tax auditors

Prepare tax provisions and financial information in line with IFRS requirements

Provide analysis and guidance on tax-related note disclosures for IFRS financial statements

Conduct tax research and analysis to support compliance, reporting, and advisory activities

Provide tax and business advice related to new and existing business transactions

Prepare and, where required, review complex tax calculations, modelling, and analytics

Analyze new tax legislation and assess impacts to BHP’s Canadian and global operations

Participate in cross-functional working groups, providing recommendations to management

Support the development and maintenance of efficient internal tax processes

Build strong working relationships with internal teams and external advisors

What You’ll Bring to the Role

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or equivalent

CPA designation or similar professional qualification

Completion of CPA Canada In-Depth Tax or a Master’s of Tax (asset)

Experience in public accounting and/or industry

Strong experience in Canadian federal and provincial corporate tax

Experience with tax accounting under IFRSERP system experience (SAP preferred)

Mining industry and/or international tax experience considered an asset

Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders

Work Location

This role is based in
Saskatoon, Saskatchewan
, working from BHP’s downtown office. BHP supports
hybrid working arrangements
, combining office-based work with flexibility to work from home. The role is full-time, 40 hours per week.

Why You'll Love Working Here

At BHP, we understand that to bring your best, you need to feel your best. That’s why our benefits are designed to support your health, your growth, and your personal balance.

Professional Development:
Continuous learning and real opportunities for growth

Compensation:
Fair and competitive, reflecting your role, skills, and achievements

Inclusive Culture:
A workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and able to be their authentic self

And so much more!

About Our Process

At BHP, we are committed to employing individuals who align with the BHP Charter Values and meet the requirements of the role. As part of the recruitment process, checks may be conducted including police/criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks, and/or reference checks.

Why Not You?

With operations worldwide, BHP offers limitless opportunities. Whether it’s competitive benefits, international career pathways, or the chance to be part of a world-class project like Jansen, at BHP you can shape a career that’s truly yours. If you're looking for a place where your work has purpose, your growth is supported, and your impact is real, this could be your next step.

We Support a Diverse Workforce

At BHP, we believe diversity makes us stronger. We’re committed to creating a safe, inclusive workplace where everyone is treated fairly and can thrive. Our workforce reflects the communities where we operate, and we value all aspects of identity; gender, age, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, education, and more.

We ensure our recruitment process is fair, accessible, and equitable. If you have a disability and require adjustments, please contact

About Copper SA Operations at BHP

BHP is a global resources company operating across more than 90 locations worldwide, with a purpose to improve lives and support a more sustainable future.

Through Copper South Australia (Copper SA), we are building a leading copper portfolio that supports the global energy transition, supplying materials essential for renewable energy, electric vehicles and digital infrastructure.

For you, this is an exciting opportunity to grow your career, make a meaningful impact, and help shape the future of one of Australia's leading copper businesses.

About Olympic Dam

Olympic Dam is Australia’s largest world-class underground mining operations, featuring a highly advanced on-site metallurgical processing plant in South Australia. It offers the opportunity to build a long-term career in a dynamic and future-focused environment.

As part of BHP, you’ll work at a large and complex site that produces copper, uranium, gold and silver, using modern technology and innovative practices.

Located approximately 560km north of Adelaide on the traditional lands of the Kokatha, Arabana and Barngarla people, Olympic Dam is a cornerstone asset within BHP’s Minerals Australia portfolio, known for its scale, innovation, and strong focus on safety and performance.

With ongoing investment, including over A$840 million in near-term growth capital, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, develop future-ready skills, and contribute to meeting the world’s increasing demand for copper and a more sustainable future.

a Project Engineer
, reporting to the
Surface Asset Integrity Remediation Team within Integrated Operations
.

The Challenge Ahead

As a
Project Engineer
, you will play a key role in remediating critical surface assets across Olympic Dam to ensure a safe, reliable platform for ongoing operations and future growth. Working as part of the Surface Asset Integrity Remediation Team, you will contribute to the successful delivery of a portfolio of remediation projects in a complex mining and minerals processing environment.

This role offers a unique opportunity to combine engineering expertise, stakeholder engagement and project delivery capability to support one of Australia's most significant mining assets. You will work closely with operational, technical and governance stakeholders to develop practical, safe and sustainable remediation solutions that maximise value and minimise disruption to production.

What You'll Bring to the Role

We're looking for an experienced engineering professional who enjoys solving complex challenges, collaborating across multidisciplinary teams and delivering outcomes safely and efficiently.

You will bring:

Degree qualifications in Structural Engineering, with additional qualifications in Project Management or Civil Engineering viewed favourably.

Experience or a strong understanding of mining, processing, heavy industry or construction environments. Exposure to structural steel and concrete remediation projects will be highly regarded.

Demonstrated capability in delivering projects or engineering studies.

Strong stakeholder engagement, collaboration and problem-solving skills.

The ability to manage competing priorities, coordinate contractors and work effectively across multiple workstreams.

Sound technical and commercial judgement, supported by clear communication and influencing skills.

The capability to develop concise reports and presentations for senior stakeholders.

In this role,
you will:

Lead by example and actively foster a culture of care and safety.

Review engineering assessments and identify structural remediation requirements.

Collaborate with operational stakeholders to ensure solutions are practical, effective and minimise production impacts.

Work closely with governance and technical stewardship teams to ensure compliance with relevant safety, engineering and design standards.

Develop scopes of work, manage tendering and support contractor selection processes.

Monitor project performance against scope, budget, schedule and delivery objectives.

Support the planning, execution and commissioning of remediation projects while effectively managing risks and maximising constructability outcomes.

Contribute to project reporting and uphold BHP Charter Values, Leadership expectations and Code of Business Conduct.

4/3 roster at Olympic Dam
and
a 5/2 arrangement in the Adelaide office
, with FIFO provided from Adelaide.

jobs.description:
Closing Date: Open Until Filled

Location:
Red Dog Mine, AK, United States

Employment Type:
Regular Full Time

Workplace Type:
On-site

About
Red Dog

Red Dog Operations is both the largest critical minerals mine in the United States and one of the largest zinc mines in the world. In 1982, Red Dog was developed through a partnership between Teck and the land-owner NANA, an Alaska Native corporation owned by the Iñupiat of northwest Alaska. The partnership between Teck and NANA ensures real benefits for the local Iñupiat community, while recognizing there is still more to do as we advance our commitment to sustainable practices and meaningful engagement.

Role Overview

Reporting to the Powerhouse Supervisor, the Powerhouse Operator Journeyperson installs, adjusts, maintains and repairs Diesel Engines, mechanical equipment and parts in power-generating stations.

Responsibilities:

Be a courageous safety leader, through promotion and adherence to established policies, procedures and safe work practices

Operate and maintains the Powerhouse, consisting of 8 ea. Wartsila 32-V16 engines, performs diesel engine repairs and maintenance as well as operates and maintains powerhouse auxiliary and support systems; cleans, lubricates parts, equipment and machinery as needed

Disassemble machinery and equipment to remove parts and make repairs; repair, replace, adjust, align components of machinery and equipment

Perform required Preventative Maintenance procedures

Troubleshoot equipment and examines parts for defects such as breakage or excessive wear; utilize hand tools, instruments and hydraulic tools to complete repairs and maintenance

Ensure all tools and equipment are maintained and kept in a clean and orderly condition

Journeyperson Level knowledge of diesel engines, turbochargers, fuel systems pumps and injectors, lube system pumps and filtration, cooling water system, charge air system, and Selective Catalytic Reduction systems

Respond appropriately to abnormal Switchgear readings (including gauges, digital read-outs for engine conditions, Kw, Voltage and Hertz), and alarms. Correctly interpret alarms indicated and reacting to the problem to ensure a constant supply of electrical power

Interact with a variety of employees on the property such as operators, engineering, trades and Supervisors on methods, procedures and hazards in order to coordinate the services of other trades and service personnel in the planning of their portion of the job; tests, inspect, evaluates , and observes operation of Power plant machinery and equipment to diagnose cause of malfunction

Maintain an accurate record of repairs and maintenance performed; tracks and places orders and requisition for parts and materials needed to complete job effectively; completes daily paperwork for engine data, performance and inspections

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of environmental risks and hazards as well as complies with safety policies and procedures (MSHA and Red Dog EMS training). Performs daily workplace inspections are completed in order to accurately identify and correct workplace hazards

Ensure compliance with all established policies and standard operating procedures. Advises coworkers and visitors of such policies and procedures as required

Perform other related duties as assigned

Qualifications:

High school diploma or GED equivalent

Seven (7) years' experience in operating and maintaining a Prime Power Diesel plant

Experience machining cylinder head surfaces/pockets and facing of valve seats

Ability to read and understand operations and maintenance manuals

Knowledge and maintenance experience of Wartsila diesel engines

Prior experience with fuel injectors, plate type heat exchangers, Turbochargers, pumps, piping systems, air handling units, waste heat recovery systems, air compressors, and selective catalytic reduction systems

Ability to adhere to high safety standards

Work day, afternoon, or night shifts as required

Team player and able to communicate well with others

Highly motivated and have ability to perform tasks with limited direction

Work outdoors with a potential exposure to extreme climatic conditions

Perform labor intensive work when required

Working Conditions:

Access:
Fly in, fly out

Schedule: We offer a two-weeks on / two-weeks off rotational schedule to support a healthy work-life balance.

Accommodation:
Our modern facilities, including dedicated spaces for group and individual physical activities, weights, cardio equipment, movie rooms, theme nights, and modern accommodation complexes. All meals are provided, making it easier for you to focus on your work and well-being.

Culture:
At Red Dog, we believe in fostering a safe and healthy environment for all our employees. We are proud to be a drug and alcohol-free workplace and will include a drug test as part of our hiring process.

Why Teck

At Teck, your work matters - to the world, to our communities and to your future.

As a leading Canadian resource company, we focus on responsibly providing the metals essential for global development and the energy transition while caring for the people, communities and land that we love. We do this guided by our values that, together, form The Teck Way. At Teck, you'll find purpose-driven work, a culture of respect and inclusion, and the opportunity to grow your career while helping build a better world.

Apply with us

Take the next step in your career by applying for the
Powerhouse Operator VI
role. We review applications on a rolling basis and encourage you to apply, even if your experience doesn't align perfectly with every requirement.

We offer competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits program, including medical, dental, life, AD&D, and long-term disability insurance, paid sick leave, vacation days, and a 401k plan. Our two-weeks on/two-weeks off schedule is designed to provide a better work-life balance for our employees.

The role includes support on international tax aspects adjacent to transactions including, but not limited to, capital structure, financing, cash repatriation.

Toronto, Ontario

The Corporate Secretary, Paralegal plays a critical role in supporting corporate governance, board administration, and legal operations. Prepare and maintain accurate meeting minutes, resolutions, and corporate records

Ensure compliance with corporate governance requirements and applicable regulatory obligations

Maintain corporate minute books, entity records, and governance documentation across jurisdictions

Support onboarding and ongoing training of Board members

Coordinate and liaise with external counsel and internally to support timely disclosures

Contract Review & Legal Support

Review, draft, and manage a wide range of contracts (e.g., vendor agreements, service contracts, NDAs)

Ensure contracts align with company policies, risk tolerance, and regulatory requirements

Track contract lifecycle, obligations, renewals, and key dates

Liaise with internal stakeholders and external counsel on legal matters

Assist in developing and maintaining contract templates and standard terms

Compliance & Risk Management

Support corporate compliance programs, including ethics, anti-corruption, and disclosure obligations

Assist with audits, due diligence, and regulatory filings

jobs.title: Assistant General Counsel, Employment
jobs.description:
About the Company

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear—even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models—alongside our novel sensors—to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. Since our founding in 2018, KoBold has become by far both the largest independent mineral exploration company and the largest exploration technology developer. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 60 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the Role

This in-house employment and litigation attorney will play an important role in building a global AI-driven clean-tech company that invents breakthrough technology, discovers billions of dollars of minerals, and helps to stop climate change.

Be an integral part of an in-house legal team in a technology and mineral exploration company growing rapidly around the world

Provide leverage and support to the CLO and DGC so that they are more effective at advancing the company’s priorities

Develop major parts of the company’s legal function with a particular focus on
employment law, global workforce matters, employment-related compliance, and litigation

Advise on employment matters across multiple jurisdictions, including the U.S., Australia, Canada, the UK, Europe, Africa, and other regions where the company operates

Draft, review, and negotiate employment agreements, consulting agreements, separation agreements, CIIAAs, offer letters, secondment arrangements, and other workforce-related documents

Develop, maintain, and improve employee handbooks, policies, procedures, trainings, and internal guidance for a rapidly growing global company

Advise on employment laws and practices affecting a mobile, international workforce, including hiring, terminations, discipline, accommodations, leaves of absence, wage and hour, workplace safety, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, retaliation, remote work, and cross-border employment issues

Partner with HR, talent acquisition, finance, tax, equity administration, and immigration counsel or mobility specialists on legal aspects of workforce mobility

Create processes and policies to help build a high-functioning legal department and scalable global employment function

Hire and supervise outside counsel across many subject areas and jurisdictions

Have many opportunities to be involved in other areas as the company and its legal functions grow, including intellectual property, data, AI, privacy, broader compliance, and corporate matters

Work on whatever needs to be done

jobs.description:
About BHP 

At BHP we support our people to grow, learn, develop their skills and reach their potential. With a global portfolio of operations, we offer a diverse and inclusive environment with extraordinary career opportunities. Our strategy is to focus on creating a safe work environment where our employees feel strongly connected to our values and objectives, and where the capability of our people is key to our success.

Come and be a part of this success.

About the Role

The New Markets Delivery Office (NMDO) is responsible for driving step change improvement in BHP’s spend, savings and supplier ecosystem through the development of New Markets suppliers and commercial models.

The Lead, New Markets is a critical leadership role within the China Hub, responsible for driving adoption of New Markets opportunities across BHP's global operations and projects by combining deep technical understanding, commercial acumen and strong stakeholder leadership. The role leads an integrated team of 4-6 commercial and technical professionals and acts as the key interface between the China Hub, onshore Procurement teams, Assets, Projects and suppliers.

The role is accountable for translating China market opportunities into actionable sourcing insights, supplier development initiatives and commercial outcomes that deliver value, resilience and supply chain competitiveness for BHP.

The successful candidate will ideally have an engineering background combined with strong commercial capability and a proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams in complex international environments.

Lead a Strategic Value Stream

Lead, coach and develop a multidisciplinary team of commercial and technical professionals, fostering a high-performance culture focused on collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.

Establish clear priorities, ways of working and performance expectations aligned to NMDO objectives.

Promote a culture of safety, inclusion, customer focus and operational excellence.

Role model BHP values and behaviours while creating an environment where team members are empowered to contribute and grow.

Drive Market Intelligence and New Markets Adoption

Lead development of actionable market intelligence across China to support operational, capital and project procurement strategies.

jobs.title: Specialist New Markets
jobs.description:
About BHP 

At BHP we support our people to grow, learn, develop their skills and reach their potential. With a global portfolio of operations, we offer a diverse and inclusive environment with extraordinary career opportunities. Our strategy is to focus on creating a safe work environment where our employees feel strongly connected to our values and objectives, and where the capability of our people is key to our success.

Come and be a part of this success.

About the Role

The New Markets Technical Specialist is a key member of the China Hub, supporting BHP's New Markets Delivery Office by providing technical expertise to identify, assess and develop suppliers across China.

The role works closely with Procurement, Assets, Projects and suppliers to evaluate technical capability, validate solutions against operational requirements, identify technical and lifecycle risks, and support the adoption of new suppliers and supply chains. The role combines engineering judgement, market knowledge and supplier engagement to ensure commercially attractive opportunities are also technically fit for purpose and aligned with BHP standards.

Key accountabilities:

Assess supplier technical capability against BHP operational, project and engineering requirements.

Evaluate supplier products, equipment, manufacturing processes and quality systems to determine suitability for BHP applications.

Support technical due diligence activities, supplier evaluations and onboarding processes.

Ensure proposed solutions are fit-for-purpose, specification-compliant and capable of meeting operational performance requirements.

Identify technical, quality, reliability and lifecycle risks early and provide recommendations to support sourcing and supplier selection decisions.

Support the development of market intelligence through technical assessments of suppliers, products, technologies and manufacturing capabilities.

Conduct supplier visits, technical reviews and factory assessments to validate capability and identify improvement opportunities.

Support tender evaluations by providing technical analysis and recommendations to Procurement and stakeholder teams.

Apply understanding of mining operations, equipment and maintenance requirements to ensure commercial decisions consider operational impacts and whole-of-life performance.

Support the embedding of BHP standards, technical governance requirements and engineering expectations with suppliers.

Build effective working relationships with Procurement, Operations, Projects and supplier stakeholders to support New Markets initiatives.

Escalate technical, quality and supplier risks in a timely manner and support development of mitigation strategies.

Act as an ambassador for BHP while fostering strong supplier relationships and driving continuous improvement.

Experience in the mining, heavy industry, engineering, manufacturing or related sectors.

Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, preferably Mechanical, Electrical, Structural or related discipline.

Practical understanding of mining equipment, fixed plant, projects, fabrication, manufacturing or maintenance environments.

Demonstrated ability to assess supplier capability, technical solutions and operational risks.

Strong engineering and problem-solving skills with the ability to balance technical requirements and commercial outcomes.

Ability to identify practical risks that may not be evident through specification reviews alone.

Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and focus on high-value activities.

Sound judgement and ability to identify risks, escalate issues and support decision-making.

As part of the recruitment process, there are a number of checks which may be conducted to demonstrate applicants suitability for a role including police / criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks, and/or reference checks. 

If you are already employed directly by BHP, please log in using your BHP email address or apply via our internal jobs portal. 

Supporting a Diverse Workforce 

The size, stability and magnitude of our business not only provides significant opportunity for professional development, but also attractive salary packages with performance-based bonuses and a best-in-class employee share program. We know there are many aspects of our employees' lives that are important, and work is only one of these, so we offer benefits to enable your work to fit with your life. These benefits include flexible working options, a generous paid parental leave policy, other extended leave entitlements and parent rooms.  

At BHP, we know that we are strengthened by diversity. jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work location:
Remote or Perth, Western Australia

Roster:
Monday – Friday

Fortescue is seeking a hands-on Senior AI Engineer – Platform & Inference to provide senior technical leadership across AI platform architecture, inference, deployment and production engineering.

You will set technical direction while staying close to the engineering detail, helping design and build secure, scalable and highly observable AI platforms and services for complex, real-world operations.This is an opportunity to influence how AI is engineered and operationalised at scale, working across distributed systems, cloud-native platforms, model serving and production inference.

Work from where you do your best work

You don't need to be based in Perth to take on this role. We are open to exceptional candidates working remotely. 

If relocating to Perth is something you're interested in, Fortescue can provide relocation support to help make the move possible.

We are also open to international talent and can provide relocation support for the candidate that wants to establish themselves in Perth Western Australia

Why this role

Principal-level influence. Shape AI platform architecture, engineering standards and technology direction while remaining hands-on.

Solve challenging engineering problems. Work across distributed systems, platform engineering, model serving and inference performance.

Build for production and scale. Help establish the engineering foundations required to move sophisticated AI workloads into reliable production environments.

Meaningful real-world impact. Apply advanced AI engineering to high-value operational challenges across a large, technology-led organisation.

Flexibility. Work remotely or from Perth, with relocation and visa support available for candidates interested in making Western Australia home.

Key Responsibilities

Set architecture and engineering standards for AI/ML platforms, model serving and inference systems.

Design scalable, secure and production-grade platform services, APIs and automation.

Lead architecture reviews, complex design decisions and hands-on technical problem solving.

Design approaches for workload orchestration, resource management and distributed AI workloads.

Establish highly observable and reliable production environments, including monitoring, telemetry, security and operational tooling.

Develop production model hosting and inference capabilities, including serving, routing, scaling and performance optimisation.

Drive improvements across performance, reliability and infrastructure efficiency.

Establish strong software engineering, testing, release and operational practices.

Qualifications and Experience

Strong software, cloud platform, distributed systems or ML infrastructure engineering experience, with the technical depth to operate at Principal or Staff level.

Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes, cloud-native infrastructure and containerised distributed workloads.

Experience with workload orchestration, scheduling and resource management in production environments.

Strong software engineering capability in Python, Go, Rust or equivalent languages.

Experience building APIs, automation and production platform services.

Experience with production model serving, inference or ML infrastructure architectures.

Strong understanding of distributed systems, observability, reliability and platform security.

Ability to independently design and build production systems while making pragmatic architectural decisions.

Highly regarded

Experience with distributed compute or scheduling technologies such as Ray, Slurm or Kubernetes-based scheduling frameworks.

Experience with model serving technologies such as vLLM, SGLang, Triton or equivalent.

Understanding of modern LLM inference architectures and performance optimisation.

Experience within  AI platform, cloud infrastructure or ML infrastructure environment.

About Us

Be part of something big. Fortescue is leading the world with our plan to decarbonise our iron ore operations, projects that harness renewable energy and the development of technology that will change our planet forever.

Our Commitment

Fortescue celebrates individual strengths and team members are encouraged to bring their whole selves to work. Our global workforce drives and promotes an inclusive culture, both within our organisation and throughout the communities we interact with. Diverse backgrounds include First Nations Peoples, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+ community, gender, neurodiverse, cultural diversity, all age groups, and those with an intersectional or multiple diverse characteristics. 
We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

https://fortescue.com/careers

Internal Candidates / Current Contractors please apply via Success Factors Careers Portal. For further information on how to apply please visit the Fortescue Hub. 

Fortescue reserves the right to close applications early should a suitable pool of candidates be identified. Fortescue will never contact you to ask for payment of any kind, whether directly or through a third party.

The Jansen project in Saskatchewan, Canada is set to become one of the largest potash mines in the world and is located approximately 140 kilometers east of Saskatoon. As the largest investment in Saskatchewan’s history, Jansen is expected to generate approximately 5,500 workforce opportunities during construction and 900 long-term roles.

Once fully ramped up, Jansen is expected to have an initial production capacity of approximately 8.5 million tonnes per annum (Mtpa), with the potential to produce 16 to 17 Mtpa in future stages. To find out more about Potash and the Jansen project,

click here

.

BHP has recently been named one of Canada's top 100 employers again for 2026.  This formal recognition is a testament to our dedication to fostering a positive, diverse and rewarding work environment.

Work Location

This role will be based at the Jansen Mine Site located in Leroy, SK. The work schedule for this role will be seven days on, seven days off. 

For those not living locally, BHP provides relocation assistance to the local Jansen area. Alternatively, you can enjoy the convenience and comfort of our onsite camp accommodation at Discovery Lodge during your shifts.

BHP offers domestic relocation assistance to support the successful incumbent in transitioning, if required. Benefits offered as part of the relocation program include (but are not limited to) new home purchase assistance, temporary accommodations, home finding trip and a resettlement allowance. 

Purpose

We are excited to share that we are recruiting for permanent Surface and Underground positions for Journeyperson Electricians and Instrumentation for our Jansen Mine.

We are advertising this position in anticipation of future requirements and may not have an immediate opening in this area.  At BHP, things move quickly, and new opportunities are always emerging.  We're building a pool of talented individuals who are interested in being considered when the right role becomes available.  If you're keen to join us, we'd love to hear from you.  We'll match your skills and experience to upcoming opportunities as they arise.

Comply to and consistently follow the standards and procedures designed to enable you to work safely and effectively every day.

Willingly embed yourself into BHP’s Operating System, culture and ways of working. 

Carry out unplanned and planned routine maintenance, inspections, and checks to processing equipment. 

Carry out planned maintenance tasks using standardized work technology to ensure efficiency and quality. 

Assist in resolution of electrical / mechanical issues affecting equipment performance and availability.

Review and update maintenance schedule plans and equipment history.

Transport cable and equipment safely to job locations, and assist in the set up and installation.

Provide trade skills to perform care maintenance tasks within the surface processing areas, to ensure overall reliability and stability.

Develop and revise maintenance procedures to continuously improve and standardize maintenance processes. 

Perform switching and isolation of various types of electrical equipment.

Adaptable and responsive to change, as well as learning new information.

Process Control System Experience.

Ability to work in a variety of different environments and climates.

As part of the recruitment process, there are several checks which may be conducted to demonstrate applicants' suitability for a role including police / criminal background checks, medical, drug and alcohol testing, due diligence checks, right to work checks, and/or reference checks.  The outcome of these checks is not determinative or whether or not BHP decides to make an offer of employment.

If you are already employed directly by BHP, please log in using your BHP email address or apply via our internal jobs' portal.

We are an Equal Opportunity employer that is committed to making BHP a safe and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive and be at their best every day. We are focused on creating a workforce that is more diverse and represents the communities where we work and live. providing a work environment in which everyone is included, treated fairly and with respect. We recognize that true diversity includes gender, age, race, disability status, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, education levels, and many more aspects of your identity. BHP is committed to providing a recruitment process that is fair, equitable and accessible for all. If you have a disability, we know that it may be helpful for us to adjust our process to make it equitable for your individual situation. If you would like to reach out to someone about your situation and our recruitment process, please email us at 
inclusion@bhp.com
.

Based on existing demographics in our Potash project preference in hiring will be given to qualified women and Indigenous peoples who self-identify as such in the application process. At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing an employment package that recognizes excellence, encourages safe production and a culture supported by our core values. Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority, all opinions are valued, and people are empowered to grow in their career. 
Apply Today!     

Where You Will Work

Located approximately 50 miles northeast of Safford, Arizona on U.S. Highway 191, Morenci operations (an open-pit copper mining complex) has been in continuous operation since 1939. The operation consists of two concentrators, crushed-ore leach pad and stacking system, a low-grade run-of-mine (ROM) leaching system; four SX plants; and three EW tank houses that produce copper cathode.  

Morenci is a unique company town where our employees and their families can reconnect with nature through hiking, fishing, camping, hunting and numerous parks. The company offers several amenities, including company housing OR employees who are required to work on-site are eligible for a $750 monthly housing allowance, provided they meet program guidelines, a newly constructed daycare and community center, library, health-care facilities, state-of-the-art fitness centers, a movie theater and a skate park. Our dedicated Parks and Recreation Division plans activities for people of all ages, making sure there’s something for everyone to enjoy. Visit the Morenci town 
website
 to learn more. 

What You Will Do

Set-up, deliver and install personal computers, telephones, networking, and peripheral equipment using established and defined procedures and processes. 

Perform preventative maintenance on voice and data communication systems and associated hardware maintaining accurate documentation. 

Actively participate in Safety and Environmental programs, ensure MIS policy compliance and site operational goals. 

Perform voice, network, and PC and basic wireless troubleshooting to isolate and diagnose infrastructure problems. 

Perform other duties as required. 

What You Bring To Freeport

Two (2) years of experience in computer/electronic systems hardware/software troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair. 

Demonstrated technical expertise in the installation, repair and maintenance of PC hardware, software, printers, fax machines and telephone handsets. 

Ability to effectively analyze, troubleshoot and diagnose issues with computers, peripherals, cellular and voice systems. 

Basic understanding of networking concepts, protocols and technology including wireless networking equipment 

Basic knowledge of voice systems (PBX/VoIP) 

Skill in effective communication, both verbal and written 

Ability to work weekends, holidays, rotating shifts and both scheduled and unscheduled overtime as business dictates. 

Must be customer service-oriented and possess good organizational skills. 

Ability to develop and maintain awareness of occupational hazards and safety precautions. 

Skilled in following safety practices and recognizing hazards. 

Preferred Qualifications

High School diploma or GED 

A+ Certification 

Network+ Certification

jobs.description:

At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing employment that recognizes excellence and encourages safe production, with a culture supported by our core values. Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority.

Apply Today!      

Where You Will Work

Our global headquarters is in Phoenix, Arizona. Several hundred employees support our operations in finance, human resources, health and safety, information technology, planning and more. This position requires work to be performed in-person at our Collaboration Hub in Phoenix. The Hub provides an open, flexible workspace for individuals and teams to come together for various business needs. Amenities at the Hub include a working café, phone booths and meeting rooms with technology tools for virtual and in-person collaboration.  

Phoenix is the capital of the Grand Canyon State and enjoys mostly bright skies throughout the year. It is great place to live and work if you enjoy the outdoors, sports, concerts, the arts and other big city amenities or technology.  

What You Will Do

Under moderate supervision, designs and deploys industrial IoT solutions that connect physical assets to enterprise data platforms across Freeport-McMoRan sites. Serves as the technical lead on advanced field engineering projects, owning solution design within established architectural patterns and directing the execution of work. Designs and implements streaming analytics, video analytics, and real-time dashboards that turn deployed telemetry into operational insight. Contributes architectural roadmap input based on field implementation experience

Lead advanced IoT field engineering projects, owning end-to-end solution design within established architectural patterns, gathering requirements, directing execution, and ensuring successful handoff.

Design and implement streaming analytics and real-time dashboards, building data transformations, configuring analytics rules, and enabling operational decision-making.

Configure and program field devices and ingestion components while building reusable patterns that standardize and scale deployments.

 Provide architecture input, participate in design reviews, propose standards improvements, and mentor junior engineers.

Perform advanced root cause analysis for complex issues while maintaining stakeholder communication and documentation

including
an intermediate understanding of IoT infrastructure, and cloud data concepts and usage.

High School diploma or GED and seven (7) years of experience in IoT technology, software, infrastructure, or computer systems maintenance and application support,
including
demonstrated hands-on experience with low-voltage field devices including cameras, sensors or data loggers, and associated field wiring and communications infrastructure.

jobs.title: Finance Director, Mining/Mineral Processing
jobs.description:
Finance Director, Mining

Location:
Toronto, ON (Hybrid with 2-3 days per week in office)

Blue Moon Metals Inc. is seeking an experienced and strategic Finance Director to join our rapidly growing team. Reporting to the corporate leadership team at our Toronto headquarters, the Finance Director will be responsible for leading the Company's financial management, reporting and treasury across our international operations.

The Finance Director will play a key role in supporting executive decision-making, ensuring financial compliance, strengthening internal controls, and providing financial leadership as Blue Moon Metals advances its mining projects and corporate growth initiatives in Canada, Norway, and the United States.

This position requires a hands-on finance leader who can operate effectively in a dynamic, growth-oriented environment while maintaining strong financial discipline and governance.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy

Lead the Company's financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial modeling processes.

Provide strategic financial analysis and recommendations to support executive and operational decision-making.

Partner with senior leadership to evaluate business performance, capital allocation, and growth opportunities.

Support financing activities, investor relations initiatives, and corporate development projects as required.

Financial Reporting & Compliance

Oversee the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with applicable accounting standards in both Canada and US for a publicly listed company in TSX and Nasdaq. Experience with IFRS is mandatory. Experience with US GAAP is desirable.

Ensure timely and accurate management reporting for executive leadership and the Board of Directors.

Coordinate external audits and serve as the primary liaison with auditors and financial advisors.

Ensure compliance with all regulatory, tax, public company, and financial reporting requirements.

Treasury & Cash Management

Manage cash flow forecasting and treasury activities to support ongoing operations and project development.

Monitor liquidity requirements and optimize working capital management.

Support banking relationships, financing arrangements, and foreign exchange management across multiple jurisdictions.

Internal Controls & Governance

Establish and maintain effective financial controls, policies, and procedures.

Ensure compliance with internal governance standards and corporate policies.

Identify opportunities to improve financial systems, reporting processes, and operational efficiencies.

Team Leadership

Provide leadership, mentorship, and guidance to finance team members.

Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Support the growth and development of finance processes as the organization expands.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Commerce, or a related field.

CPA designation required.

Minimum 10 years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership responsibilities.

Experience within the mining, natural resources, industrial, or project-based sectors is strongly preferred.

Strong knowledge of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury management, and internal controls.

Experience supporting public company reporting requirements is considered a strong asset.

Demonstrated ability to partner with executive leadership and influence strategic decision-making.

Advanced proficiency with financial systems, ERP platforms, and Microsoft Excel.

Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills.

Pay Range and Compensation Package

Compensation and benefits details will be discussed during the interview process.

Equal Opportunity Statement

We are committed to diversity and inclusivity in our hiring practices and encourage applications from all qualified individuals.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Government Relations
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Work Location: 
256 St Georges Terrace, Perth WA 

Roster: 
Monday to Friday with regional travel as required 

Fortescue is building the world’s largest off-grid system dedicated to decarbonising heavy industry, accelerating our Real Zero target.  We are playing an important role in helping shape energy policy now and into the future.
Reporting to the Director of Global Sustainability and External Affairs, and working closely with the CEO and Director Communities, Approvals and Services, this person is responsible for delivering all elements of Government Relations support to Fortescue’s businesses across Australia.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain political awareness and relationships particularly Western Australia and Canberra, and global awareness of regional impacts.

Provide government relations advice for identified projects and the offtake/marketing of electrons, hydrogen and materials.

Act as trusted advisor to senior leaders and an active member of the regional leadership team.

Lead and/or support the engagement of governmental and other political stakeholders to facilitate Fortescue’s projects and operations.

Provide advice to the project and regional teams on identified political risks and the development of associated mitigation plans.

Support teams to develop and take forward advocacy plans to promote Fortescue projects and secure required government support and incentives.

Develop and maintain a detailed understanding of energy, hydrogen, and mining related policies and regulation in Western Australia, Australia and the APAC region.

Work collaboratively with internal stakeholders as they engage with external political stakeholders.

Prepare government relations communications and materials for political stakeholder engagement.

Lead a team government relations professionals fostering a high-performance, collaborative and values-driven culture.

Qualifications and Experience

Tertiary qualification (Law, Economics, Policy or Politics desirable.)

Significant government relations experience within the energy and/or mining sector, and/or a background working in government and policy formulation.

Experience of working with a diverse range of people across all levels including government officials and senior business leaders across Australia.

Proven track record of building strong governmental relationships.

Outstanding interpersonal skills with the ability to interact with a diverse range of people in a professional manner, representing the company. 

Ability to navigate and coordinate across a complex internal environment

Candidates must be able to bring a flexible mindset, challenge traditional thinking and be prepared to work outside of their comfort zone.

Be part of something big. Fortescue is leading the world with our plan to decarbonise our iron ore operations, projects that harness renewable energy and the development of technology that will change our planet forever.

jobs.title: Mine Safety Engineer - Underground Mine Operations, Nussir - Norway
jobs.locationRaw: Nussir,  Hammerfest, Troms og Finnmark, Norway
jobs.description:
Mine Safety Engineer

Location: Hammerfest Municipality (Kvalsund), Finnmark, Norway

Company: Blue Moon Metals Inc. (Nussir ASA)

Mine Type: Underground Copper Mine

Project Status: Early-stage Construction moving to Operations

Position Overview

We are looking for a
Mine Safety Engineer
, for the
Nussir Project
. The project is currently advancing through full-scale underground construction and preparing to move into the operations phase in late 2027.

In this dual-phase role, you will initially oversee safety during underground construction
, including

horizontal and vertical development
. As the project transitions, you will establish, scale, and manage the day-to-day operational safety systems for a long-life, underground asset.

Key Responsibilities

Construction Phase Execution (Immediate focus)

Contractor Safety Management:
Partner with and audit major engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contractors having deliveries underground to ensure alignment with corporate and local safety cultures.

Excavation & Structural Oversight:
Support mining team, including contractors, in performing structural and ground control safety assessments along the growing decline, conveyor tunnels, and silo tunnel networks.

Commissioning Risk Analysis:
Lead Pre-Start Health and Safety Reviews (PHSR) and risk assessments for the installation and no-load commissioning of fixed and semi fixed machinery (mobile/semimobile crushers, conveyor belts, main pumping station installation and other).

Operational Phase Strategy (Long-term focus)

Underground Systems Management:
Design, calibrate, and monitor critical safety systems including mine ventilation shafts, toxic gas detection arrays, blast clearances, and autonomous/collision warning equipment.

Regulatory Compliance:
Interpret and ensure strict adherence to Norwegian mineral and labor laws under the
Norwegian Directorate of Mines (Direktoratet for mineralforvaltning)
and
Arbeidstilsynet
(Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority).

Culture & Training:
Ensure, and support development and delivery of customized safety training programs for both underground production crews and surface maintenance teams to foster an incident-free mindset.

Emergency Preparedness:
Author, test, and adapt the underground emergency response plan, mine rescue protocols, and evacuation drill strategies.

Incident Management:
Lead all incident and near-miss root cause investigations, mapping corrective action pathways to ensure zero repetition.

Qualifications & Requirements

Education & Experience

Education:
Bachelor's degree in Mining Engineering, Geological Engineering, or Occupational Health & Safety.

Experience:
Minimum of 5–8 years of experience in heavy industrial environments, with at least 3 years directly focused on
underground mine operations or underground civil tunneling
.

Phase Exposure:
Proven experience navigating the transition of an industrial asset from heavy construction/handover through to steady-state operations is highly valued.

Technical & Regulatory Competencies

Local Legislation:
Solid familiarity with Norwegian health and safety regulations (
Arbeidsmiljøloven
) and Nordic mining practices is highly advantageous.

Industry Standards:
Deep understanding of international machinery safety standards and risk management methodologies (e.g., ISO 45001, IEC 61508).

Languages:
Business-level fluency in English is mandatory; professional competency in Norwegian or in Swedish is a distinct advantage for local contractor coordination.

Personal Attributes

Strong leadership capability with the emotional intelligence to manage safety cultures across diverse multicultural contractor teams.

Exceptional communication skills, capable of transparently conveying safety data to both executive management and on-site laborers.

Pay range and compensation package

Compensation details will be discussed during the interview process.

Equal Opportunity Statement

We are committed to diversity and inclusivity in our hiring practices and encourage applications from all qualified individuals.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Experience in identifying and tracking key performance indicators (KPI)
